title: A covariant self-contact mass operator
summary: 1. Result Let Q_d be the real d-dimensional manifold on which a particle sector lives. For every positive particle mode n, set N=n-1. There is a canonical rank-S(n,d) mode bundle over Q_d: \mathcal E_{N,d} = \operatornam
text:
Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. 1. Result Let Q_d be the real d-dimensional manifold on which a particle sector lives. For every positive particle mode n, set N=n-1. There is a canonical rank-S(n,d) mode bundle over Q_d: \mathcal E_{N,d} = \operatorname{Sym}^{N} \left( \mathbf 1_{\mathbb C}\oplus T^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C ight). Its rank is \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}\mathcal E_{N,d} =  inom{N+d}{d} =  inom{n+d-1}{d} =S(n,d). The additional trivial line \mathbf1_{\mathbb C} homogenizes the cumulative occupation condition: \operatorname{Sym}^{N}(\mathbb C\oplus V) \cong  igoplus_{k=0}^{N}\operatorname{Sym}^{k}(V). For V=T_q^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C, the right-hand side contains every d-direction oscillator shell from 0 through N. The extra occupation number records the unused portion of the total excitation. The Hermitian fibre W_{d,q}=\mathbb C\oplus T_q^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C has ray space \mathbb P(W_{d,q})\cong\mathbb{CP}^{d}. On \mathcal E_{N,d,q}=\operatorname{Sym}^{N}(W_{d,q}), rank-one support on the occupied coherent ray, covariance, and unit normalization uniquely determine a positive localization density \Lambda_{N,d}([z]) =D_{N,d}\, |z;Nangle\langle z;N|, \qquad D_{N,d}=S(N+1,d), where |z;Nangle=z^{\odot N} is the normalized symmetric coherent state. This operator obeys \int_{\mathbb{CP}^{d}} \Lambda_{N,d}([z])\,d
u_{m FS}([z]) =I_{\mathcal E_{N,d}}, and \Lambda_{N,d}([z])^2 =D_{N,d}\Lambda_{N,d}([z]). It therefore has one nonzero eigenvalue, exactly D_{N,d}. A scalar self-contact contribution \mathcal M_{N,d}([z]) =\mu_d\Lambda_{N,d}([z]) has the coherent localized mode as an eigenvector with rest mass  oxed{ m(n,d)=\mu_dD_{N,d} =\mu_d inom{n+d-1}{d}. } This derives the combinatorial multiplier as the eigenvalue of the localized contact density on the cumulative tangent-mode bundle. The proposed physical identification assumes the following additional occupied-ray prescription for the scalar self-interaction: The master Dirac interaction is algebraic in the local scalar current and its sector coordinates, with no derivatives of that current. The current is evaluated at the occupied projective mode ray determined by the field's local amplitude and covariant derivatives. The rank-one formula requires contact at a specified occupied coherent ray in the auxiliary projective fibre, with the stated measure and evaluation map. Locality in the physical base coordinate alone does not imply this. A local identity operator has a delta kernel too, yet band compression gives the identity on the band, not the rank-one operator \Lambda_{N,d}([z]). The combinatorial multiplier is therefore derived for the explicitly assumed coherent-ray contact operator. Deriving that operator, its band-independent coefficient \mu_d, and the occupied modes from the master action remains open; normalization is not the only remaining problem. 2. The cumulative oscillator bundle At a point q\in Q_d, the complexified cotangent space V_{d,q}=T_q^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C has complex rank d. Its degree-k symmetric power has rank \operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Sym}^{k}(V_{d,q}) = inom{k+d-1}{d-1}. This is the shell multiplicity of d commuting creation directions. The cumulative band through degree N is \mathcal B_{N,d} = igoplus_{k=0}^{N}\operatorname{Sym}^{k}(V_{d,q}). Consequently, \operatorname{rank}\mathcal B_{N,d} =\sum_{k=0}^{N} inom{k+d-1}{d-1} = inom{N+d}{d}. The count is independent of coordinates. Changes of orthonormal cotangent frame act through U(d) on V_{d,q} and through its symmetric powers on the band. The band can be written as one homogeneous representation. For arbitrary vector spaces A and B, \operatorname{Sym}^{N}(A\oplus B) \cong  igoplus_{k=0}^{N} \operatorname{Sym}^{N-k}(A)\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{k}(B). Taking A=\mathbb C gives \operatorname{Sym}^{N}(\mathbb C\oplus V_{d,q}) \cong  igoplus_{k=0}^{N}\operatorname{Sym}^{k}(V_{d,q}), because every symmetric power of a one-dimensional vector space is one-dimensional. In occupation numbers, a monomial in the cumulative band is labelled by (a_1,\ldots,a_d), \qquad \sum_{j=1}^{d}a_j\leq N. Introduce a_0=N-\sum_{j=1}^{d}a_j. Then a_0+\cdots+a_d=N, \qquad a_j\geq0, and stars-and-bars gives \#\{(a_0,\ldots,a_d):a_0+\cdots+a_d=N\} = inom{N+d}{d}. Thus a d-direction cumulative spectrum has d+1 homogeneous slots while its base remains d-dimensional. 3. Particle manifold and mode-ray fibre Two projective spaces can occur in the electron construction and must be kept distinct. The electron lives on Q_6=\mathbb{CP}^{3}, \qquad \dim_{\mathbb R}Q_6=6. Its cumulative six-direction mode fibre has rays \mathbb P \left( \mathbb C\oplus T_q^*Q_6\otimes\mathbb C ight) \cong\mathbb{CP}^{6}. Thus \dim H^0(\mathbb{CP}^{3},\mathcal O(L)) = inom{L+3}{3} and \operatorname{rank}\mathcal E_{n-1,6} = inom{n+5}{6} are both correct. They count different structures:  inom{L+3}{3} counts degree-L holomorphic flux states on the electron's configuration manifold;  inom{n+5}{6} counts the cumulative symmetric tangent-mode band through degree n-1. The first governs the projective orbital representation. The second supplies the mass multiplier. The labels L and n belong to these two distinct counts. For a general sector, \mathbb{CP}^{d} is the ray space of the rank-(d+1) homogenized mode fibre over the particle manifold Q_d. 4. Covariant localization forces the dimension factor Fix q\in Q_d and write W=W_{d,q}, \qquad \mathcal H_N=\operatorname{Sym}^{N}(W), \qquad D=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H_N. Give W its metric-induced Hermitian structure. For a unit vector z\in W, define |z;Nangle=z^{\odot N}, \qquad \langle z;N|z;Nangle=1. Its projector depends only on the ray [z]: P_N([z])=|z;Nangle\langle z;N|. Let d
u_{m FS} be the U(d+1)-invariant probability measure on \mathbb P(W). Consider A_N=\int_{\mathbb P(W)}P_N([z])\,d
u_{m FS}([z]). The representation \operatorname{Sym}^{N}(W) of U(d+1) is irreducible. Invariance of the measure gives U A_N U^\dagger=A_N for every U\in U(d+1). Schur's lemma therefore gives A_N=c_NI. Taking the trace fixes the coefficient: 1 =\int\operatorname{tr}P_N([z])\,d
u_{m FS} =\operatorname{tr}A_N =c_ND. Hence A_N= rac{I}{D}. The covariant localization density resolving the identity is consequently \Lambda_N([z])=DP_N([z]). Once the localization operator has rank-one support on the coherent line, covariance, positivity, and resolution of the identity force the factor D. This is the finite-dimensional coherent-state resolution of the identity used in geometric quantization. General coherent-state and reproducing-kernel constructions on compact integral symplectic manifolds are reviewed by Kirwin; explicit SU(N) coherent-state resolutions are constructed by Mathur and Mani. 5. From localization density to rest mass Let the sector spinor bundle be \Sigma_d. For a spin sector this is the ordinary spin bundle. For a \mathrm{Spin}^c sector it includes the required line connection. The mode-N field is a section of \Sigma_d\otimes\mathcal E_{N,d}. The localization density acts only on the mode factor: \widehat\Lambda_{N,d} =I_{\Sigma_d}\otimes\Lambda_{N,d}. It therefore commutes with Clifford multiplication: [\widehat\Lambda_{N,d},\gamma(v)]=0, \qquad v\in TQ_d. It is a Lorentz-scalar mass endomorphism. The effective projected Dirac equation can consequently take the form \left( i\gamma^a
abla_a -\mu_d\widehat\Lambda_{N,d}([z]) ight)\psi_{N,d}=0. For a localized coherent mode \psi_{N,d}=\chi\otimes|z;Nangle, the contact operator gives \widehat\Lambda_{N,d}([z])\psi_{N,d} =D_{N,d}\psi_{N,d}. The rest equation is therefore \left(i\gamma^a
abla_a-m(n,d)ight)\psi_{N,d}=0, with m(n,d)=\mu_dD_{N,d} =\mu_dS(n,d). The symmetric power acts on the bosonic orbital or derivative directions of one spinor field. 6. Projection from the master field Let P_{d,N} project the master spinor onto the particle manifold Q_d and the cumulative mode bundle \mathcal E_{N,d}. Separate the master Dirac operator into its kinetic and self-interaction parts: \mathcal D_\infty =i\Gamma^A
abla_A-\mathcal K_\infty[\Psi_\infty]. The projected operator is \mathcal D_{d,N} =P_{d,N}\mathcal D_\infty P_{d,N}. The mass theorem applies if the scalar contact component satisfies P_{d,N}\mathcal K_\infty P_{d,N}  ig|_{m scalar,contact} =\mu_d\widehat\Lambda_{N,d}([z]). The following subsections derive this identity from the minimal local self-interaction. 6.1 The projective ray is local mode-phase data The fibre W_{d,q} =\mathbb C\oplus T_q^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C is the homogenized oscillator-symbol fibre. The cotangent factor contains the d complex oscillator amplitudes. In an orthonormal frame centred on the mode, they combine displacement x_a and conjugate momentum p_a as a_a = rac{1}{\sqrt2} \left(  rac{x_a}{\ell_d} +i rac{\ell_dp_a}{\hbar} ight), \qquad a=1,\ldots,d. Here \ell_d is the spatial sector length. The connection identifies p_a with the covariant derivative symbol of the field. Both quadratures are dimensionless. Real orthonormal sector-frame changes act through O(d), a subgroup of U(d). The larger unitary oscillator symmetry also mixes canonical quadratures; it is not supplied by spatial frame changes alone. The additional component a_0 records the unused part of the cumulative excitation bound. The completed vector z=(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_d)\in W_{d,q} defines the projective mode-phase ray [z]\in\mathbb P(W_{d,q}). Common complex rescaling leaves the ray invariant. The value of \ell_d changes the physical phase-space embedding while preserving the rank of \mathcal E_{N,d} and the diagonal trace identity. At fixed homogeneous oscillator action, |a_0|^2+\sum_{a=1}^{d}|a_a|^2=R_N^2, the completed amplitudes lie on S^{2d+1}. Quotienting their common phase gives S^{2d+1}/U(1)=\mathbb{CP}^{d}. This is the classical projective completion of the cumulative oscillator band. Quantization at homogeneous degree N gives \operatorname{Sym}^N(\mathbb C^{d+1}). The same construction therefore produces both the ray space and its simplex dimension. Higher oscillator degree fills the degree-N representation of the same spatial coordinates: \operatorname{Sym}^N(W_{d,q}), and the definite ray becomes the coherent line |z;Nangle=z^{\odot N}. Equivalently, the filtered symbols through derivative order N have associated graded bundle  igoplus_{k=0}^{N} \operatorname{Sym}^k(T^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C). The sector connection splits this filtration into the homogenized bundle \mathcal E_{N,d}. The ray is the local oscillator phase of the field on Q_d. A definite orbit supplies a definite [z] at each instant. 6.2 Conditional occupied-ray insertion Lift the scalar current to the graph of its occupied projective symbol: \mathcal J_d(q,[u]) =J_d(q)\, \delta_{m FS} \left([u],[z_{\Psi_d}(q)]ight), \qquad J_d= ar\Psi_d\Psi_d. The invariant delta is normalized by \int_{\mathbb P(W_{d,q})} f([u])\delta_{m FS}([u],[z])\,d
u_{m FS}([u]) =f([z]). This graph lift assigns a specified ray to the source. Its identification with the field's physical amplitude-gradient data is an additional premise, not a consequence of scalar locality on Q_d. Consider the leading scalar self-interaction of a nonlinear Dirac field: \mathcal L_{m sc} =- rac{\kappa_d}{2}J_d^2. Its Euler--Lagrange contribution is  rac{\partial\mathcal L_{m sc}}{\partial ar\Psi_d} =-\kappa_dJ_d\Psi_d. In integral-kernel language, multiplication by the current has distribution kernel \kappa_dJ_d(q)\, \delta_{Q_d}(q,q')\, \delta_{m FS}([u],[u']). The diagonal delta is the kernel representation of multiplication. In the ray variable it represents the identity, not a point insertion at a selected ray. Its band compression is P_N I P_N=I_{\mathcal H_N}, which has full rank. General order-zero multiplication can also have a nonconstant coefficient in [u]; locality does not determine that coefficient. To obtain the point insertion \kappa_d\delta_{[z]}, separately assume that the interaction evaluates against the graph-supported source at the occupied ray. Its finite-band projection is computed in the next section. A physical derivation must specify the lifted action, its measure, and its pairing; formally squaring the distributional graph current in a quartic action is not a defined replacement for those data. 6.3 Exact projection of a point contact Let \mathcal H_N =\operatorname{Sym}^{N}(W_{d,q}) and let P_N be the orthogonal projector onto its holomorphic realization over \mathbb P(W_{d,q}). Denote its reproducing kernel by K_N. For every s\in\mathcal H_N, s([z])=\langle K_{N,z},sangle, \qquad K_{N,z}(\,\cdot\,)=K_N(\,\cdot\,,[z]). Define the Toeplitz projection of the point contact by its quadratic form: \langle s,T_{N,[z]}tangle = \int \overline{s([u])}\, \delta_{m FS}([u],[z])\, t([u])\,d
u_{m FS}([u]). Evaluation gives \langle s,T_{N,[z]}tangle =\overline{s([z])}t([z]) =\langle s,K_{N,z}angle \langle K_{N,z},tangle. Therefore T_{N,[z]} =P_N\delta_{[z]}P_N =|K_{N,z}angle\langle K_{N,z}|. Its nonzero eigenvalue is \|K_{N,z}\|^2=K_N([z],[z]). The diagonal is constant because U(d+1) acts transitively on \mathbb{CP}^{d} and preserves both P_N and d
u_{m FS}. Its value is fixed by the trace: \int_{\mathbb{CP}^{d}} K_N([u],[u])\,d
u_{m FS}([u]) =\operatorname{tr}P_N =\dim\mathcal H_N. The measure has total volume one, hence K_N([z],[z]) =\dim\mathcal H_N = inom{N+d}{d} =S(N+1,d). Writing |z;Nangle = rac{K_{N,z}}{\sqrt{K_N([z],[z])}} gives the exact identity  oxed{ P_N\delta_{[z]}P_N =S(N+1,d)|z;Nangle\langle z;N| =\Lambda_{N,d}([z]). } Here U(d+1) is the covariance of the homogenized cumulative mode fibre. The original U(d) rotates the d derivative directions. Projective completion adds the homogeneous slack component and extends the finite band to the irreducible U(d+1) representation \operatorname{Sym}^N(\mathbb C^{d+1}). Treating that completion isotropically is a necessary mode-space premise of the exact simplex law. This is the required projection theorem. Toeplitz operators with singular measure and distribution symbols are part of the general reproducing-kernel framework described by Rozenblum and Vasilevski. Here the finite-dimensional projective case is an exact consequence of the reproducing property. 6.4 Conditional projected nonlinear Dirac equation Assume the occupied-ray interaction of Section 6.2 supplies the following term, with the ray held fixed during this operator evaluation, and project it onto the mode band: P_{d,N} \left(\kappa_dJ_d\delta_{[z]}ight) P_{d,N} = \mu_dP_N\delta_{[z]}P_N, where \mu_d is the sector-normalized scalar contact strength after the Q_d profile and spinor normalization have been taken. The projection theorem gives P_{d,N}\mathcal K_\infty P_{d,N}  ig|_{m scalar,contact} = \mu_dS(N+1,d) |z;Nangle\langle z;N|. Acting on the occupied coherent line, P_{d,N}\mathcal K_\infty P_{d,N}|z;Nangle =\mu_dS(N+1,d)|z;Nangle. With n=N+1, the projected Dirac equation therefore contains the rest mass  oxed{ m(n,d)=\mu_dS(n,d). } All explicit N-dependence comes from the diagonal of the finite-band reproducing kernel. The resulting \mu_d is shared by all ordinary particle modes in sector d provided the normalized one-particle scalar-current contraction is the same in every band. This is automatic for a universal unit-normalized point current, but must be checked for the normalized spinor convention used by the projected master action. The action-level derivation has four necessary ingredients: Locality in the mode ray. The self-interaction evaluates the wave against its own phase-space ray [z]. Covariance. Rotating the mode frame sends \Lambda([z]) to \Lambda([Uz]) by conjugation. Resolution normalization. Integrating the mutually overlapping localized rays over invariant measure gives the identity. Band-blind contact strength. The coefficient \mu_d depends on the sector and is independent of N. The graph-supported contact is the first premise; it is not forced by the local scalar current. The Bergman projection proves the second and third within the chosen isotropic mode space and produces the factor S(n,d). Absence of a band label in a bare coupling does not by itself establish the fourth: normalized projected profiles and scalar-current matrix elements can depend on the band. Their independence must also be demonstrated. If the occupied ray is itself a function of the varied field or its derivatives, variation of the lifted action must include that dependence. The fixed-ray operator calculation does not already derive those additional Euler--Lagrange terms or prove a self-consistent occupied-ray solution. The family-ratio theorem is conditional on this interaction and normalization. This makes the shared scale experimentally meaningful: the successful family-ratio tests are evidence that the projected contact strength is band-blind. At one fixed ray, \Lambda_{N,d}([z]) has a (D_{N,d}-1)-dimensional nullspace. The coherent rays form an overcomplete family and \int\Lambda_{N,d}([z])\,d
u_{m FS}=I, so every nonzero state is detected by some contact density. At a given [z], the occupied localized particle is the one nonzero eigenline. 7. Kinetic and contact operators A spatial Dirac or Laplace operator on Q_d supplies kinetic eigenvalues and their multiplicities through \slashed D_{Q_d} and \Delta_{Q_d} respectively. The localized contact operator supplies the rest-energy endomorphism whose eigenvalue grows as S(n,d)\sim n^d. The kinetic operator constructs the mode eigenspace. The contact density then maps its rank D to the eigenvalue of a normalized localized operator. This is the two-stage origin of the mass multiplier. 8. Boundaries of the theorem 8.1 The photon The construction begins at n=1, where N=0 and S(1,d)=1. The photon has n=0 and belongs to the zero-band boundary \mathcal E_{-1,d}=0 whose self-contact mass eigenvalue is zero: m(0,2)=0. Its propagating energy and momentum are distinct from this self-contact mass operator. Both describe the same field on the same physical manifold. 8.2 The bottom beat The ordinary theorem gives the single-band masses m(n,3)=\mu_3S(n,3). The bottom formula m_b=\mu_3\sqrt{S(16,3)S(17,3)} requires a two-band coupling. Its closure condition is that the off-diagonal contact operator between \mathcal E_{15,3} and \mathcal E_{16,3} have a singular value equal to the geometric mean of their diagonal contact eigenvalues. 8.3 Sector scales For a band-blind master contact coefficient, one \mu_d multiplies every ordinary occupied band in a sector. Numerical projection must determine \mu_2,\mu_3,\mu_4,\mu_5,\mu_6,\mu_{10} and their cross-sector relations from the normalized master kernel and its overlap between the corresponding Q_d sectors. Observed masses provide the empirical test of those projected values. 8.4 Mode selection The operator supplies a collective mass eigenbranch for every positive integer n. A separate stability or resonance condition must select which branches occur as particles. The accuracy of the mass-depth scan is conditional on those occupied indices. 8.5 Occupied-ray and ray-averaged quartic densities The distinction between contact at the occupied ray and averaging over all rays is mathematically observable. For a normalized coherent state |w;Nangle, define its normalized phase-ray density ho_w([z]) =D_N|\langle z;N|w;Nangle|^2. It obeys \intho_w\,d
u_{m FS}=1. Because |\langle z;N|w;Nangle|^2 =|\langle z|wangle|^{2N}, the invariant moment formula gives \int_{\mathbb{CP}^{d}} |\langle z|wangle|^{4N}\,d
u_{m FS} = rac{1}{D_{2N}}, \qquad D_{2N}= inom{2N+d}{d}. A quartic energy averaged over the whole ray space is \intho_w([z])^2\,d
u_{m FS} = rac{D_N^2}{D_{2N}}, while occupied-ray self-contact has eigenvalue D_N. The two interactions are 	ext{occupied-ray self-contact} \quad\longrightarrow\quad D_N, 	ext{ray-averaged quartic density} \quad\longrightarrow\quad rac{D_N^2}{D_{2N}}. The observed simplex multiplier selects the first interaction with a band-independent sector scale. 8.6 Coordinate harmonic kernel and phase-ray contact A scalar coordinate kernel whose isotropic mean field is V_d(q)=\lambda_d|q|^2 derives a harmonic well and hence the shell spaces \operatorname{Sym}^k(T_q^*Q_d\otimes\mathbb C). That is enough to derive the rank D_N of the cumulative band. The corresponding band projection is P_{N,d}|q|^2P_{N,d} and the phase-ray contact density is D_N|z;Nangle\langle z;N|. Their relation requires either a master interaction written locally on the homogenized phase-ray bundle; or a derivation showing that the coordinate-space nonlinear kernel transforms into the occupied-ray contact density after the oscillator and sector projections. This step completes the map from coordinate confinement to phase-ray self-contact. 9. Sector normalization The universal combinatorial part of the scalar contact projection is now fixed: P_N\delta_{[z]}P_N =S(N+1,d)|z;Nangle\langle z;N|. Write the scalar coefficient left after sector projection as \mu_d=\kappa_dR_dB_d. Here \kappa_d is the projected master-contact coefficient, R_d is the normalized spatial-profile overlap on Q_d, and B_d is the scalar spinor contraction. Suppose the order-zero vertex is a scalar identity on the normalized non-mode factors, its coefficient is constant on the occupied contact graph, and its coefficient is independent of the band projector. Under these band-blind hypotheses, all three factors are independent of N. The contact theorem then gives m(n,d)=\kappa_dR_dB_d\,S(n,d). For the stated band-blind scalar vertex, \mu_d=\kappa_dR_dB_d is independent of N. Derivative vertices, nonconstant order-zero coefficients, finite contact width, spectral functions, mode-dependent spinor polarization, and band-dependent state normalization generate testable modifications of the mass sequence. For two sectors with equal self-couplings, the ratio of mass units is  rac{\mu_a}{\mu_b}= rac{R_aB_a}{R_bB_b}. Thus the proposed \mu_6=\mu_{10} symmetry requires both g_{66}=g_{10,10} and equality of the normalized projected overlaps. 9.1 The conditional common-anchor relation There is a compact way to state the scale relations that have direct mass tests. Let n_d^\star be a specified reference band in sector d and define its contact mass M_d^\star=\mu_dS(n_d^\star,d). Under the projected fixed-point condition  rac{(M_d^\star)^2}{g_{dd}} =  rac{m_e^2}{g_{66}}. the sector scale is  oxed{ \mu_d =  rac{m_e}{S(n_d^\star,d)} \sqrt{ rac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}} }. The square root is the direct algebraic consequence of this quadratic fixed-point equation. The master equation of motion must supply that equation. For the proposed reference choices, the formula reads  egin{aligned} \mu_6&= rac{m_e}{S(13,6)},\ \mu_3&=m_e\sqrt{ rac{g_{33}}{g_{66}}},\ \mu_4&= rac{m_e}{S(3,4)} \sqrt{ rac{g_{44}}{g_{66}}}. \end{aligned} The electron fixes the unit. The d=3 and d=4 expressions then make absolute predictions for directly measured quark masses and can be tested empirically. The proposed d=2 formula \mu_2=m_e\sqrt{ rac{g_{22}}{g_{66}}} uses a unit-count back-reaction reference. It is testable because it predicts the absolute W, Z, and Higgs masses after their mode indices are specified. Likewise, \mu_{10}=\mu_6 is testable against the tau mass, but still requires the normalized 6\leftrightarrow10 overlap equality just identified. These are the direct empirical checks of the conditional fixed-point equation and coupling counts. 9.2 The neutrino scale is unresolved The proposed relation \mu_5 =  rac34 rac{\mu_6^3}{\mu_4^2} is a phenomenological normalization calibrated to the observed neutrino order of magnitude. V2 treats \mu_5 as an undetermined projected normalization. An operator equation must select the factor 3/4 and powers (3,-2) before this expression becomes a derived scale law. Neutrino oscillations measure mass-squared differences. Given the proposed mode indices, they constrain a common \mu_5. An absolute neutrino-mass measurement will provide the direct scale test. The current status is  oxed{\mu_5	ext{ remains an undetermined projected normalization.}} A derivation requires evaluating \kappa_5R_5B_5 from the master action. 9.3 Remaining numerical calculation The outstanding work is to evaluate (\kappa_d,R_d,B_d), \qquad d\in\{2,3,4,5,6,10\}, from one normalized projected action and recover the cross-sector relations. The simplex multiplier is derived, the non-neutrino scale relations are conditional and empirically testable, and the neutrino expression is a phenomenological ansatz. The construction also makes sharp deformation predictions: a finite ray-contact width replaces the constant diagonal evaluation with a convolution of the Bergman kernel and changes the mass sequence; derivatives of the contact delta insert powers of the representation generators and generate additional N-dependence; a band-dependent scalar coefficient spoils the scale-free family ratios; a mixed state on several projective rays splits or averages the rank-one mass eigenvalue. The successful bare spectrum selects order-zero local self-contact at a definite projective mode ray, projected onto a finite cumulative band.

title: Dimensional constriction and hadronic mass
summary: Current scope: This is an exploratory calculation ledger, not a derived hadron-mass formula. Numerical residuals and trial normalizations below are conditional comparisons. Neither 154.808228 MeV nor twice that value is
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Current scope: This is an exploratory calculation ledger, not a derived hadron-mass formula. Numerical residuals and trial normalizations below are conditional comparisons. Neither 154.808228 MeV nor twice that value is an established constriction eigenfrequency. Section 2 distinguishes action from frequency; Sections 64--76 give the normalization and spectral limitations. 1. Question The quark sectors in V2 are assigned different spatial depths: Q_4 \quad \text{for up-type quarks}, and Q_3 \quad \text{for down-type quarks}. The cross-depth geometry is asymmetric. A four-dimensional mode projected into a three-dimensional hadronic sector loses one independent spatial oscillator direction. The three-dimensional state does not gain one. This raises a specific dynamical question: Can the large difference between light current-quark masses and observed hadron masses be interpreted as the energy cost of constraining a four-dimensional oscillator into three dimensions? The calculation below separates what follows mathematically from dimensional constriction from what remains an empirical or dynamical input. 2. Oscillator action and the separate frequency-rescaling hypothesis For an isotropic oscillator with d directions, E_d=\omega_d I_{\rm total}^{(d)} =d\,\omega_d I_{\rm per}^{(d)}. Conservation of total action under a hypothetical 4\to3 transfer gives 4I_{\rm per}^{(4)}=3I_{\rm per}^{(3)}. This fixes the action per surviving direction, not the frequency. If both total action and total oscillator energy are conserved, the displayed Hamiltonian instead gives \omega_3=\omega_4. The equation 4\omega_4 I_1=3\omega_3 I_1 assumes equal energy and the same per-direction action on both sides. It yields \omega_3=4\omega_4/3, but changes total action from 4I_1 to 3I_1. It is not a consequence of total-action conservation. The numerical explorations below use \boxed{\omega_3=\frac43\omega_4} as a separate frequency-rescaling hypothesis. No current V2 dynamics derives it. Transferring eliminated action into surviving directions, by itself, does not establish this hypothesis. 3. Mass-like energy from the constriction For a relativistic bound mode, oscillator or confinement energy contributes to the rest energy observed in the lower-dimensional sector. Define the effective confinement contribution per valence quark by \epsilon_h = \frac{M_h-\sum_i m_{q_i}}{N_q}, where M_h is the observed hadron mass; m_{q_i} are the current-quark masses used by V2; N_q is the number of valence quarks in the minimal quark assignment. If the observed three-dimensional confinement quantum is the constricted oscillator quantum, \epsilon_h=\hbar\omega_3, then the corresponding pre-constriction four-dimensional quantum is \boxed{ E_{4,h} =\hbar\omega_4 =\frac34\epsilon_h. } If the four-dimensional oscillator has characteristic spatial scale R_h, dimensional analysis gives E_{4,h}\sim\frac{\hbar c}{R_h}, so the effective constriction radius inferred from a hadron mass is \boxed{ R_h =\frac{4\hbar c}{3\epsilon_h}. } Equivalently, \boxed{ M_h =\sum_i m_{q_i} +N_q\frac43\frac{\hbar c}{R_h}. } This is the simplest quantitative hadronic-mass law produced by the 4\to3 constricted-oscillator hypothesis. 4. Nucleon test Using the V2 light-quark masses m_u=2.16\ {\rm MeV}, \qquad m_d=4.70\ {\rm MeV}, the proton current-quark sum is 2m_u+m_d=9.02\ {\rm MeV}. With m_p=938.272088\ {\rm MeV}, the excess mass is \Delta M_p =929.252088\ {\rm MeV}. Per valence quark, \boxed{ \epsilon_p =309.750696\ {\rm MeV}. } The inferred pre-constriction oscillator quantum is E_{4,p} =\frac34\epsilon_p =232.313022\ {\rm MeV}, and therefore \boxed{ R_p^{\rm constr} =\frac{\hbar c}{E_{4,p}} =0.8494\ {\rm fm}. } The neutron gives almost the same result. With m_n=939.565421\ {\rm MeV}, and m_u+2m_d=11.56\ {\rm MeV}, one finds \boxed{ \epsilon_n =309.335140\ {\rm MeV}, } E_{4,n}=232.001355\ {\rm MeV}, and \boxed{ R_n^{\rm constr} =0.8505\ {\rm fm}. } Thus proton and neutron independently select essentially the same constriction scale: \boxed{ R_N^{\rm constr}\simeq0.850\ {\rm fm}, } with a three-dimensional confinement quantum \boxed{ \hbar\omega_3\simeq309.5\ {\rm MeV}. } The near equality of the proton and neutron values is nontrivial because their current-quark sums differ. 5. Relation to the measured nucleon size The proton charge radius is approximately r_p\simeq0.84\ {\rm fm}. The mass-derived constriction radius R_p^{\rm constr}\simeq0.849\ {\rm fm} is therefore within roughly one percent of the observed proton charge-radius scale. Conversely, inserting a radius near 0.84 fm into \epsilon=\frac43\frac{\hbar c}{R} gives a confinement quantum near 313\ {\rm MeV}, close to the 309--310 MeV required by the proton and neutron masses. This is the strongest numerical result of the dimensional-constriction test. It does not by itself prove the mechanism because the relation E_4=\hbar c/R is a characteristic confinement estimate rather than a derived eigenvalue of the present V2 master operator. What is striking is that the independent mass excess and the physical nucleon size select nearly the same scale once the exact 4/3 constriction factor is imposed. 6. Broader hadron test A genuine hadronic mechanism must not be judged from the nucleon alone. The same inversion can be applied to other ground-state hadrons. For each hadron define \epsilon_h =\frac{M_h-\sum m_q}{N_q}, E_{4,h}=\frac34\epsilon_h, and R_h^{\rm constr}=\frac{\hbar c}{E_{4,h}}. Using representative central hadron masses gives: hadron valence assignment \epsilon_h (MeV) E_{4,h} (MeV) R_h^{\rm constr} (fm) p uud 309.751 232.313 0.849 n udd 309.335 232.001 0.851 \Lambda uds 338.441 253.831 0.777 \Sigma^+ uus 363.850 272.887 0.723 \Sigma^0 uds 364.094 273.071 0.723 \Sigma^- dds 364.850 273.637 0.721 \Xi^0 uss 375.233 281.425 0.701 \Xi^- dss 376.670 282.502 0.698 \Delta light qqq 408.5 306.4 0.644 \Omega^- sss 463.983 347.988 0.567 \rho light q\bar q 384.1 288.1 0.685 \omega light q\bar q 387.9 290.9 0.678 K^* q\bar s 398.0 298.5 0.661 \phi s\bar s 416.2 312.2 0.632 \pi light q\bar q 66.4 49.8 3.97 K q\bar s 199.0 149.3 1.32 The table reveals two important facts. First, a single universal additive confinement quantum of about 310 MeV per valence quark is not sufficient for all hadrons. If one calibrates that number on the nucleon, it underpredicts strange baryons, spin-3/2 baryons, and vector mesons. Second, the failures are not random in sign. The inferred confinement quantum increases systematically for more compact or more strongly excited spin/flavor configurations: N < \Lambda < \Sigma,\Xi < \Delta < \Omega in the rough ordering of \epsilon_h. The associated inferred radii move in the opposite direction: 0.85\ {\rm fm} \to 0.78\ {\rm fm} \to 0.70\ {\rm fm} \to 0.64\ {\rm fm} \to 0.57\ {\rm fm}. Thus the dimensional mechanism is better interpreted as a relation between confinement scale and mass than as a universal fixed mass increment. 7. The pseudoscalar exception The pion and kaon do not follow the vector/baryon pattern. Their inferred constriction energies are much smaller: \epsilon_\pi\simeq66\ {\rm MeV}, \epsilon_K\simeq199\ {\rm MeV}. This is expected to be a decisive test rather than a nuisance. In QCD the light pseudoscalar mesons are special because their masses are controlled strongly by chiral symmetry and its breaking. A purely geometric confinement contribution cannot simply be added to them in the same way as a generic constituent-energy estimate. Therefore any V2 hadron model based on dimensional constriction must contain a channel-dependent cancellation or symmetry protection for pseudoscalar states. Without such a mechanism, the model fails on the pion. 8. What the calculation establishes The 4\to3 oscillator constriction gives an exact relative statement under fixed total action: \boxed{ \omega_3=\frac43\omega_4. } When the large nucleon mass excess is interpreted as the resulting three-dimensional confinement energy, the proton and neutron independently imply \boxed{ \hbar\omega_3\simeq309.5\ {\rm MeV} } and \boxed{ \hbar\omega_4\simeq232.2\ {\rm MeV}. } This corresponds to \boxed{ R_N\simeq0.850\ {\rm fm}, } which is remarkably close to the physical proton-size scale. The broader spectrum rules out the stronger claim that every valence quark simply receives the same 309.5 MeV additive mass. Instead the data require a state-dependent constriction scale R_h, or equivalently a state-dependent projected oscillator frequency. The natural V2 interpretation is therefore \boxed{ M_h =\sum_i m_{q_i} +E_{\rm constriction}[\Psi_h] +E_{\rm spin/flavor}[\Psi_h], } where the first large term is generated by the loss of one accessible spatial degree of freedom and the remaining splittings come from the projected polarization, spin, flavor, and curvature structure of the hadronic state. 9. Why this is compatible with known hadronic mass generation The light-quark current masses account for only a small fraction of the nucleon rest mass. Most nucleon mass is dynamical field and confinement energy rather than the sum of the light current-quark masses. The dimensional-constriction hypothesis does not contradict that fact. It proposes a geometric origin for the dynamical energy: \text{four-dimensional quark mode} \longrightarrow \text{three-dimensional constrained mode} \longrightarrow \text{higher oscillator frequency} \longrightarrow \text{large rest-energy contribution}. In a complete V2 derivation, this contribution must emerge from the projected master Dirac operator rather than being inserted phenomenologically. 10. Connection with the CKM obstruction The CKM calculation independently showed that the 4\to3 transition cannot be a passive partial trace alone. A pure loss map cannot generate the observed u\to s transition because it cannot increase cumulative mode degree. The hadronic-mass calculation points in the same direction. If dimensional reduction constricts the oscillator rather than merely deleting a coordinate, the projected operator must redistribute action among the surviving directions. Therefore the same unresolved cross-sector operator \mathcal R_{34} may be responsible for both \text{mode redistribution / flavor mixing} and \text{confinement energy / hadronic mass generation}. This makes \mathcal R_{34} a central dynamical object rather than a small correction. 11. The missing first-principles calculation The remaining task is sharply defined. Starting from the master operator, D_{34}=P_3D_\infty P_4, one must derive its decomposition into surviving tangential modes and the eliminated normal mode. If the four-dimensional oscillator action is conserved during projection, the operator should contain a term whose expectation value satisfies \langle H_3\rangle =\frac43\langle H_4\rangle for the isotropic ground configuration. The hadronic mass contribution would then be \boxed{ E_{\rm constriction} = \langle\Psi_h| H_3-P_3H_4P_3 |\Psi_h\rangle. } A successful calculation must then derive, rather than fit, the state-dependent length scale R_h or its equivalent oscillator stiffness from the d=3 projected geometry. For the nucleon the target is \boxed{ R_N\approx0.85\ {\rm fm} } or equivalently \boxed{ \hbar\omega_4\approx232\ {\rm MeV}, \qquad \hbar\omega_3\approx310\ {\rm MeV}. } If the projected V2 operator independently produces that scale, the bulk of the nucleon mass follows without using the nucleon mass as an input. If it does not, the numerical agreement found here remains dimensional phenomenology rather than a derivation. 12. Status The present result can be stated compactly: \boxed{ 4\to3\ \text{oscillator constriction at assumed frequency rescaling} \Longrightarrow \omega\to\frac43\omega. } Applied to the observed nucleon mass excess, this yields an inferred pre-constriction scale \boxed{ \hbar\omega_4\simeq232\ {\rm MeV} } and radius \boxed{ R_N\simeq0.850\ {\rm fm}, } which closely matches the physical nucleon-size scale. The wider hadron spectrum shows that dimensional constriction can plausibly account for the dominant confinement-scale mass but cannot by itself explain all hadron masses. Spin, flavor, chiral structure, and state-dependent geometry remain required. The next decisive calculation is therefore not another numerical fit. It is the explicit spectrum of the normal/extrinsic part of P_3D_\infty P_4. That spectrum must simultaneously address the hadronic confinement scale and the mode-changing transitions already demanded by CKM. Data note Hadron masses are representative Particle Data Group central values. The V2 current-quark masses used here are the values already committed in idwt-v2.py: m_u=2.16 MeV, m_d=4.70 MeV, and m_s=93.5 MeV. Numerical conversions use \hbar c=197.3269804\ {\rm MeV\,fm}. Particle Data Group listings: https://pdg.lbl.gov/2026/listings/particle_properties.html 13. Explicit codimension-one Dirac test The previous sections identify the required confinement scale phenomenologically. The next question is whether the canonical codimension-one Dirac geometry itself produces that scale. For a hypersurface Q_3\subset Q_4, choose a unit normal n and a local orthonormal tangent frame e_a, a=1,2,3. In a tubular neighbourhood the ambient Dirac operator has the schematic decomposition D_4 =\gamma(n)\left(\nabla_n+D_3-\frac{3}{2}H\right), up to the conventional sign of \gamma(n) and the convention used for mean curvature H. Here D_3 is the three-dimensional spatial Dirac operator and the curvature term is the codimension-one extrinsic contribution. For a round three-sphere of radius R embedded in flat four-space, the normalized mean curvature is H=\frac1R. The spatial Dirac spectrum on the round S^3(R) is \lambda_k^{\pm} =\pm\frac{k+3/2}{R}, \qquad k=0,1,2,\ldots, so the smallest absolute eigenvalue is \boxed{ |\lambda_0|=\frac{3}{2R}. } At the nucleon-scale radius inferred above, R=0.850\ {\rm fm}, this gives \hbar c\,|\lambda_0| =\frac{3}{2}\frac{\hbar c}{R} \simeq348.2\ {\rm MeV}. This is not the required nucleon confinement contribution \epsilon_N\simeq309.5\ {\rm MeV}. Therefore \boxed{ \text{the nucleon mass scale is not the lowest spatial }S^3\text{ Dirac eigenvalue.} } The scalar Laplacian does not repair the mismatch. Its first nonconstant eigenvalue on S^3(R) is \lambda_{\Delta,1}=\frac{3}{R^2}, which corresponds to the momentum scale \hbar c\sqrt{\lambda_{\Delta,1}} =\sqrt3\frac{\hbar c}{R} \simeq402.1\ {\rm MeV} at R=0.850 fm. Thus the successful 309--310 MeV scale is not an ordinary spatial eigenvalue of a round S^3. 14. The normal oscillator is the viable channel The scale that does line up is the normal confinement quantum. For a codimension-one coordinate y normal to Q_3, introduce the local oscillator Hamiltonian H_\perp =\frac{p_y^2}{2\mu} +\frac12\mu\omega_4^2y^2. Its characteristic quantum is E_\perp=\hbar\omega_4. The V2 oscillator-symbol construction already associates one position and one momentum quadrature with every spatial direction. Removing the fourth accessible direction therefore removes one complete complex oscillator amplitude a_4 =\frac1{\sqrt2} \left( \frac{y}{\ell_4} +i\frac{\ell_4p_y}{\hbar} \right). To obtain a 4/3 frequency multiplier one may separately assume equal oscillator energy and unchanged action I_1 per surviving direction. Then 4\omega_4 I_1 =3\omega_3 I_1, and again \boxed{ \omega_3=\frac43\omega_4. } The resulting three-dimensional mass contribution per quark is \boxed{ \epsilon_{4\to3} =\frac43\hbar\omega_4. } This is distinct from the spatial Dirac curvature energy 3\hbar c/(2R). If the normal oscillator length and frequency satisfy the relativistic confinement scaling \hbar\omega_4=\frac{\hbar c}{R_\perp}, then \boxed{ \epsilon_{4\to3} =\frac43\frac{\hbar c}{R_\perp}. } At R_\perp=0.850\ {\rm fm}, one obtains \hbar\omega_4 =232.15\ {\rm MeV}, and \boxed{ \epsilon_{4\to3} =309.53\ {\rm MeV}. } This agrees with the proton and neutron excess-energy values derived independently from their masses: \epsilon_p=309.751\ {\rm MeV}, \qquad \epsilon_n=309.335\ {\rm MeV}. The mismatch is at the few-10^{-4} to 10^{-3} relative level if R_\perp is chosen near the common mass-inferred radius. 15. What is and is not derived The calculation now separates three statements with different logical status. 15.1 Conditional frequency-rescaling ansatz The dimensional reduction 4\to3 removes one oscillator amplitude. Under the separately imposed frequency-rescaling ansatz, \boxed{ \omega_3/\omega_4=4/3. } This ratio is a model input here, not a consequence of total-action conservation. 15.2 Ruled out as the source of the nucleon bulk mass The canonical spatial spectral scales of a round S^3(R) are \frac{3}{2R} for the lowest Dirac mode and \frac{\sqrt3}{R} for the first scalar momentum scale. Neither gives the observed nucleon excess at the physical radius. Thus the bulk mass cannot be identified with the ordinary spatial S^3 Dirac or scalar spectrum alone. 15.3 Still missing dynamically The absolute normal oscillator scale \omega_4 is not fixed by the currently written V2 master operator. Equivalently, V2 has not yet derived the normal confining potential, boundary condition, or stiffness that would produce \boxed{ \hbar\omega_4\simeq232\ {\rm MeV}. } That is the remaining first-principles problem. The exact operator target is therefore more specific than before. In tubular coordinates (x,y) around the d=3 sector, the normal/extrinsic part of the master operator must reduce to an effective transverse Hamiltonian H_\perp =-\frac{\hbar^2}{2\mu}\partial_y^2+V_\perp(y) or its relativistic Dirac analogue, with lowest characteristic spacing \boxed{ \Delta E_\perp\approx232\ {\rm MeV}. } The projected three-dimensional state must then inherit \boxed{ \Delta E_{3} =\frac43\Delta E_\perp \approx310\ {\rm MeV}. } 16. Sharpened falsification criterion The dimensional-constriction mass proposal is now falsifiable at the operator level. Construct the actual normal potential or normal Dirac block generated by P_3D_\infty P_4. Then compute its lowest normal excitation scale \Delta E_\perp without using nucleon masses or radii. The mechanism succeeds at leading order only if \boxed{ \Delta E_\perp\approx232\ {\rm MeV}, } because assumed frequency-rescaling constriction then predicts \boxed{ \frac43\Delta E_\perp \approx309\text{--}310\ {\rm MeV}. } If the derived normal spectrum instead begins near the spatial round-S^3 Dirac scale 3\hbar c/(2R) or another incompatible value, then the proposed explanation of the nucleon bulk mass fails. This distinction prevents the numerical nucleon agreement from being promoted prematurely to a derivation. 17. Updated status The explicit operator analysis strengthens and narrows the proposal: \boxed{ \text{hadronic bulk mass candidate} =\text{redistributed normal-oscillator energy,} } not \text{spatial }S^3\text{ Dirac energy}. The dimensional factor 4/3 is assumed, not geometrically derived. The absolute normal quantum, approximately 232 MeV for nucleons, is the remaining quantity the master geometry must derive. This same normal/extrinsic block is already independently required by the CKM analysis to change mode degree during the 4\to3 transition. A successful derivation would therefore explain two otherwise separate phenomena with one operator: \boxed{ \mathcal R_{34} \quad\longrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \text{normal-mode energy redistribution} & \text{(hadronic mass)},\\ \text{off-diagonal mode transitions} & \text{(CKM mixing)}. \end{cases} } 18. A closed V2-native candidate for the normal gap Although the existing master action does not yet derive the absolute transverse gap, the committed V2 scales produce one exceptionally close candidate that deserves an explicit test. The depth-three scale is \mu_3=m_e\sqrt{\frac{g_{33}}{g_{66}}}, with g_{33}=8\sqrt7. The product \mu_3g_{33} has dimensions of energy and is built entirely from quantities already fixed in the V2 conditional scale chain. Numerically, \mu_3g_{33}=99.519575\ {\rm MeV}. For a 4\to3 transition, the dimension-incidence ratio \frac{d_{\rm in}+d_{\rm out}}{d_{\rm out}} =\frac{4+3}{3} =\frac73 produces the candidate pre-constriction normal quantum \boxed{ \Delta E_\perp^{\rm cand} =\frac73\mu_3g_{33} =232.212342\ {\rm MeV}. } Fixed-action redistribution then gives \boxed{ \Delta E_3^{\rm cand} =\frac43\Delta E_\perp^{\rm cand} =\frac{28}{9}\mu_3g_{33} =309.616456\ {\rm MeV}. } No proton or neutron mass enters this numerical value once \mu_3 and g_{33} are taken from the existing V2 scale construction. Using m_u=2.16\ {\rm MeV}, \qquad m_d=4.70\ {\rm MeV}, the resulting nucleon predictions are \boxed{ m_p^{\rm cand} =2m_u+m_d+3\Delta E_3^{\rm cand} =937.869369\ {\rm MeV}, } compared with m_p=938.272088\ {\rm MeV}. The difference is \boxed{-0.403\ {\rm MeV}}, or about -0.043\%. For the neutron, \boxed{ m_n^{\rm cand} =m_u+2m_d+3\Delta E_3^{\rm cand} =940.409369\ {\rm MeV}, } compared with m_n=939.565421\ {\rm MeV}, a difference of \boxed{+0.844\ {\rm MeV}}, or about +0.090\%. Thus the same V2-native candidate confinement quantum lands between the proton and neutron requirements: \epsilon_p=309.750696\ {\rm MeV}, \Delta E_3^{\rm cand}=309.616456\ {\rm MeV}, \epsilon_n=309.335140\ {\rm MeV}. 18.1 Why the 7/3 coefficient is not yet derived The numerical agreement alone is not sufficient to establish \Delta E_\perp=\frac73\mu_3g_{33}. There are two structural observations behind the candidate coefficient: the spatial transition has incoming depth four and surviving depth three, so \frac{d_{\rm in}+d_{\rm out}}{d_{\rm out}}=\frac73; each spatial direction carries a position and momentum quadrature, so the reciprocal 4\to3 phase-space contact involves eight incoming and six surviving real quadratures, giving the same ratio \frac{8+6}{6}=\frac73. The V2 cross-depth action is reciprocal: the lower-depth state samples the complete marginal of the higher-depth state, while the higher-depth state feels the lower-depth state uniformly across the additional fibre. This makes a normalization involving both incident and surviving sectors plausible. However, the currently written action does not contain a theorem saying that the reciprocal contact energy is normalized by \frac{2d_{\rm in}+2d_{\rm out}}{2d_{\rm out}}. Thus the bound-state calculation seeks \boxed{\ker\!\left[z_BI_{P_B}-\mathsf H_{\rm eff}(z_B)\right]\ne\{0\}.} A determinant equation is available in a finite representation. At excluded complementary eigenvalues, the original system must be checked or the model space enlarged; denominator clearing alone is insufficient. This is standard Feshbach-Schur reduction, not a newly derived V2 interaction. See Dusson, Sigal, and Stamm, The Feshbach-Schur map and perturbation theory, Theorem 1.2 and equations (1.15)--(1.16). The independently checked two-channel example in Section 74 fixes the sign convention used here. 76.2 Derive the color factor from the specified generators The V2 gauge-block proposal uses fundamental generators T^a=\lambda^a/2. With \operatorname{tr}(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}/2, define C_{ij}=\sum_{a=1}^8T_i^aT_j^a =\frac12\left(\mathsf X_{ij}-\frac13I\right), where \mathsf X_{ij} exchanges the two color slots. The generator normalization and completeness identity are standard; see Haber, Useful relations among the generators in the defining and adjoint representations of SU(N). On the determinant singlet, \mathsf X_{ij}=-I. Therefore \boxed{P_\epsilon C_{ij}P_\epsilon=-\frac23P_\epsilon,} \qquad \boxed{P_\epsilon\sum_{i<j}C_{ij}P_\epsilon=-2P_\epsilon.} The sum contains three unordered pairs. These are operator eigenvalues from representation theory, not field amplitudes and not an inserted hadron-mass fit. 76.3 What this fixes in an actual pair interaction If the derived dimensionless interaction has the form \mathsf V_{\rm pair}(z)=\sum_{i<j}C_{ij}\otimes K_{ij}(z), with K_{ij}(z) acting on the remaining factors, its singlet restriction is \boxed{\mathsf V_{{\rm pair},B}(z)=-\frac23\sum_{i<j}K_{ij}(z).} It reduces to -2K(z) only when the three remaining pair operators actually coincide. It does not supply a universal frequency ratio of two or 2/3. The sign is retained; whether this is an attractive contribution depends on the remaining operator convention. This form is a conditional template for matching to the V2 master interaction. The audit has derived its color coefficient, not the existence, radial dependence, spin dependence, or normalization of K_{ij}. 76.4 What has and has not been solved The static/spectral Schur distinction, the projection-versus-frequency error, and the singlet pair coefficient have been resolved exactly. A normalized eigenvector may be used to represent a mode, but no measured field amplitude is used as an input. Electron anchoring fixes the unit. It does not, by itself, determine every dimensionless interaction coefficient. The next calculation must derive the remaining blocks and their spectral dependence from the V2 dynamics, retaining induced terms rather than guessing an integer near the desired mass. No numerical baryon-frequency prediction is claimed by this revision.

title: Neutrino mass splittings and the simplex spectrum
text:
Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. 1. Result In the V2 neutrino sector, the three occupied modes are (n_{
u_1},n_{
u_2},n_{
u_3})=(10,15,22), at depth d_
u=5. The bare mass law is m_i=\mu_5 S(n_i,5), \qquad S(n,d)= inom{n+d-1}{d}. For the three neutrino modes, S(10,5)=2002, S(15,5)=11628, S(22,5)=65780. Therefore (m_1,m_2,m_3) =\mu_5(2002,11628,65780). The common normalization \mu_5 cancels exactly from the ratio of the two independent mass-squared splittings. The V2 neutrino assignments therefore make a parameter-free prediction:  oxed{  rac{\Delta m_{21}^2}{\Delta m_{31}^2} =  rac{11628^2-2002^2}{65780^2-2002^2} =0.030349842234897634. } The depth-scan companion uses a different PDG-2024 benchmark and reports 1.98\% for that comparison. The 2.68\% below belongs specifically to the two inputs displayed here; these benchmarks must not be interchanged when quoting accuracy. Using the benchmark oscillation values \Delta m_{21}^2=7.49	imes10^{-5}\ {m eV}^2, \Delta m_{31}^2=2.534	imes10^{-3}\ {m eV}^2, the observed ratio is  rac{\Delta m_{21}^2}{\Delta m_{31}^2} =0.029558011049723762. The V2 simplex prediction is therefore high by approximately  oxed{2.68\%}. This comparison contains no fitted neutrino mass scale. 2. Independent reconstruction of the neutrino scale The same mass law permits \mu_5 to be inferred independently from either measured splitting. From the solar splitting, \Delta m_{21}^2 =\mu_5^2\left[S(15,5)^2-S(10,5)^2ight], so \mu_5^{(21)} = \sqrt{  rac{\Delta m_{21}^2} {11628^2-2002^2} } =7.5556190385	imes10^{-7}\ {m eV}. From the atmospheric splitting, \Delta m_{31}^2 =\mu_5^2\left[S(22,5)^2-S(10,5)^2ight], so \mu_5^{(31)} = \sqrt{  rac{\Delta m_{31}^2} {65780^2-2002^2} } =7.6561541256	imes10^{-7}\ {m eV}. Their ratio is  rac{\mu_5^{(21)}}{\mu_5^{(31)}} =0.9868687221. Thus the two experimentally independent splittings infer the same sector normalization to approximately  oxed{1.31\%}. This is a direct internal consistency test of the one-scale neutrino-sector hypothesis. 3. Absolute neutrino masses Once either splitting fixes \mu_5, the simplex law determines the absolute neutrino masses. Using \Delta m_{21}^2 gives m_1=0.00151263\ {m eV}, m_2=0.00878567\ {m eV}, m_3=0.04970086\ {m eV}, and hence  oxed{ \sum_i m_i=0.05999917\ {m eV}. } Using \Delta m_{31}^2 instead gives m_1=0.00153276\ {m eV}, m_2=0.00890258\ {m eV}, m_3=0.05036218\ {m eV}, with  oxed{ \sum_i m_i=0.06079752\ {m eV}. } The two independent absolute-spectrum reconstructions therefore lie in the narrow interval \sum_i m_i\simeq0.0600	ext{--}0.0608\ {m eV}. The absolute spectrum is not an additional fit once one measured splitting fixes the common normalization. The second splitting then tests the mode pattern. 4. Joint one-scale reconstruction A single common scale may also be chosen to reproduce both measured splittings simultaneously. If a=S(15,5)^2-S(10,5)^2, b=S(22,5)^2-S(10,5)^2, and x=\mu_5^2, the unweighted least-squares value minimizing (xa-\Delta m_{21}^2)^2 +(xb-\Delta m_{31}^2)^2 is x=  rac{a\Delta m_{21}^2+b\Delta m_{31}^2} {a^2+b^2}. This gives \mu_5=7.6560622136	imes10^{-7}\ {m eV}, and (m_1,m_2,m_3) = (0.00153274,0.00890247,0.05036158)\ {m eV}. The corresponding mass sum is  oxed{ \sum_i m_i=0.06079679\ {m eV}. } The reconstructed splittings are \Delta m_{21}^2=7.69047	imes10^{-5}\ {m eV}^2, \Delta m_{31}^2=2.53394	imes10^{-3}\ {m eV}^2. Because the atmospheric splitting is numerically much larger, an unweighted fit in absolute squared residuals is dominated by it. The scale-free ratio in Section 1 is the cleaner test of the simplex pattern itself. 5. Why the result is nontrivial For three masses obeying m_i=\mu_5 S(n_i,5), the two measured splittings are \Delta m_{21}^2 =\mu_5^2 \left[S(n_2,5)^2-S(n_1,5)^2ight], \Delta m_{31}^2 =\mu_5^2 \left[S(n_3,5)^2-S(n_1,5)^2ight]. Their ratio removes the only continuous parameter: R_
u =  rac{S(n_2,5)^2-S(n_1,5)^2} {S(n_3,5)^2-S(n_1,5)^2}. Once the discrete mode triple (10,15,22) and depth d=5 are specified, R_
u is fixed. The comparison with oscillation data is therefore not a three-mass fit and not a one-parameter fit. It is a test of the discrete spectrum shape. The second form of the same test is to infer \mu_5 separately from each measured splitting. If the simplex mode assignments were badly wrong, the two inferred scales would generally disagree. Instead they differ by only about 1.31\%. 6. Relation to depth selection The same scale-free ratio can be evaluated while keeping the mode indices fixed and varying the candidate depth: R_
u(d)=  rac{S(15,d)^2-S(10,d)^2} {S(22,d)^2-S(10,d)^2}. For the neighboring depths, R_
u(4)\approx0.05550, R_
u(5)\approx0.03035, R_
u(6)\approx0.01686. Thus the observed oscillation hierarchy selects d=5 sharply relative to the adjacent integer depths. This result is also summarized in the mass-spectrum depth test. 7. What is established and what remains conditional Established mathematics Given the V2 mass law and the stated neutrino mode assignments: the simplex counts are exactly (2002,11628,65780); the predicted splitting ratio is exactly 0.030349842234897634; the ratio is independent of \mu_5; the two measured splittings independently infer nearly the same \mu_5; fixing \mu_5 from either splitting determines the complete absolute spectrum; the resulting mass sum is approximately 0.060--0.061\ {m eV}. Conditional inputs The physical interpretation remains conditional on the mode assignments (10,15,22) being selected independently of the measured neutrino splittings; the neutrino sector obeying the same one-scale simplex mass law as the other V2 sectors; normal mass ordering; the benchmark oscillation measurements used in the numerical comparison. The result does not by itself derive the mode-selection rule or the projected normalization \mu_5 from the master geometry. 8. Discrete null tests The immediate null test is discrete rather than continuous. For all ordered integer triples 1\leq n_1<n_2<n_3\leq N, at fixed depth d=5, define R(n_1,n_2,n_3) =  rac{S(n_2,5)^2-S(n_1,5)^2} {S(n_3,5)^2-S(n_1,5)^2}. 8.1 Unrestricted integer triples The unrestricted search is deliberately permissive: every increasing integer triple is allowed, without imposing the V2 mode-selection construction. Using the benchmark ratio R_{m obs}=0.02955801105, the committed V2 triple (10,15,22) has relative error 2.6789\%. It is good but not unique in the unrestricted search. Its rank remains near the best 0.6\% of triples as the cutoff grows: Maximum index N Number of triples Rank of (10,15,22) Percentile 22 1,540 10 0.649% 30 4,060 24 0.591% 50 19,600 111 0.566% 75 67,525 390 0.578% 100 161,700 909 0.562% 150 551,300 3,153 0.572% 200 1,313,400 7,269 0.553% Many arbitrary triples fit the oscillation ratio more closely. For example, (5,10,15) gives a relative error of about 0.099\%, and by N=200 some accidental triples match at the 10^{-3}\% level. Therefore the oscillation ratio by itself is not strong evidence for the particular integers (10,15,22). The unrestricted null does exactly what it should: it shows that one real-valued ratio can be approximated well by many freely chosen discrete triples. 8.2 Null constrained by the V2 mode-generation rule The physically relevant comparison is narrower because the V2 indices are not arbitrary integers. The mode-selection construction generates the first two neutrino indices from a common seed k through adjacent simplex firings, n_1(k)=S(k,3), n_2(k)=S(k,4), and generates the third through the inclusion--exclusion pushout n_3(k)=n_1(k)+n_2(k)-k. For the committed seed k=3 this gives S(3,3)=10, \qquad S(3,4)=15, \qquad 10+15-3=22. The resulting index triple is then passed through the independent depth-five mass law, m_i(k)=\mu_5 S(n_i(k),5). Scanning the seed family 1\leq k\leq100 gives the following leading results: Seed k Generated triple Predicted R_
u Relative error 3 (10,15,22) 0.03034984 2.679% 5 (35,70,100) 0.03064535 3.679% 4 (20,35,51) 0.02724713 7.818% 6 (56,126,176) 0.03695042 25.010% 7 (84,210,287) 0.04511132 52.620% 8 (120,330,442) 0.05464059 84.859% 2 (4,5,7) 0.06057782 104.946% Within this constrained family,  oxed{k=3\ 	ext{ranks first among all tested seeds }1\leq k\leq100.} This distinction is essential. The unrestricted null shows that arbitrary integer triples can fit the measured ratio easily. The constrained null shows that the specific triple generated by the V2 contact-resonance construction is the best member of the tested seed-generated family. The evidential content therefore lies not in the ratio alone but in the composition of two independent structures: 	ext{mode selection} \longrightarrow (10,15,22) \longrightarrow 	ext{depth-five simplex masses} \longrightarrow R_
u. The remaining question is whether the seed rule and pushout are themselves uniquely forced by the projected master interaction rather than chosen after the spectrum is known. 9. A caution on extrapolated higher neutrino modes The simplex law exists for every positive integer n, but this does not imply that every integer mode corresponds to a physical neutrino state. Physical states require the independent V2 mode-selection mechanism. For example, S(36,5)=658008, so if n=36 were independently shown to be an occupied neutrino mode, its bare mass would satisfy  rac{m(36,5)}{m(22,5)} =  rac{658008}{65780} =10.0031620553. The large-n approximation \left( rac{36}{22}ight)^5 \approx11.7327 overestimates the exact simplex ratio by about 17.3\%. No heavy-neutrino prediction should therefore be attached to n=36, or to any other unoccupied integer, until the selection mechanism derives that mode independently. 10. Falsifiable next calculation The neutrino sector now presents two separate mathematical problems: Discrete uniqueness: determine whether (10,15,22) is exceptional among competing integer triples under fair null ensembles. Geometric normalization: calculate \mu_5 from the projected master kernel rather than from either oscillation splitting. The second problem is especially decisive. If the master projection independently produces \mu_5\approx7.6	imes10^{-7}\ {m eV}, then the three absolute neutrino masses and both oscillation splittings become outputs of the same geometry. If the projected normalization is incompatible with that scale, the neutrino realization of the V2 simplex mass law is false.

title: Contact-kernel audit
summary: Point-contact and smooth-density spectra are compared without identifying their operators.
text:
Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Point-contact and smooth-density spectra are compared without identifying their operators. NOT A PHYSICS MODULE. These are exact finite-band comparison calculations and an action-level audit. The graph-supported point-contact construction remains a live hypothesis; no alternative tested here is silently substituted for it. 1. The source distinction that motivated the test The self-contact source, Section 6.2, explicitly lifts the scalar current onto the graph of a chosen projective ray: \mathcal J_d(q,[u])=J_d(q)\delta_{m FS}([u],[z_{\Psi_d}(q)]), \qquad J_d= ar\Psi_d\Psi_d. It then writes the scalar interaction \mathcal L_{m sc}=-(\kappa_d/2)J_d^2, whose scalar Euler--Lagrange term is -\kappa_dJ_d\Psi_d. Its diagonal kernel is local multiplication. Later in the same subsection, the self-field insertion is identified with a delta concentrated at the selected ray. Section 6.3 proves the finite-band projection theorem for that point insertion, and Section 6.4 applies it to the proposed nonlinear Dirac term. The distinction is important: a kernel f(u)\delta(u,u') specifies multiplication by f, whereas a coefficient f(u)=\delta(u,z) specifies a point-supported multiplier. Locality of the diagonal kernel alone does not choose that coefficient. The graph lift is explicitly an additional part of the written construction; it must neither be ignored nor mistaken for an already completed derivation of the action's projected dynamics. Merely integrating J(q)^2 against the normalized graph delta returns J(q)^2. It does not automatically insert a new finite-band pairing kernel into the action. Establishing that pairing is the remaining dynamical step identified by this audit, not a request for an amplitude measurement. 2. The exact point-contact theorem survives For \mathcal H_N=H^0(\mathbb{CP}^d,\mathcal O(N)), \qquad D_N= inom{N+d}{d}, use unit Fubini-Study measure and the specified homogeneous Hermitian normalization. The reproducing kernel has constant diagonal K_N(z,z)=D_N. Its normalized coherent line is |z;Nangle=K_{N,z}/\sqrt{D_N}. The point-symbol quadratic form is \langle s,T_{\delta_z}tangle=\overline{s(z)}t(z). It gives T_{\delta_z}=P_N\delta_zP_N =|K_{N,z}angle\langle K_{N,z}| =D_N|z;Nangle\langle z;N|. Its nonzero eigenvalue is exactly D_N. This result depends on the stated ray, finite band, measure, and covariance assumptions. It is not the claim that every algebraic scalar interaction has this spectrum. The source itself makes isotropic projective completion a necessary premise and separately requires a band-blind normalized coefficient; see Sections 6.3--6.4 and 9. 3. Three different local multiplier prescriptions In the same finite Hilbert space, compare the following unit-normalized symbols: Symbol on the ray space Projected operator spectrum Constant 1 Eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity D_N Point source \delta_z Eigenvalue D_N once, otherwise zero Smooth coherent density j_z(u)=D_N|\langle u,zangle|^{2N} Full positive spectrum below, with largest eigenvalue D_N^2/D_{2N} All three have projected trace D_N. Equal trace therefore does not imply equal spectrum. The smooth case has rank D_N, whereas the point case has rank one. These are different operators, not alternative normalizations of the same eigenvector. The smooth symbol is normalized because \int_{\mathbb{CP}^d}|\langle u,zangle|^{2N}d
u(u)= rac{1}{D_N}. It is a comparison prescription: the source graph lift selects a point symbol, not automatically this smooth density. 4. Full smooth-symbol spectrum Choose z along coordinate zero. On normalized degree-N monomials, let k be the occupation of that coordinate. The remaining d occupations sum to N-k. Unit-FS monomial moments obey \int \prod_{r=0}^{d}|u_r|^{2m_r}d
u(u) = rac{d!\prod_rm_r!}{(d+\sum_rm_r)!}. The normalized monomial of multi-index \alpha, |\alpha|=N, has squared normalization (N+d)!/(d!\prod_r\alpha_r!). Multiplication by D_N|u_0|^{2N} therefore gives the diagonal eigenvalue  oxed{\lambda_k =D_N rac{(N+d)!}{(2N+d)!} rac{(N+k)!}{k!}}, \qquad 0\le k\le N, with multiplicity  oxed{m_k= inom{N-k+d-1}{d-1}}. Phase invariance makes the off-diagonal monomial integrals vanish. The largest eigenvalue occurs at k=N and simplifies to  oxed{\lambda_{\max}= rac{D_N^2}{D_{2N}}}. The checks verify positivity, \sum_km_k=D_N, and \sum_km_k\lambda_k=D_N for the tested bands, using exact rational arithmetic. They do not require constructing the largest matrices explicitly. N,d D_N Smooth largest eigenvalue Smooth largest eigenvalue divided by D_N 1,1 2 4/3 2/3 2,2 6 12/5 2/5 3,3 20 100/21 5/21 2,4 15 45/14 3/14 12,6 18564 580.391724138 0.0312643678161 34,6 3838380 79530.8961572 0.0207199120872 For example, at (N,d)=(3,3) the complete spectrum is 5/21, 20/21, 50/21, 100/21, with multiplicities 10,6,3,1, respectively. 5. A same-sector shape test, not a scale fit Using the already specified electron and muon bands, N_e=12, N_\mu=34, d=6, a common band-independent coefficient cancels in either prescription. The point prescription gives  rac{D_{34}}{D_{12}}= rac{3515}{17} \approx206.764705882353. The smooth-symbol occupied-line prescription gives  rac{D_{34}^2/D_{68}}{D_{12}^2/D_{24}} = rac{9441729375}{68902802} \approx137.029686760779. These are calculated spectral ratios under two different prescriptions, not new experimental measurements. An overall electron unit conversion cannot make the prescriptions identical. This demonstrates the importance of the operator choice. It does not disprove the graph-supported point construction by imposing the smooth construction in its place. No experimental precision or significance claim is made in this note. 6. Single contact evaluation versus double smearing The finite-band coherent pairing kernel is B_N(z,w)=\langle z;N|T_{\delta_w}|z;Nangle =D_N|\langle z,wangle|^{2N}. It satisfies \int B_N(z,w)d
u(w)=1, \qquad B_N(z,z)=D_N. A point source evaluated at its own ray uses the coincident value of this one kernel. Replacing the source by its smooth coherent density and averaging the test coherent density against it instead gives \int B_N(z,w)^2d
u(w)= rac{D_N^2}{D_{2N}}. This is the previously undocumented explanation of the two eigenvalues. A graph-source interaction with one such finite-band pairing can retain the linear simplex count; two smoothings yield a different quantity. Neither operation may be silently substituted for the other. What remains open is the action-level origin and ordering of the pairing: the proposed graph current, the nonlinear variation, and the finite-band projection have to be joined in one specified construction. The test establishes a consistent mathematical distinction, not that the full master action has already supplied this joining. 7. Moving self-consistent ray: the limited cancellation that is exact Differentiate P^2=P for a differentiable orthogonal projector: (\delta P)P+P(\delta P)=\delta P. Multiplying by P on both sides gives  oxed{P(\delta P)P=0.} For a normalized u on the occupied line, \langle u,\delta P\,uangle=0. This was checked with a complex ray u=(3/5,4i/5)^T and a Hermitian generator of projector motion. It removes the automatic objection that every change of the self-consistent ray must shift the occupied eigenvalue at first order. It does not imply (\delta P)u=0, erase off-diagonal variations, or prove the full nonlinear Euler--Lagrange equation. In particular, derivative dependence of the ray, variation of the contact coefficient, kinetic contributions, and stability of the coherent branch remain separate questions. No claim of complete variational closure follows from the diagonal projector identity. 8. Findings to carry forward Checked: the point-contact identity; the constant, point, and smooth comparison spectra; the exact smooth-symbol family ratio; normalization and coincidence of the single pairing kernel; its squared-kernel integral; and the diagonal moving-projector cancellation. Not established: that ordinary diagonal locality alone forces the graph symbol; that the graph lift by itself supplies the required action pairing; that double smearing is the correct V2 prescription; that the chosen coherent branch solves and is selected by the full projected dynamics; or that these calculations determine a baryon frequency. No current magnitude, field amplitude, or profile parameter was fitted. The unknowns are operator identification and the derivation or cancellation of their physical coefficients. The regression script reproduces the finite tests; the source passages are self-contact Sections 6.1--6.4 and 9. Related Research status — current proof boundaries and correction guidance.

title: Circulating isotropic orbitals
summary: Auxiliary model only: Pure excited orbitals can have isotropic position moments while carrying a full-rank circulation that supplies a conditional singlet spin source.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Auxiliary model only: Pure excited orbitals can have isotropic position moments while carrying a full-rank circulation that supplies a conditional singlet spin source. Interpretation correction This calculation concerns an auxiliary field or local spin model, not the actual electron orbit constructed in the 6D demo. Its stationary states, angular expectations, and stability results have not been mapped to that trajectory or its observer readout. They must not be used as a replacement for the existing orbit-shape derivation. See Actual orbit research correction. 1. Position moments do not exhaust orbital data The positive scalar ground-state result remains intact. The following is an excited-state construction, not another ground-state minimum. It shows why isotropic second moments do not imply vanishing orbital current. Use a flat six-dimensional oscillator H_omega=p^2+omega^2 r^2, with unit norm, and split its real basis into O=(e1,e2,e3) and H=(e4,e5,e6). Define orthonormal circular modes z_a=(e_a-i e_(a+3))/sqrt(2), a=1,2,3. In the oscillator shell of total degree N>=2 take \phi_N=\frac1{\sqrt3}\sum_{a=1}^3|N\hbox{ quanta in }z_a\rangle. This is a pure superposition, not a mixture. The coordinate polynomials (x_a-i x_(a+3))^N are harmonic, so the state lies in ell=N as well as shell N. Its one-body cross matrix elements vanish because a one-body operator cannot transfer all N>=2 quanta between two orthogonal modes. With rho the trace-N one-body density matrix, \rho=\frac N3 P_-,\qquad P_-=\frac12(I+iJ_0),\qquad J_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_3\\-I_3&0\end{pmatrix}. Thus Re rho=N I/6, while Im rho=N J_0/6 is nonzero. For a fixed shell, the anomalous expectations of two creation or two annihilation operators vanish, giving M=\langle xx^T\rangle=\frac{N+3}{6\omega}I_6, \qquad \langle L\rangle=-2\operatorname{Im}\rho=-\frac N3J_0. The position covariance is isotropic and the circulation has full rank six. The density itself need not be isotropic: the quadratic scalar kernel sees only its second moments, not its higher angular moments. 2. These are scalar self-consistent stationary solutions For the single-sector functional E=T+(g/2)tr M^2 with g>0, variation gives the mean-field potential g x^T M x. It equals omega^2 r^2 precisely when \omega_N^3=\frac{g(N+3)}6. At that width, phi_N is an exact stationary scalar Hartree solution, with phase eigenvalue mu=(2N+6)omega_N. Its energy is E=(3/2)(N+3)omega_N, not mu. For N=2, choosing omega=1 gives g=6/5, M=5I/6, and mu=10. The scalar problem supplies an entire symmetry-related family, not a chosen absolute J_0 or a particle-index selector. The state is above the unconstrained scalar ground state. Its linear stability is a separate calculation. 3. Conditional spin source and the circulation sign If this orbital is used in the local vector-potential Dirac reduction of the spin-orbit audit, its angular expectation produces \mathcal S=-\frac N3\sum_{a=1}^3\Sigma_{a,a+3}. In the stated chiral convention this has eigenvalues {-N,N/3,N/3,N/3}. For a positive spin-orbit coefficient the unique lowest ray lies in the locked orbit, with complex structure J_0. Reversing the orbital circulation negates the matrix and gives a triply degenerate lowest eigenvalue instead. Thus the current sign relative to chirality and the interaction coefficient must be retained; a magnitude-only source calculation misses the distinction. The scalar Hartree functional does not prove that its potential is the time-component vector potential of the Dirac model. Nor does a projected spin matrix identify the spatial Dirac-section fibre with the homogeneous CP3 base coordinate. These bridges remain open. 4. A shared-well normalization constraint With fixed g and unit norm, these isolated self-bound solutions have N-dependent omega_N. They cannot all be treated as excitations of one fixed harmonic well while each is simultaneously taken to source that well alone. For charge Q the relation becomes omega_N^3=g Q(N+3)/6. Keeping omega fixed would require Q proportional to 1/(N+3), or a separate dominant background that fixes the well. Neither is supplied by the one-quantum normalization. This does not disprove a fixed-background cumulative-band construction. It specifies what must distinguish that construction from isolated self-binding. N here is a flat oscillator degree, not an independently derived assignment to an electron, a chemistry orbital, or a V2 projective band. Verification circulating_hartree_checks.py verifies the N=2 state's norm, moment matrix, self-consistent width, one-body current, and both signed chiral spectra. Its further linearized checks are documented separately. The general N>=2 statements follow from the one-body selection rule and the displayed moment identities.
