Orbital projection source test — the earlier two-plane construction is extended to three planes and isotropic position moments. Spin-orbit source audit — supplies the conditional derivative vertex and its approximation limits. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Controlled orbital gap
summary: Auxiliary model only: An exactly solved orbital-gap model quantifies when a projected spin source survives orbital backreaction.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Auxiliary model only: An exactly solved orbital-gap model quantifies when a projected spin source survives orbital backreaction. Interpretation correction This calculation concerns an auxiliary field or local spin model, not the actual electron orbit constructed in the 6D demo. Its stationary states, angular expectations, and stability results have not been mapped to that trajectory or its observer readout. They must not be used as a replacement for the existing orbit-shape derivation. See Actual orbit research correction. Supplied selector, not a derived interaction Let A = Σ σ_ab ⊗ L_ab on the harmonic degree-two orbital space tensored with one chiral spinor. Its spectrum is −6 (multiplicity 20), +2 (multiplicity 60). Choose the normalized two-plane quadratic orbital φ in the projection source test. Let P = I₄ ⊗ |φ⟩⟨φ| and Q = I − P. Study the deliberately supplied selector \mathcal H=\epsilon A+\Delta Q,\qquad \epsilon>0,\quad\Delta>0. Δ is an orbital gap assumption. This projector penalty is not claimed to be a local potential, a result of the scalar moment functional, or part of the already derived V2 action. Its role is to turn the frozen-orbital approximation into a solvable diagnostic. Exact reduction The compressed spin operator H₀ = ⟨φ|A|φ⟩ has eigenvalues h = −2, −2/3, 2/3, 2. On the harmonic orbital space, A² + 4A = 12I. For v_h = s_h ⊗ φ, define c_h = 12 − 4h − h². If c_h > 0, w_h = (A − h)v_h / √c_h is orthogonal to P and the two-dimensional span is invariant. In its orthonormal basis, \mathcal H_h=\begin{pmatrix} \epsilon h&\epsilon\sqrt{c_h}\\ \epsilon\sqrt{c_h}&\Delta+\epsilon(-4-h) \end{pmatrix}, E_\pm(h)=\frac{\Delta-4\epsilon \pm\sqrt{\Delta^2-4\epsilon\Delta(2+h)+64\epsilon^2}}{2}. The h = 2 case has c_h = 0 and only the actual vector v_h with energy 2ε. The second formal root is not a second vector in this collapsed two-dimensional construction. Other harmonic states can independently have the dark energies Δ − 6ε and Δ + 2ε. Selection and its error For every positive Δ and ε the unique ground branch is h = −2: E_0=\frac{\Delta-4\epsilon-\sqrt{\Delta^2+64\epsilon^2}}2 =-2\epsilon-\frac{16\epsilon^2}{\Delta} +O(\epsilon^4/\Delta^3). It is below the dark energy Δ − 6ε. At Δ = 0 the original 20-fold ground degeneracy returns; the gap begins as Δ/6 and approaches 4ε/3 as Δ/ε grows. In this particular orbital example, tracing out the orbital gives fidelity with the projected ground spin ray F=\frac12\left(1+\frac{\Delta} {\sqrt{\Delta^2+64\epsilon^2}}\right) =1-\frac{16\epsilon^2}{\Delta^2} +O(\epsilon^4/\Delta^4). At Δ/ε = 1, 10, 100 the fidelities are approximately 0.5620, 0.8904, 0.9984. Existence of a unique ground is therefore much weaker than accuracy of a frozen pure-spin state. The second-order effective operator is εH₀ − (ε²/Δ)(12I − 4H₀ − H₀²), preserving its spin eigenvectors in this model but not eliminating orbital entanglement. Reproduction and boundary orbital_gap_checks.py checks invariant blocks, full eigenvalues, and reduced-spin fidelities at five gap strengths. Its 84-dimensional implementation retains the scalar trace sector as four decoupled states of energy Δ; this does not alter the harmonic ground. What remains is to derive an orbital-selecting operator, its strength, its sign, and the appropriate field-to-spatial-coordinate relation. summary: Auxiliary model only: The coupled scalar 3-in-6 model admits excited circulating stationary states with an exact oscillatory linear moment spectrum along the equal-coupling family.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: Auxiliary model only: The coupled scalar 3-in-6 model admits excited circulating stationary states with an exact oscillatory linear moment spectrum along the equal-coupling family. Interpretation correction This calculation concerns an auxiliary field or local spin model, not the actual electron orbit constructed in the 6D demo. Its stationary states, angular expectations, and stability results have not been mapped to that trajectory or its observer readout. They must not be used as a replacement for the existing orbit-shape derivation. See Actual orbit research correction. 1. Same functional, different branch Use the positive rank-one, fixed-embedding 3-in-6 scalar functional from the ground-state moment test, with both norms and kinetic coefficients one. The mean-field quadratic matrices are W_3=v_3^2M_3+v_3v_6PM_6P^T,\qquad W_6=v_6^2M_6+v_3v_6P^TM_3P, \qquad P=(I_3,0). The unique ground-state covariance has no mixed current. That result did not exclude excited stationary solutions. The following construction includes the nuclear-sector response instead of assuming it is absent. 2. Elliptical circular modes Put r = √(v₃/v₆). Choose an integer N ≥ 2 with N > 3r/2, and set \alpha^2=\frac12-\frac{3r}{4N},\qquad \beta^2=\frac12+\frac{3r}{4N},\qquad \omega^3=v_6^2\left(\frac{N+3}{6}+\frac r4\right). Use three orthonormal complex oscillator modes z_a = αe_a − iβe_(a+3), and the pure shell state φ = 3^(-1/2) Σ_a |N quanta in z_a⟩. For α ≠ β its coordinate polynomial is not simply a harmonic power: it is defined by applying the oscillator creation operator N times. It remains in the oscillator shell N, but need not have a single angular degree ℓ. N is not identified with a CP3 band. Take the nuclear field to be the oscillator ground state with frequency ω₃ = rω. The moments are M_3=aI_3,\quad a=\frac1{2r\omega},\qquad M_6=\operatorname{diag}(m_OI_3,m_HI_3), m_O=\frac{1/2+N\alpha^2/3}{\omega},\qquad m_H=\frac{1/2+N\beta^2/3}{\omega}. Substitution gives exactly W₃ = r²ω²I₃ and W₆ = ω²I₆. Increased unobserved width compensates the additional observed-plane nuclear term. Both fields are consequently eigenfunctions of their own self-consistent operators, with μ₃ = 3rω and μ₆ = (2N+6)ω. These are phase eigenvalues, not total energies or physical rest masses. The mixed position covariance vanishes, but the angular expectation is \langle L\rangle=-\frac{2N\alpha\beta}{3}J_0. It has full rank for the strict threshold N > 3r/2. At equality α = 0, the circulation disappears. This is a family of current-carrying excited states, not an orientation selected by minimizing the unrestricted energy. 3. Exact linear moment spectrum at one point For N = 2 and v₃ = v₆ = √(12/13), both frequencies are one: α² = 1/8, β² = 7/8, M₃ = I₃/2, M₆ = diag(7I₃/12,13I₃/12), C₆ = −√7 J₀/12, C₃ = 0. Here C_ab = ⟨{x_a,p_b}⟩/2 and K_d = ⟨p_dp_dᵀ⟩ = M_d. For each sector the exact quadratic moment equations are \dot M_d=2(C_d+C_d^T),\quad \dot C_d=2K_d-2M_dW_d,\quad \dot K_d=-2(W_dC_d+C_d^TW_d). Their full real linearization has 99 variables. Six independent symmetric 3-by-3 spatial components each carry an identical 13-dimensional block; three antisymmetric components each carry a 7-dimensional block. The characteristic polynomials for the growth exponent λ are p_S(\lambda)=\frac{\lambda^3(\lambda^2+16)(\lambda^2+24)}{169} (169\lambda^6+7800\lambda^4+89856\lambda^2+7168), p_A(\lambda)=\frac{\lambda^5(13\lambda^2+288)}{13}. For the remaining squared frequencies u = −λ², the cubic 169u³ − 7800u² + 89856u − 7168 has one root in each of (0,1), (20,22), and (24,25), by endpoint sign changes. These exhaust its roots and are positive. Thus every nonzero moment exponent is purely imaginary. As in the single-sector analysis, the full field linearization is a pair of self-adjoint oscillator evolutions forced only by these closed moment variables. No nonzero exponential instability can hide entirely outside the moments. Neutral modes, resonant polynomial growth, and nonlinear stability still need separate analysis. The symbolic calculation extends to every N ≥ 2 on the equal-coupling branch, choosing units with ω = 1 and g = v₃² = v₆² = 12/(2N+9). Here g denotes the rescaled coefficient: for an original fixed physical coupling g₀ it is g₀/ω³. This rescaling is fixed by self-consistency and does not retune g₀ separately for each state. Physical growth exponents and frequencies are restored by multiplying by ω. Put D = 2N+9. The symmetric block keeps the factors λ³(λ²+16)(λ²+24); its remaining squared-frequency polynomial is F_N(u)=D^2u^3-24D(4N+17)u^2+1152(N+4)Du -1024(4N^2-9). Its signs at u = 0,16,24,32 are respectively negative, positive, negative, positive for every N > 3/2. Thus it has three distinct positive roots, one in each intervening interval. The antisymmetric block has the sole nonzero squared frequency 48(N+4)/D. Hence the equal-coupling circulating family has no exponential linear moment instability for every integer N ≥ 2, not just the displayed N = 2 example. Unequal couplings and nonlinear stability remain outside this result. 4. Significance and remaining boundary The scalar cross interaction does not eliminate all mixed circulation: self-consistent excited widths can restore the frequency degeneracy it needs. This gives an explicit cross-sector source candidate within the imported scalar model only as an angular expectation. No derivation connects it to the actual electron-orbit generator in the 6D demo; calling it an established cross-sector orbit source would be incorrect. It does not turn its scalar potential into a Dirac vector potential, derive a nonfactorizing transition, identify a spatial spinor fiber with a CP3 base coordinate, or select an observed particle index. The isolated fixed-circulation energy bound is not a proof of nonlinear stability for this coupled branch, since that mixed circulation is no longer separately conserved. Reproduction coupled_circulation_checks.py verifies four stationary parameter choices and both exact characteristic polynomials, including the symbolic equal-coupling family. coupled_circulation_bdg_checks.py independently constructs the two-field Bogoliubov matrix at N = 2 from actual Fock amplitudes and quadratic interaction columns. The nonlinear coupling is entirely captured by nuclear shells 0,2 and electron shells 0,2,4, giving 155 complex amplitudes and a 310-dimensional doubled matrix. Its nonzero frequencies agree with the exact moment polynomials; omitted shell directions have the free self-adjoint oscillator evolution. Tiny near-zero imaginary roundoff is not interpreted as an instability or as proof that the zero eigenspace is diagonalizable. All couplings, embedding, field types, and normalization assumptions are the ones stated above; no observed constants were fitted. Related Spin-orbit source audit — conditional derivative vertex needed before orbital current becomes a spin source. Selecting a normalized unobserved/normal spinor |\chi\rangle\in\mathbf2_H gives the most direct contraction \boxed{ B_\chi=I_O\otimes\langle\chi|. } Consequently \boxed{ B_\chi^\dagger B_\chi =I_O\otimes|\chi\rangle\langle\chi|. } This is a rank-two product projector. A transition involving a background/nuclear doublet can therefore pass through either \mathbf2\otimes\mathbf1\to\mathbf2 or \mathbf2\otimes\mathbf3\to\mathbf2. Then \boxed{ E_L=A_OJ_2A_H^T. } If x_O\not\parallel p_O and x_H\not\parallel p_H, both A_O and A_H have column rank two and J_2 is invertible. It is already fixed, up to sign, by the oriented normals of the two rank-two planes. 99.2 Rank-two 3\times3 tensors have a unique SO(3) Procrustes maximizer Let a real rank-two tensor have singular-value decomposition E=U \begin{pmatrix} \sigma_1&0&0\\ 0&\sigma_2&0\\ 0&0&0 \end{pmatrix} V^T, \qquad \sigma_1,\sigma_2>0. Because the third singular vectors correspond to zero singular value, their signs may be chosen so that U,V\in SO(3). Consider the orientation-preserving Procrustes problem \max_{Q\in SO(3)}\operatorname{tr}(Q^TE). Write Q=URV^T, \qquad R\in SO(3). Then \operatorname{tr}(Q^TE) = \sigma_1R_{11}+\sigma_2R_{22}. Since every diagonal entry of an orthogonal matrix is at most one, \operatorname{tr}(Q^TE) \le \sigma_1+\sigma_2. Equality requires R_{11}=R_{22}=1. Orthogonality then forces the first two rows and columns to be the first two coordinate basis vectors, and the condition \det R=1 forces R_{33}=1. Hence R=I_3 is the unique maximizer. Therefore \boxed{ Q_E=UV^T } is a uniquely selected element of SO(3) even though \det E=0. So full matrix rank is not required for full orientation selection in three dimensions. 99.3 Canonical exact example For E= \begin{pmatrix} 0&a&0\\ -b&0&0\\ 0&0&0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad a,b>0, one has E=Q_0 \operatorname{diag}(b,a,0), with \boxed{ Q_0= \begin{pmatrix} 0&1&0\\ -1&0&0\\ 0&0&1 \end{pmatrix} \in SO(3). } For any Q=Q_0R, \qquad R\in SO(3), the trace objective is \operatorname{tr}(Q^TE) =bR_{11}+aR_{22} \le a+b, with equality only for R=I. Then only one or zero independent directions are correlated and a continuous frame ambiguity returns. Thus the physical distinction is not \text{rank three versus rank two}, but \boxed{ \text{two independent oriented directions versus fewer than two}. } This matches ordinary three-dimensional frame geometry: two noncollinear axes determine the third by the right-hand rule. 99.7 Revised bottleneck The source audit of Section 98 remains valid: the current non-note V2 corpus does not yet insert an orbital/scattering bifundamental into the electron--nucleus kernel. title: CP5 tangent splitting obstruction
summary: The complex tangent bundle of CP5 admits no global rank-three plus rank-two splitting, even without imposing determinant one.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The complex tangent bundle of CP5 admits no global rank-three plus rank-two splitting, even without imposing determinant one. Why this matters Gauge selection §15 already excludes determinant-one tangent holonomy because c1(T CP5)=6H. The obstruction is stronger: a global complex 3+2 tangent splitting itself is impossible. Keeping the determinant connection does not cure that failure. 1. Exhaust the possible Chern factors Let E=T^(1,0) CP5. The Euler sequence gives c(E)=1+6H+15H^2+20H^3+15H^4+6H^5, \qquad H^*(\mathbb{CP}^5;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[H]/(H^6). Suppose E=A_3 direct-sum B_2. The Whitney product formula says c(E)=c(A)c(B). Since both factors have degree at most their ranks, their product has degree at most five. Equality modulo H^6 is therefore an exact polynomial equality. The top coefficient is nonzero, so the degrees must be exactly three and two. Over the rationals the polynomial factors as c(E)=(1+2H)(1+H+H^2)(1+3H+3H^2). The two quadratics are irreducible (discriminant -3), and the linear factor occurs only once. Normalizing constant terms to one, the only possible rank-two Chern factors are c(B)=1+H+H^2\quad\hbox{or}\quad c(B)=1+3H+3H^2. 2. Both factors fail a necessary bundle condition Restrict B to a linear CP3 inside CP5. A complex rank-two bundle on CP3 with c1=aH and c2=bH^2 must satisfy ab=0 modulo 2. This is the classical Atiyah–Rees/Schwarzenberger condition; see Opie, Theorem 1.2 and Remark 1.3. The two candidates have (a,b)=(1,1) and (3,3), hence ab odd in both cases. Neither is the Chern class of such a bundle. The supposed splitting cannot exist. An independent check uses K(CP3)=Z[t]/(t^4), t=[O(1)]-1, and ch(t)=exp(H)-1. The rank-two candidate characters are \operatorname{ch}(B)=2+aH+\frac{a^2-2b}{2}H^2 +\frac{a^3-3ab}{6}H^3. Their coefficients in the integral K-theory basis (1,t,t^2,t^3) would be (2,1,-1,1/2) and (2,3,0,-1/2), respectively. Half-integral final coefficients are impossible. The K-theory basis is established in Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory, §2.2. 3. Precise consequence for V2 No unitary connection on T^(1,0) CP5 can have its full holonomy contained in a conjugate U(3) times U(2): such a reduction would produce the excluded rank-three and rank-two subbundles. This conclusion does not assume the connection is Levi–Civita, holomorphic, or determinant one. Tensoring the tangent bundle by a line bundle cannot help with the splitting: a split of E tensor L would untwist to a split of E. Separately its first Chern class would be (6+5k)H for L=O(k), never zero for integer k. The pointwise exterior-algebra branching, charge normalization, and local stabilizer calculations remain valid. What fails is promoting that local split to the literal global tangent bundle. An auxiliary gauge bundle, a different effective carrier, or a properly specified non-global construction is required. This theorem does not forbid the Standard Model group on CP5 or every possible V2 gauge completion. Two different notions of encounter A crucial distinction is required. 2.1 Full-depth direct encounter For two particles of the same depth d, let their relative coordinate be \Delta X_d\in Q_d. A genuinely local same-depth interaction samples the full relative geometry. In a locally Euclidean model, R_d^2=\sum_{i=1}^d(\Delta x_i)^2. If the interaction is central, V=V(R_d), then F_i=-\frac{dV}{dR_d}\frac{\Delta x_i}{R_d}. Thus all nonzero components of the one separation vector evolve together. The uncontrolled coordinates are not automatically independent random variables. The correct probabilistic object for an observer resolving only a subspace is therefore P(\Delta X_\perp\mid\Delta X_{\rm obs}), not the unconditional P(\Delta X_\perp). A correlation law such as \mathbb E\!\left(|\Delta X_\perp|^2\mid r\right) =\alpha r^2 would imply \mathbb E(R_d^2\mid r)=(1+\alpha)r^2, so full coincidence follows as the visible separation r\to0. 2.2 Interaction through a lower-depth carrier The current V2 cross-depth theorem gives a different mechanism. Let two matter sectors have depths b and c, and suppose an interaction carrier or shared interaction base has depth a\leq\min(b,c). Push both higher-depth currents to the common base: \bar J_{b\to a}=(\pi_{ba})_*J_b, \qquad \bar J_{c\to a}=(\pi_{ca})_*J_c. Then a carrier-mediated interaction can have the form \boxed{ I^{(a)}_{bc} = \int_{Q_a} \left\langle \bar J_{b\to a}(x), K_a\bar J_{c\to a}(x) \right\rangle \,d\mu_a(x). } For normalized nonnegative densities, complete marginalization preserves total weight: \int_{Q_a}\bar\rho_{b\to a}=1, \qquad \int_{Q_a}\bar\rho_{c\to a}=1. Therefore the b-a and c-a extra coordinates do not generate a naive coincidence penalty of the form (a/L)^{(b-a)+(c-a)}. They have already been integrated out of the interaction channel. summary: Action and kinetic-normalization tests locate the unresolved fixed-reference bridge.

This note records the action-level attempt to derive or falsify the V2 common-anchor law as it proceeds. 1. Target The relation under test is \frac{(M_d^\star)^2}{g_{dd}}=\frac{m_e^2}{g_{66}}, or, in frequency language, \frac{\omega_d^\star}{\omega_e}=\sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}}. The task is to determine whether this follows from the written V2 projected dynamics rather than being an additional scale ansatz. 2. First source-level result The self-contact module explicitly starts from a sector-diagonal scalar interaction \mathcal L_{\rm sc}=-\frac{\kappa_d}{2}J_d^2 and derives the projected scalar coefficient \mu_d=\kappa_dR_dB_d. The finite-band contact theorem then gives M_{n,d}=\mu_dS(n,d). Therefore the written operator ordering is \boxed{\mu_d\;\longrightarrow\;\mu_dS(n,d)}. The sector coefficient is formed first; the simplex/contact eigenvalue multiplies it afterward. Section 9.1 of the self-contact module introduces the common-anchor equation separately as a projected fixed-point condition and explicitly states that the master equation of motion must supply that equation. No equation in the inspected self-contact passage identifies \kappa_dR_dB_d with g_{dd} or \sqrt{g_{dd}}. 3. The higher-dimensional-polarization module writes a schematic current/gauge interaction S_{\rm int}=g_{ab}\int_{Q_a}\langle A_a,(\pi_{ba})_*J_b\rangle. These establish incidence, reciprocity, representation filtering, and the existence of coupling coefficients. In the inspected passages they do not identify the scalar self-contact coefficient \kappa_d, the projected scalar coefficient \mu_d, or an occupied reference frequency with g_{dd} or \sqrt{g_{dd}}. The polarization source in fact says that a nonzero invariant vertex leaves its coupling coefficient to the projected dynamics. 4. Exact placement test for the rank-one proposal Let v_d=\sqrt{g_{dd}},\qquad G=vv^T, and for the proposed depth-3, depth-4, and electron reference bands define D_\star=\operatorname{diag}(1,15,18564). If the rank-one response acts on primitive pre-contact coefficients, \sigma=GJ=v(v^TJ), then the written contact projection gives M^\star=D_\star\sigma=(D_\star v)(v^TJ). Hence \boxed{ \frac{M_d^\star}{M_6^\star} =\frac{D_d^\star\sqrt{g_{dd}}}{D_6^\star\sqrt{g_{66}}} }. This is Case B, not the desired common-anchor law. If instead a deeper master equation acts directly on the already-projected occupied reference coefficients, M^\star=vC, then \boxed{ \frac{M_d^\star}{M_6^\star}=\sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}} }. This is Case A. The algebraic way to begin before contact multiplication and still end in Case A is to use \widetilde G=D_\star^{-1}vv^TD_\star^{-1}, so that D_\star\widetilde GJ lies along v. But this changes the primitive diagonal couplings to \widetilde g_{dd}=\frac{g_{dd}}{(D_d^\star)^2}. That is not a harmless relabeling of the quoted V2 couplings unless an independent projection or kinetic-normalization theorem derives exactly this weighting. 5. Interim verdict The naive rank-one source-to-self-energy mechanism does not derive the common-anchor law when attached directly to the scalar coefficient already written in V2. With the explicit self-contact ordering it produces Case B. Case A remains possible only if the deeper projected master dynamics supplies additional structure, for example: a rank-one equation acting directly on occupied reference frequencies; an independently derived two-sided reference-count weighting before contact projection; sector-dependent projected overlap or kinetic factors that cancel the reference counts exactly; or a nonlinear fixed-point equation in which the reference-band factors enter before the final ratio is formed. None of those mechanisms has yet been found in the inspected source passages. The identity g_{34}^2=g_{33}g_{44} is therefore insufficient by itself. It establishes rank one for a coupling-coefficient matrix, but does not determine the operator layer on which that matrix acts. Since D_\star v is not proportional to v, the simplex projection and the proposed rank-one image do not commute in the way required by the anchor law. The remaining problem is an operator-ordering and normalization problem, not an unknown-amplitude problem. 6. Next proof obligation Trace the actual derivation and mathematical role of g_{33}=8\sqrt7,\qquad g_{44}=12/\sqrt7,\qquad g_{34}=4\sqrt6,\qquad g_{66}=1/4. For each value, determine whether it is defined as a scalar self-interaction coefficient, a polarization/gauge normalization, a stiffness, a kernel eigenvalue, or another object. Only then can the use of these same numbers in the scalar reference-frequency fixed-point equation be classified as derived, merely compatible, or category-invalid. No V1 material is used as evidence here. 7. Historical V2 action supplies a real candidate mechanism - but not yet a current-V2 derivation The git history contains an earlier V2, not V1, formulation from August 28, 2026. It is useful provenance because it shows what the common-anchor statement was intended to mean before the present projective-contact modules were written. That historical V2 wrote one quartic master interaction S_{\rm int} =\frac12\sum_{d,e}g_{de} \int K_{de}(\xi_d,\xi_e)\,\rho_d\rho_e, with g_{de}=v_dv_e, \qquad g_{dd}=v_d^2. For the displayed kernel, K_{de}=(\xi_d\cdot\xi_e)^2. The same historical text then states the lightest-mode fixed point \frac{(M_d^\star)^2}{g_{dd}} =\frac{m_e^2}{g_{66}}, which is exactly the present common-anchor condition. This matters because the rank-one-response idea was not invented during the present audit: an earlier V2 master action already contained a rank-one coupling matrix and explicitly described one collective interaction channel. 7.1 Exact variation of the historical rank-one action Let \rho_d=\bar\Psi P_d\Psi. For a symmetric kernel and symmetric coupling matrix, variation of the quadratic density functional with respect to \rho_d gives \Sigma_d =\sum_e g_{de}K_{de}\rho_e. Using g_{de}=v_dv_e, \boxed{ \Sigma_d =v_d\sum_e v_eK_{de}\rho_e. } This is an important refinement of the simpler toy calculation \Sigma=v(v^TJ). Rank one of the coefficient matrix alone does not yet imply \Sigma_d=v_dC with one sector-independent scalar C, because the geometric kernel still carries the external sector label d through K_{de}. The required additional condition is \boxed{ \sum_e v_eK_{de}\rho_e=C \quad\text{independent of }d } on the relevant fixed-point branch, or an equivalent projector/normalization theorem that reduces the full kernel to a common scalar functional. The historical prose asserts precisely such a common condensate, but the displayed action by itself does not prove that the K_{de} dependence collapses this way. 7.2 Why this still does not automatically solve the present projective-contact problem The historical V2 and current V2 place the spectral count at different conceptual stages. The current self-contact theorem derives M_d^\star=D_d^\star\mu_d, where \mu_d is the sector-normalized scalar contact coefficient before multiplication by the occupied-band dimension. Therefore, if the historical rank-one response \Sigma_d is identified with the current primitive coefficient \mu_d, then M_d^\star =D_d^\star v_dC, which is Case B: \frac{M_d^\star}{M_6^\star} =\frac{D_d^\star v_d}{D_6^\star v_6}. To recover Case A in the current architecture, one must establish one of two precise identifications: post-projection response: the historical \Sigma_d corresponds directly to the occupied reference eigenvalue M_d^\star, not to \mu_d; or count-compensated primitive response: projection of the historical kernel produces \mu_d\propto\frac{v_d}{D_d^\star}, so that the subsequent contact multiplier restores M_d^\star\propto v_d. The historical source does not perform the present finite-band projective-contact calculation, so it cannot decide between these two identifications. 7.3 A second incompatibility that must be resolved The historical V2 derives a self-consistent harmonic stiffness \lambda_d=\left(\frac{g_{dd}}2\right)^{2/3} from the quartic kernel, and then separately states that the physical mass spectrum is m(n,d)=m_{{\rm scale},d}S(n,d). But the ordinary isotropic harmonic-oscillator eigenvalues scale linearly with excitation number and with \sqrt{\lambda_d}; their degeneracy count is S(n,d) only after cumulative counting. The historical source does not derive why the eigenfrequency itself equals the cumulative degeneracy rather than the usual oscillator eigenvalue. The current projective-contact theorem was written precisely to supply a genuine operator whose occupied eigenvalue is S(n,d). Consequently, importing the historical harmonic-well fixed point wholesale would mix two distinct spectral mechanisms. 7.4 Result of the historical-source test Survives as provenance and a candidate mechanism: V2 originally intended g_{de} to be one rank-one quartic self-interaction matrix; V2 originally intended the electron-relative scale law to be a kernel-vacuum fixed point; the square-root coupling ratios therefore have a coherent action-level motivation, not merely a numerical coincidence. Does not yet survive as a derivation in the current V2 operator architecture: rank one of g_{de} does not by itself remove the sector dependence of the geometric kernel K_{de}; the historical action does not derive the inverse reference-count factor required if its response is pre-contact; the historical harmonic-well spectrum and the current projective-contact spectrum are not the same operator construction. The common anchor is therefore better motivated than the current files alone made visible, but still unproved in present V2. 8. Sharpened next calculation The next decisive calculation is now concrete. Project the historical-style rank-one master kernel through the current finite-band projectors and ask whether its occupied-line matrix element has the form \langle z_d;N_d|P_d\mathcal K_\infty P_d|z_d;N_d\rangle =C\sqrt{g_{dd}} or =C\sqrt{g_{dd}}\,D_d^\star, or instead acquires a compensating factor 1/D_d^\star before the contact eigenvalue is applied. Equivalently, define the projected source functional F_d[\rho] =\sum_e v_e\,\langle z_d;N_d|P_dK_{de}[\rho_e]P_d|z_d;N_d\rangle. Case A requires D_d^\star F_d[\rho] \propto \text{constant in }d, when the primitive scalar coefficient is used, whereas a direct post-projection formulation requires simply F_d[\rho]\propto\text{constant in }d. This is now the exact normalization theorem to prove or falsify. 9. Fixed reference normalization is compatible with band blindness The current self-contact theorem states that, for the ordinary family law, M_{n,d}=\mu_dS(n,d), with all explicit band dependence carried by the reproducing-kernel diagonal S(n,d). Its action-level domain explicitly requires the scalar contact strength \mu_d to be band-blind. This sharpens the Case A/Case B fork. Suppose the historical rank-one master response is attached to the current primitive scalar coefficient: \mu_d=v_dC, \qquad v_d=\sqrt{g_{dd}}. Then the present contact theorem gives M_d^\star=D_d^\star v_dC, and therefore Case B. The only primitive-level algebraic rescue previously identified was \mu_d\propto\frac{v_d}{D_d^\star}. Here D_d^\star is fixed once per sector. Dependence on that fixed reference does not imply dependence on the varying occupied band n or N=n-1. Thus \mu_d=Cv_d/D_d^\star is band-blind and gives M_{n,d}=Cv_dD_{n,d}/D_d^\star, with M_d^\star=Cv_d. The earlier claim that band blindness alone excludes this normalization is withdrawn. Replacing D_d^\star by the running D_{n,d} would violate band blindness, but that is a different prescription. Therefore: \boxed{ \mu_d=Cv_d\text{ forces Case B; fixed }\mu_d=Cv_d/D_d^\star\text{ gives Case A.} } A fixed inverse-reference normalization changes the primitive-response identification, not the band-blind contact theorem. Its physical origin remains unproved; it cannot be silently inserted as a result of the historical kernel. This rules out only the simultaneous unweighted primitive response \mu_d=Cv_d and the desired reference ratios with unequal reference counts. Case A can follow from a post-contact / occupied-reference fixed point, or from a derived fixed sector normalization at the primitive layer. Neither route has been derived from the current master action. 10. Current V2 explicitly records the missing coordinate-kernel to phase-ray bridge Section 8.6 of the present self-contact module distinguishes two operators: P_{N,d}|q|^2P_{N,d} from the coordinate harmonic kernel, and D_N|z;N\rangle\langle z;N| from phase-ray point contact. It then states that their relation still requires either: a master interaction written locally on the homogenized phase-ray bundle; or a derivation showing that the coordinate-space nonlinear kernel transforms into occupied-ray contact after oscillator and sector projection. This is exactly the missing bridge between the historical V2 master kernel (\xi_d\cdot\xi_e)^2 and the present projective-contact mass operator. So the source audit now yields a stronger documentary conclusion: \boxed{ \text{the current V2 source itself identifies the historical-to-current operator bridge as unfinished.} } Consequently, the historical statement that the kernel vacuum supplies the common anchor cannot presently be imported as a completed derivation. It points to the right location in the dynamics, but the required projection theorem has not yet been written. 11. Revised status after the bridge audit Established in current V2: occupied phase-ray point contact gives the exact simplex eigenvalue D_N=S(n,d); the ordinary family law has a band-blind primitive coefficient \mu_d; therefore a primitive response proportional to \sqrt{g_{dd}} produces Case B. Established as historical V2 provenance: an earlier V2 master action used a rank-one coupling matrix g_{de}=v_dv_e; it intended one collective self-interaction channel; it stated the electron-relative common-anchor law as a kernel-vacuum fixed point. Still missing: the projection of that coordinate-space rank-one kernel into the current occupied phase-ray scalar-contact operator; a proof that the resulting complete occupied reference eigenvalue, rather than the primitive coefficient, lies along v_d; or any other current-V2 equation that yields M_d^\star\propto\sqrt{g_{dd}} with a derived fixed sector normalization or occupied-reference fixed point. The common-anchor law is not disproved. The unweighted primitive identification is excluded; a fixed inverse-reference normalization remains algebraically allowed but physically underived. 12. Kinetic-normalization audit: no present rescue of the primitive rank-one anchor The remaining obvious place for a compensating factor was canonical or kinetic normalization. The current V2 mass module does not provide one. Its operator ordering is explicit: the spatial Dirac/Laplace operator constructs the mode eigenspace; the localized contact operator maps the rank of that eigenspace to the rest-energy eigenvalue; the sector coefficient is \mu_d=\kappa_dR_dB_d, and is independent of the band label under the ordinary mass theorem. No reference-band wavefunction renormalization or kinetic factor proportional to \frac1{D_d^\star} appears in that derivation. A separate gauge/polarization module does say that propagation laws and kinetic normalizations of the projected gauge connection remain to be obtained from the master action. But that statement concerns projected connection components and cross-sector propagation; no current source identifies such a normalization with the scalar rest-energy contact coefficient, and no formula supplies the reference-band dependence required here. The cross-depth contact theorem also preserves complete normalized marginal weight: \int \bar\rho_{b\to a}=1. Thus full marginalization does not furnish an inverse simplex factor either. Combining these facts gives the following present-V2 no-go statement. 12.1 Primitive-rank-one incompatibility theorem Assume simultaneously: the ordinary current V2 contact law M_{n,d}=\mu_dD_{n,d}, \qquad D_{n,d}=S(n,d); band blindness of the primitive scalar contact coefficient \mu_d; normalized cross-depth marginalization with no band-dependent loss of weight; identification of the historical rank-one response with that primitive coefficient, \mu_d=C\sqrt{g_{dd}} for one sector-independent C. Then for any chosen reference bands, \boxed{ \frac{M_d^\star}{M_6^\star} = \frac{D_d^\star}{D_6^\star} \sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}} } and not \sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}} unless accidentally D_d^\star=D_6^\star. For the adopted references, D_3^\star=S(1,3)=1, \qquad D_4^\star=S(3,4)=15, \qquad D_6^\star=S(13,6)=18564, so the accidental-equality condition fails drastically. Therefore the four assumptions above are mutually incompatible with the common-anchor law. At least one must change. Since assumptions 1--3 are explicit parts of the current V2 contact construction, the natural conclusion is: \boxed{ \text{the desired anchor is incompatible with the unweighted identification }\mu_d=Cv_d. } It can instead act on the complete occupied reference eigenvalues, or arise from a derived fixed sector weighting such as \mu_d=Cv_d/D_d^\star. The latter preserves assumptions 1--3 but replaces assumption 4; it is not excluded merely because it acts at the primitive layer. 12.2 Numerical size of the contradiction The difference is not perturbative. The desired Case A factors relative to the electron reference are \sqrt{g_{33}/g_{66}}\approx 9.2013065, \qquad \sqrt{g_{44}/g_{66}}\approx 4.2593773. A primitive rank-one response followed by the present contact theorem instead gives \frac{1}{18564}\sqrt{g_{33}/g_{66}} \approx 4.9565\times10^{-4}, and \frac{15}{18564}\sqrt{g_{44}/g_{66}} \approx 3.4416\times10^{-3}. These differ from the required reference-frequency ratios by factors exactly equal to the missing count ratios. This cannot be repaired by unit conventions. 13. Status of the common-anchor attack The first attempted action-level derivation has therefore failed in a precise way. It did not fail because rank-one coupling is useless. Historical V2 shows why rank one is a serious clue. It failed because the current exact simplex theorem fixes where the count enters, and a primitive rank-one response then places that count on the wrong side of the proposed fixed point. The surviving proof target is now narrower: Derive a fixed-point equation for the complete occupied reference eigenvalue M_d^\star, or derive the fixed sector normalization of the primitive coefficient (for example 1/D_d^\star) from the master projection. Any future derivation that merely writes \mu_d\propto\sqrt{g_{dd}} has already been ruled out for the present V2 mass operator. title: Rank-one common anchor
summary: A conditional source-cancellation mechanism fixes output ratios but not their physical identification.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A conditional source-cancellation mechanism fixes output ratios but not their physical identification. NOT A PHYSICS MODULE OR COMPLETED SCALE DERIVATION. The source-cancellation calculation below is exact for a specified rank-one response. Its identification with the actual V2 projected reference-frequency dynamics remains unproved. 1. The constructive possibility The earlier work treated a coupling matrix as though it had to act directly on wave-mode coefficients, then diagonalized it or took its square root. A different role is possible: the matrix can map scalar source currents to scalar Dirac self-energies. In that role, its rank-one image fixes ratios of output coefficients without determining the source magnitudes. This provides a concrete sufficient mechanism for the square-root coupling ratios. It does not require an oscillator frequency-squared matrix, and it does not require an amplitude measurement. The remaining physical identification is substantial and is kept explicit below. 2. Exact source elimination Consider a finite, compatibly normalized common source space. The test interaction is \mathcal L_{\rm int}=-\frac12\mathbf J^TG\mathbf J, \qquad G=vv^T, \qquad v_d=\sqrt{g_{dd}}>0. This is an algebraic candidate after choosing common units and integration conventions. Any common dimensional prefactor is suppressed here and can be absorbed in the common response scalar. A physical cross-depth action must establish the compatible measures and maps; the displayed finite expression does not do that automatically. Writing U=(1/2)\mathbf J^TG\mathbf J, its scalar self-energy coefficients are \Sigma_d=\frac{\partial U}{\partial J_d} =\sum_eG_{de}J_e =v_dC, \qquad C=\sum_ev_eJ_e. For arbitrary symbolic source entries, the row relations give \boxed{v_6\Sigma_d-v_d\Sigma_6=0.} On a nonzero electron-reference branch, \boxed{\frac{\Sigma_d}{\Sigma_6}=\frac{v_d}{v_6} =\sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}}.} No J_d has been assigned a measured value, fitted, or solved for. The source vector and any common multiplier cancel. This is elimination of an unneeded source, not an amplitude-domain reconstruction. The positive choice of v specifies the adopted sign convention. Relating these scalar coefficients to positive rest frequencies still requires the appropriate common mass-sign branch. A zero response cannot serve as the electron anchor. 3. Coefficient ratios are not automatically pole ratios The exact result above concerns \Sigma_d. To conclude \frac{\omega_d^\star}{\omega_e}=\sqrt{\frac{g_{dd}}{g_{66}}}, one must establish that \Sigma_d is the relevant complete occupied scalar rest-frequency coefficient after canonical kinetic normalization and the prescribed mode projection. Different kinetic factors, additional mass terms, noncommuting operator pieces, spatially varying backgrounds, or frequency-dependent self-energies can prevent this coefficient ratio from being the ratio of physical poles. A common local scalar function is not automatically a common constant in every sector's eigenvalue problem. The self-contact source, Section 9.1, currently introduces the common-anchor relation conditionally and says the master equation must supply it. The present calculation offers a sufficient response mechanism to test against that obligation. It does not change that documentary status into a completed theorem. 4. The decisive reference-band versus primitive-unit test Use the specified references (n_3^\star,n_4^\star,n_6^\star)=(1,3,13), whose contact multipliers are (D_3^\star,D_4^\star,D_6^\star)=(1,15,18564). The ordinary contact law gives \omega_d^\star=D_d^\star\varpi_d. There are two inequivalent ways to place the rank-one response relative to this multiplication. Case A: response already gives the occupied reference frequencies If \Sigma_d=Cv_d already denotes \omega_d^\star, then \frac{\omega_d^\star}{\omega_e}=\frac{v_d}{v_6}, \qquad \boxed{\frac{\varpi_d}{\omega_e} =\frac{v_d}{D_d^\star v_6}.} For the adopted g_{33}=8\sqrt7, g_{44}=12/\sqrt7, g_{66}=1/4, this gives: Depth Occupied reference frequency divided by \omega_e Primitive unit \varpi_d/\omega_e 3 9.201306535164823 9.201306535164823 4 4.259377267212064 0.28395848448080424 6 1 1/18564\approx0.0000538677009265245 This reproduces the proposed anchor architecture, conditional on the Case A identification. The calculation does not independently derive the adopted coupling values. Case B: response gives the coefficient before contact multiplication If instead \varpi_d=Cv_d is the pre-contact unit, the occupied reference frequencies obey \boxed{\frac{\omega_d^\star}{\omega_e} =\frac{D_d^\star v_d}{D_6^\star v_6}.} The same numerical couplings now give: Depth Occupied reference frequency divided by \omega_e 3 0.0004956532285695337 4 0.0034416429114512473 6 1 The discrepancy is not a rounding error or a choice of MeV units. Case A divided by Case B is exactly 18564 at depth three and 18564/15 at depth four. The response and the simplex multiplier cannot be composed in an unspecified order. This distinction is directly motivated by self-contact Sections 6.4 and 9: the source first defines the projected coefficient \mu_d, then multiplies it by S(n,d). Its separate common-anchor statement concerns M_d^\star=\mu_dS(n_d^\star,d). A rank-one law for the former is not automatically a rank-one law for the latter with the same vector. 5. What two-sided reference-count weighting would do Let D_\star=\operatorname{diag}(1,15,18564). A symmetric primitive response matrix \widetilde G=D_\star^{-1}GD_\star^{-1} =\widetilde v\widetilde v^T, \qquad \widetilde v=D_\star^{-1}v, has diagonal entries \boxed{\widetilde g_{dd}=g_{dd}/(D_d^\star)^2.} If this were the primitive response, multiplying its outputs by D_d^\star would give a vector proportional to v, recovering the Case A reference ratios. This is a correct algebraic construction and retains rank one. It is not a derived V2 normalization. The primitive matrix is no longer the original G with the original diagonal entries. Dividing only one side would also change the action's symmetric response interpretation. Calling the two-sided transformation a harmless field redefinition would require transforming the kinetic form, currents, measures, and the meaning of the quoted couplings consistently. No such projection/kinetic-normalization theorem was established in the inspected passages. The reference counts must not be inserted solely because they recover the desired numbers. 6. Why cross-depth geometry is still an obstruction to automatic factorization The reciprocity source, Section 5, writes the two variations of the same cross-depth interaction as a lower-depth response to the higher-depth marginal and a higher-depth response to the lower-depth field extended across the additional fibre. The polarization-coupling source, Section 6, separately assigns pushforward to contact, invariant brackets to polarization selection, and the coupling coefficient and field equations to dynamics. These are valuable geometric and variational structures. They do not automatically make every sector's full response proportional to the same source functional after projection. Even when the numerical coefficients factor as g_{de}=v_dv_e, the full operator can contain sector-dependent kernels, fibre maps, spinor contractions, and kinetic normalizations. Factorization of the coefficient matrix is not yet factorization of all those maps together. The common-source cancellation is therefore sufficient when the projected response has the proved finite form. Checking that premise in the actual source geometry is indispensable. The bounded searches returned in this session did not establish an independent full projected reference-response action; that search result is not a universal absence theorem. 7. Proof obligations before promoting the mechanism The immediate task is an identification calculation, not a source-amplitude solve. It must show that the projected scalar interaction has the needed common response after the cross-depth measures and kernels are included; track every D_d^\star through projection and variation; put the kinetic term into the same normalization used for the frequency extraction; and connect the resulting scalar coefficient to the complete reference pole on the appropriate branch. If those steps establish Case A, the reference ratios follow without determining C. If the action instead establishes Case B, the different ratios are a real consequence of that prescription and must not be hidden by relabeling \Sigma_d. If additional kernels destroy the common response, their frequency effects have to be calculated rather than silently absorbed into a universal source. Closing the reference law would still not solve the baryon problem by itself. A composite operator, its color-singlet constraint, and any induced frequency-dependent interactions remain to be derived. The signed color-pair coefficient and exact block reduction in the review note are tools for that next stage, not missing mass factors that can simply be multiplied together. 8. Reproducible status The regression script differentiates the symbolic quadratic interaction, proves the row annihilator identities for arbitrary sources, calculates both reference prescriptions, and verifies the two-sided count weighting. These tests were checked independently in the session and are packaged for repetition. Established: a rank-one scalar response can give the desired square-root coefficient ratios with complete cancellation of unmeasured source magnitudes. Not established: that the written V2 master action realizes this response for canonically normalized occupied reference frequencies, that the reference-count weighting is dynamically selected, that the self-consistent branch exists and is stable, or that a nucleon pole has been predicted. This is the principal constructive lead from the latest calculations. Its conditional status is part of the finding, not a reason to discard it or to claim more than has been shown. Related Research status — current proof boundaries and correction guidance.

Summary: A six-coordinate Kepler model with reciprocal source angular momentum has exact signed-rose trajectories, including repelling two-electron solutions, but the pair is unstable and magnetic quadratic completion changes the motion. What is restored, and what is a new premise The visualization history contains Coulomb binding plus a prescribed precession construction, not a single implemented force-law integration joining them. The old c50ef57 prose used a visible 1/r potential plus a separate sector Hamiltonian; it did not derive the subsequent frequency lock. This test supplies actual Cartesian positions and canonical momenta q_i,p_i in R6, without appending another independent six-dimensional electron position. Flat R6 is a mechanical diagnostic geometry, not a derived replacement for the candidate physical CP3 metric. Use the explicitly chosen Kepler kernel -k/|q| as a control. It is not silently identified with the Green function of an unrestricted six-dimensional field, nor with the unresolved interaction of a flat nucleus and a depth-six electron. A radial potential -k/r^a has circular effective-potential curvature a k (2-a)/r^(a+2). Thus a=1 has stable radial circular motion, whereas the unrestricted six-dimensional inverse-fourth-power potential does not in this flat point-particle model. Kernel and geometry selection remain explicit. The responding source is now a real skew 6 by 6 angular-momentum matrix C on a fixed coadjoint orbit. This is a new source phase-space premise, motivated by angular-momentum-bearing response, not a relabeling of the previous singlet-plus-gapped-amplitude source. No equivalence between the two source models or identification with a measured nuclear current is claimed. In particular C=0 remains zero: this source can reorient a prepared angular momentum but cannot induce its magnitude from an initially zero source. The petal preparations require nonzero source angular momentum as input. One autonomous Hamiltonian Define L=sum_i(q_i p_i^T-p_i q_i^T), pairing <A,B>=-tr(AB)/2, and H_0=\sum_i\left(\frac{p_i^2}{2m}-\frac{k}{|q_i|}\right) +\sum_{i<j}\frac{\gamma}{|q_i-q_j|},\qquad H=H_0+\lambda\langle C,L\rangle+\frac{\langle C,C\rangle}{2I}. Use canonical brackets for q,p and the angular-momentum Lie-Poisson bracket for C. The equations are \dot q_i=p_i/m-\lambda Cq_i,\qquad \dot p_i=F_i(q)-\lambda Cp_i,\qquad \dot C=\lambda[C,L]. Here F is the full attraction-plus-pair-repulsion force from H0. The source energy is a Casimir and adds no orientation torque. The source is not frozen: C and L generally precess, with dot L=-dot C. Total J=C+L, energy, the spectrum of C, and the spectrum of total orbital L are conserved. The source and orbit exchange angular momentum. There are no prescribed time-dependent fields in these equations. They describe classical actual trajectories. The two-electron version includes direct repulsion, but is not an antisymmetric quantum many-body state and does not replace the separate Pauli-compatible carrier tests. The canonical p is not m dot q when the angular coupling is present. Exact reduction to Coulomb motion plus reciprocal precession Let Q_i(t),P_i(t) solve the uncoupled rotationally invariant H0 problem, with conserved total L0 and the same initial Cartesian data. Then R(t)=e^{-\lambda Jt}e^{\lambda L_0t},\qquad q_i(t)=R(t)Q_i(t),\quad p_i(t)=R(t)P_i(t), \qquad C(t)=e^{-\lambda Jt}C_0e^{\lambda Jt} solve the coupled equations. Indeed dot R R^T=-lambda C(t), and the central and pair forces are rotation-covariant. This is an exact autonomous backreaction solution, not an imposed precession schedule. It also shows a limitation: this interaction only rotates the ordinary Coulomb configuration; it does not repair its radial or pair instabilities. Prepared signed-rose family Set radius and mass to one, k=1, lambda=0.2. For N=1 choose q=e1,p=ell e2 with ell=1. For N=2 take an antipodal pair with opposite momenta and gamma=0.4. Both remain separated by distance two, and their canonical circular momenta obey ell=sqrt(k-gamma/4)=sqrt(0.9). In either case define beta=ell/m-N lambda ell. Choose conserved total angular momentum J=j(E14+E25), where Eab is the unit skew generator; indices here run from one to six. These planes mix the first two visible axes with the fourth and fifth axes. Set lambda j=l beta and C0=J-L0. Then the first electron has the exact Cartesian path q(t)=(\cos(l\theta)\cos\theta,\ \cos(l\theta)\sin\theta,\ 0, \ \sin(l\theta)\cos\theta,\ \sin(l\theta)\sin\theta,\ 0), \qquad\theta=\beta t. Its full radius is one, so projected center crossings are not collisions with the nucleus. The source backreaction is nonzero. The second electron, when present, is its antipode. The computed clocks are beta=0.8 for N=1 and beta=0.569209978830 for N=2. Neither clock is imposed in the RHS. However, the integer ratio is selected by the initial conserved J, not dynamically attracted or quantized by this Hamiltonian. The source coadjoint spectrum changes when this preparation changes. No shell index or nuclear response spectrum has been derived from choosing integer l. Relation to the visualization The direct planar projection is the smooth signed rose w=cos(l theta) exp(i theta). For even integer l it has 2l distinct petals and the same planar image as the demo's |cos(l theta)| exp(i theta). Thus l=2 and l=4 yield actual four- and eight-petal projected paths. Their time parametrization differs from the modulus-folded demo at center crossings; the demo's additional height readout is not derived here. For odd l the signed curve instead has l distinct petals. In particular l=1 is an offset circle and l=3 is a three-petal rose, not the demo's two- and six-petal images. The absolute-value detector map cannot be silently substituted for this linear spatial projection. Matching selected even-l images is a concrete partial match, not reproduction of the entire display. Perturbation and two-electron instability Independent integration agrees with the exact prepared paths over a full clock turn for N=1,2 and l=1,2,3,4. For one electron, perturbed bound Kepler motion stays radially bounded because R is orthogonal. Small changes can alter the clock ratios and lose exact recurrence; the periodic petal path is not an attractor. For the l=2 test, changing one unobserved position component and one canonical tangential momentum component by 0.0001 or 0.001 gives the following maximum position deviations over two intended clock turns: N Perturbation Position deviation Radius deviation 1 0.0001 0.00488624 0.000400115 1 0.001 0.0487993 0.00401144 2 0.0001 4.48656 2.31761 2 0.001 4.92009 4.02402 The repelling pair has an analytic exponential instability, not merely a poor numerical trajectory. Its common-displacement mode has no first-order change in total orbital angular momentum and therefore is not stabilized by the reciprocal rigid rotation. In the ordinary co-rotating Coulomb frame its 4 by 4 Jacobian is [-W,I; diag(2k,-k),-W], with W=[[0,-Omega],[Omega,0]] and Omega²=k-gamma/4. In the tested units, \sigma^2=\frac{k-2\Omega^2+\sqrt{9k^2-8k\Omega^2}}2>0. The growth rate is 0.520404067288 in the test's time units, predicting amplification 64.2789706 over eight units. The checker computes this eigenvalue and tests its predicted growth in a full coupled integration from a 1e-7 perturbation. Consequently the exact two-electron family is an existence result, not a stable atomic model. Magnetic quadratic completion must not be omitted The linear angular coupling can stand as a phenomenological gyroscopic Hamiltonian, but calling it a complete magnetic minimal coupling requires the quadratic term. For a spatially uniform linear connection, the completed kinetic Hamiltonian is H_{\rm min}=\sum_i\frac{|p_i-m\lambda Cq_i|^2}{2m} -\sum_i\frac{k}{|q_i|}+\sum_{i<j}\frac{\gamma}{|q_i-q_j|} +\frac{\langle C,C\rangle}{2I}. This adds m lambda² sum |Cq|²/2. The source equation must change as well: dot C=[C,lambda L-m lambda² sum(q wedge Cq)]. Both versions are checked against their own energy gradients, with conserved total angular momentum. This is a consistency test for this uniform-connection interpretation, not a uniquely derived nuclear electromagnetic field. On the prepared trajectories, the initial quadratic/uncoupled-kinetic energy ratios are: N l=1 l=2 l=3 l=4 1 0.68 2.60 5.80 10.28 2 0.52 1.60 3.40 5.92 The term is not perturbatively small for the complex petal examples. Adding it reciprocally changes the old l=2 preparation: over one intended turn the one-electron position error reaches 1.86827 with radius change 0.595951; the pair position error reaches 2.53216 with radius change 0.527079. These are tests of the same initial data, not an exclusion of other solutions of the completed equations. The subsequent completed relative-equilibrium calculation finds different exact solutions of the completed Hamiltonian, including one-electron four- and eight-petal branches without resolved exponential linear modes. Thus this initial-data failure is not a no-petal conclusion. Conclusion Actual autonomous petal-shaped projections with reciprocal source motion now exist in an explicit Coulomb-plus-angular-response Hamiltonian, including an exact repelling two-electron family. The source, coupling, and preparation are explicit, and the even-l planar matches are checked, not drawn by an assigned clock. The remaining problems are specific: the pair is unstable; the integer frequency ratio is prepared rather than selected; odd-l and height readouts do not match the visualization; and the magnetic quadratic completion is large and changes these trajectories. title: CP3 response selection
summary: At fixed electron depth six, an explicit filled-band response selects equal nonzero skew strengths and CP3 minimum components, with positive stiffness for normal variations in matrix space but unresolved source occupation and first-order dynamics.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: At fixed electron depth six, an explicit filled-band response selects equal nonzero skew strengths and CP3 minimum components, with positive stiffness for normal variations in matrix space but unresolved source occupation and first-order dynamics. Fixed-depth question The particle depths supplied by the mass formula are fixed inputs to this investigation, as directed by the user. In particular the electron has six spatial dimensions. The question here is whether a six-dimensional interaction selects the complex-structure geometry, not whether the electron should be reassigned to a different depth. Allow an unconstrained real antisymmetric 6x6 variable B. Its three signed canonical plane strengths are lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3. We do not impose B squared proportional to minus the identity. Introducing B as a collective electron order parameter is itself a modeling premise; its microscopic definition remains to be derived. An arbitrary six-dimensional particle does not automatically have this order parameter as its configuration. A specified matrix response rather than a prescribed CP3 penalty Introduce two six-component vector response bands with gap Delta>0 and coupling g!=0. Their real symmetric one-particle operator is h(B)=\begin{pmatrix}0&gB\\-gB&\Delta I_6\end{pmatrix}. Under B -> R B R^T it transforms by conjugation with diag(R,R); no rotation plane is distinguished. Twelve is the number of source states, not a particle depth. This is a new candidate self-response model, distinct from the earlier singlet-plus-nine nuclear-contact model. Neither its source carrier nor its occupation is claimed to follow already from the V2 master kernel. For each plane, the source eigenvalues are e_\pm(y)=\frac{\Delta\pm\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2y}}2, \qquad y=\lambda_i^2, each with multiplicity two. Assume all six lower-band states are occupied, and add a positive bare cost mu times the squared skew norm, with mu>0. Equivalently use the lower-band trace as an explicitly specified effective energy. The fixed six-occupation interpretation is a possible source model, not a claim that an electron has six constituent particles. With <B,B>=−tr(B squared)/2=sum lambda_i², the total energy is exactly E(B)=\mu\langle B,B\rangle+\operatorname{Tr}_{-}h(B) =\sum_{i=1}^3 f(\lambda_i^2),\qquad f(y)=\mu y+\Delta-\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2y}. The source force in each plane is bounded at large strength, while the positive quadratic cost makes the total energy coercive. Thus the energy is not an unstable truncated expansion. Near B=0 its expansion is (mu−2g²/Delta) sum lambda_i²+(2g^4/Delta³) sum lambda_i^4 plus higher orders. The equalizing quartic sign follows from this source spectrum, not a fit. Exact global minimum: the complex-structure constraint emerges For y>=0, f'(y)=\mu-\frac{2g^2}{\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2y}},\qquad f''(y)=\frac{4g^4}{(\Delta^2+4g^2y)^{3/2}}>0. Strict convexity makes equal squared strengths the unique minimizer at any fixed sum of squared strengths. Allowing that sum to vary gives: If mu>=2g²/Delta, the minimum is B=0, not CP3. If 0<mu<2g²/Delta, each squared strength has the same positive minimum \rho^2=\frac{4g^4/\mu^2-\Delta^2}{4g^2}. Consequently every global minimum obeys B^2=-\rho^2 I_6,\qquad J=B/\rho,\qquad J^2=-I_6. The full minimum set is O(6)/U(3). It has two connected components, distinguished by Pfaffian sign. Each component is SO(6)/U(3), hence CP3. The response energy does not select one component or a handedness. The orthogonal-complex constraint has been obtained by minimization rather than inserted into the definition of B. For the dimensionless diagnostic mu=Delta=g=1, rho²=.75 and E_min=−.75. The stationary states with one or two nonzero plane strengths have energies −.25 and −.5; they do not minimize the full energy. Full fluctuation calculation Here "normal variations in matrix space" means changes away from the CP3 minimum family in the auxiliary matrix B, not extra spatial directions. A skew 6x6 matrix has 6(6−1)/2=15 independent rotation-plane components: six variations are tangent to the CP3 family and nine are normal to it in this parameter space. The electron's assigned spatial depth remains six. The gradient in the skew pairing is \nabla E=2\mu B-4g^2B(\Delta^2 I_6-4g^2B^2)^{-1/2}. At B=rho J, skew perturbations H split into six matrix-space variations satisfying HJ+JH=0 and nine satisfying HJ−JH=0. The first are tangent to the CP3 component. The Hessian is zero on them and is a positive scalar on the nine normal variations in matrix space: k_\perp=\frac{16g^4\rho^2}{(2g^2/\mu)^3}>0. This tests all fifteen skew coordinates, not just the three canonical strengths. The diagnostic has six zero eigenvalues and nine eigenvalues equal to 1.5. Flat orientation directions are expected along a family of minima; they do not imply attraction to a unique orientation. What dynamics this energy can and cannot supply A commutator-only equation dot B=[F(B,t),B] preserves all spectral invariants tr(B^n). It cannot turn unequal strengths into equal ones. For this invariant energy, [gradient E,B]=0 identically. Thus simply substituting E into the earlier coadjoint equation would give no amplitude-selection dynamics. As an explicit additional kinetic assumption, introduce canonical momentum Pi for B and Hamiltonian <Pi,Pi>/(2M)+E(B). This allows strength fluctuations. Near the selected family the nine oscillation modes for normal variations in matrix space have frequency sqrt(k_perp/M). Direct evolution verifies their linearized oscillations and total-energy conservation. There is no damping and no claim of relaxation from arbitrary initial states. Low-energy confinement near the minimum manifold is distinct from dissipative capture into it. Restricting the flat kinetic term to B=rho J gives an induced CP3 metric. For a normalized geometric ray Z and horizontal dZ, the existing Pauli map obeys <dJ,dJ>=8||dZ||². With the convention ds_FS²=dZ dagger dZ−|Z dagger dZ|², the kinetic term is therefore 4M rho² ds_FS²/dt². The metric is proportional to Fubini–Study under this specific kinetic assumption, rather than separately named by fiat. This is still a collective-coordinate construction. If B is a field over an already chosen particle base, CP3 is its target/order-parameter space, not automatically that base. Identifying these collective coordinates with the actual six-dimensional electron configuration requires a microscopic reduction that does not double-count spatial variables. The source does not generate the needed first-order term The filled-band projector of h(B) is real symmetric. Its derivative is real symmetric, so the determinant-band Berry curvature i tr(P[dP,dP]) vanishes: a symmetric matrix has zero trace against a real antisymmetric commutator. The calculation checks this using independent projector differences in all skew directions. Therefore this filled real source cannot by itself supply the nonzero first-order symplectic term used in the previous CP3 precession equation. The canonical kinetic example is an inertial model, not a derivation of that first-order equation. An existing electron action term or a suitable complex/chiral response would have to provide it. Geometry selection and the origin of the precession action must not be conflated. Occupation is a substantive premise: counterexample Keep the same h(B) but occupy only its lowest state. The source energy depends only on the largest squared plane strength. All other strengths cost positive mu energy without lowering that occupied level. When the coupling exceeds its corresponding threshold, this version prefers rank two B, not three equal nonzero strengths. For mu=.5, Delta=g=1, the single occupied state gives one squared strength .75 and minimum energy −.125. Both the global bound and the cost of adding other planes are checked. This is not an alternative particle-depth assignment. It shows precisely why the filled-band premise must be derived: rotational symmetry and the displayed source operator alone do not select CP3. Verification and next derivation cp3_geometry_selection_checks.py checks the complete twelve-state spectrum, exact energy, global bounds, finite-difference gradient, full Hessian, pure-ray metric, zero filled-band Berry curvature, partial-rank stationary states, threshold behavior, single-occupation counterexample, and canonical dynamics of normal variations in matrix space. All tests use explicit runtime failures and remain active under Python -O. Normal and optimized runs each completed 631 evaluations across 24 runtime conditions. Reversing the gradient in memory was rejected by the independent energy-gradient check in both modes; no mutated source was saved. The next source-level task is to derive or reject this response operator, its filled-band occupation, and an amplitude kinetic term from the V2 master interaction. Then determine the first-order electron term and the identification with physical spatial coordinates. The result already obtained is a conditional forward mechanism selecting CP3 components at fixed depth six, not a completed physical identification of the electron geometry. Question beyond radial balance The finite cylindrical profile calculation found restoring roots when every ligand was constrained to share one radius. That only tests the breathing coordinate. A molecular candidate can be restoring in that coordinate and still buckle or shear. This check holds the central nucleus and prescribed 6D electron route fixed, but varies every supported-space coordinate of every ligand independently. For ligand centres R_a\in\mathbb R^3, it evaluates U(R_1,\ldots,R_n)=Z_L\left\langle \sum_a V_{r_N}(|q_{\rm vis}(t)-R_a|)\right\rangle_t +\sum_a\frac{Z_0Z_L}{|R_a|} +\sum_{a<b}\frac{Z_L^2}{|R_a-R_b|}, using the finite uniform-ball cylindrical profile V_{r_N} and the same diagnostic values as the radial calculation. title: Dimensional magnetic kernel comparison
summary: The constrained magnetic kernel distinguishes five-dimensional null-axis polarization from six-dimensional complex-structure polarization, while the scalar-exchange bridge explicitly supplies a five-dimensional vector-channel escape route.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: The constrained magnetic kernel distinguishes five-dimensional null-axis polarization from six-dimensional complex-structure polarization, while the scalar-exchange bridge explicitly supplies a five-dimensional vector-channel escape route. Same kernel, different spinor moments Use the existing magnetic bridge: a fixed square-integrable density envelope, one uniform pure polarization, positive magnetic cost, and the leading Pauli coupling. At nonzero Fourier wavevector k, the closed-field projector on skew matrices is \mathcal P_kJ=P_kJ+JP_k,\qquad P_k=\frac{kk^T}{|k|^2}. This formula is valid in either ambient dimension. Its amplitude-space rank is d-1 and its isotropic angular average is (2/d)I on bivectors. In particular the average factor is 2/5 in five dimensions and 1/3 in six. An average projector factor is not itself a particle-depth measurement. With \|J\|^2=-\operatorname{tr}(J^2)/2, \|\mathcal P_kJ\|^2=\frac{|Jk|^2}{|k|^2}. The selected moments derived from the explicit spinors obey J_5^2=-I_5+nn^T,\quad |n|=1, \qquad J_6^2=-I_6. Therefore their directional response strengths are \|\mathcal P_kJ_5\|^2=1-(n\cdot\widehat k)^2, \qquad \|\mathcal P_kJ_6\|^2=1. There is a genuine zero-response direction in five dimensions. No rescaling of the coupling removes it. More generally every skew matrix in an odd-dimensional real space is singular, since \det J=\det(-J)=(-1)^d\det J. Thus a nonzero isotropic response for every wavevector at one fixed polarization is impossible for any odd-dimensional bivector in this kernel. Four-dimensional invertible skew matrices exist, so this parity result alone does not establish exactly six. Envelope anisotropy changes the minimum family differently Write f(k)=|\widetilde n(k)|^2\geq0 for the prescribed envelope weight, using a consistent Fourier convention, and define W=\int f(k)\,dk,\qquad T=\int f(k)\widehat k\widehat k^T\,dk,\qquad\operatorname{tr}T=W. After constrained field minimization, the polarization energies are E_5(z)=-\frac{g^2}{2Z_B}\left(W-n(z)^TTn(z)\right), \qquad E_6(z)=-\frac{g^2}{2Z_B}W. For an isotropic five-dimensional envelope, T=(W/5)I_5, the whole CP3 polarization family still minimizes and the magnitude is (4/5)g^2W/(2Z_B). For a generic anisotropic envelope with a simple lowest eigenvalue, n instead aligns with either sign of its lowest-eigenvalue axis. For any unit n, the condition \gamma(n)z=z defines a complex two-dimensional eigenspace, and its normalized rays form CP1. The explicit spinor identity gives precisely these rays the prescribed n. Hence a simple lowest envelope eigenvalue leaves two CP1 minimum families, one over each sign of the selected axis, not the full CP3. At either family, four ray directions acquire positive curvature and two remain flat. In six dimensions all six ray directions remain flat under this spin-magnetic energy for any such fixed envelope. If the lowest eigenvalue of T has multiplicity m, its allowed unit vectors form S^{m-1} and each has a CP1 ray fibre. The minimum family therefore has real dimension m+1; this dimension count does not assert that the bundle is globally a product. The m=1 case is the two CP1 components above, and m=5 restores all of CP3. In particular, an envelope respecting a three-visible-plus-two-unobserved split has T=\operatorname{diag}(t_V I_3,t_H I_2), with 3t_V+2t_H=W. If t_H<t_V, the minimum family has dimension three; if t_V<t_H, dimension four; if they are equal, dimension six. This symmetry-respecting comparison is more relevant to a fixed nuclear three-plane than assuming an arbitrary five-distinct-eigenvalue envelope. The corresponding six-dimensional pure-spinor magnetic energy remains ray-independent within the stated uniform-polarization approximation. For T=\operatorname{diag}(2,2,2,1,1)/8, a separate finite-difference check gives ray Hessian (0,0,0,1,1,1) to 4\times10^{-8}, as the dimension count predicts. The fibre argument is explicit: \gamma(n)^2=I and \operatorname{tr}\gamma(n)=0 give a two-complex-dimensional positive eigenspace. A ray in it has n(z)\cdot n=1; the already proved unit norm of n(z) forces n(z)=n. Rotational covariance gives the same smooth two-real-dimensional fibre over every axis. An exact axis-weight quadrature with five-dimensional weights (5,4,3,2,1)/15 yields the ray Hessian eigenvalues \left(0,0,\frac8{15},\frac{16}{15},\frac{24}{15},\frac{32}{15}\right), for energy normalized by g^2/(2Z_B)=1. Numerical derivatives reproduce these values. With six-dimensional weights (6,5,4,3,2,1)/21 every ray Hessian eigenvalue is zero analytically and below 1.2\times10^{-8} in the finite-difference calculation. This is a structural prediction of two competing kernels, not a fit of their coupling constants. The five-dimensional null axis and the envelope are explicit variables; no V1 choice of S5 or CP2 spatial base was used. Relation to the spectral discriminator The spectral comparison assumed an isotropic unrestricted bivector cost. For an isotropic envelope, the integrated magnetic projector merely rescales that coupling, preserving the corresponding gap multiplicities. For an anisotropic envelope the selected field is generally not proportional to J. Consequently the six-dimensional frozen-field excited gaps need not remain triply equal for an anisotropic envelope, even though its joint field-plus-ray minimum family remains CP3. These are different statements. Do not demand the isotropic-source singlet-triplet spectrum of every anisotropic magnetic preparation. The existing scalar-exchange bridge supplies the escape channel The operator-class restriction is substantive in the project's other source proposal. In five dimensions the sixteen Hermitian matrix directions are the identity, five \gamma_a, and ten bivectors H_{ab}, orthogonal with trace norm four. For any Hermitian density matrix \varrho, write N=\operatorname{tr}\varrho,\quad v_a=\operatorname{tr}(\varrho\gamma_a), \quad b_{ab}=\operatorname{tr}(\varrho H_{ab}). Completeness gives 4\operatorname{tr}(\varrho^2)=N^2+|v|^2+|b|^2. The same explicitly assumed Gaussian scalar-exchange reduction used in the scalar bridge therefore becomes E_G=\frac\kappa2\left(N^2-\operatorname{tr}\varrho^2\right) =\frac{3\kappa}{8}N^2-\frac\kappa8\left(|v|^2+|b|^2\right). It supplies both a vector and a bivector channel. Dropping the vector channel would not preserve that exchange identity. For a pure ray, S(b)+v\cdot\gamma=4zz^\dagger-I, exactly the operator that evades the five-dimensional bivector-only spectral no-go. Thus the leading Pauli/magnetic proposal and the full scalar-exchange proposal do not have the same dimension-discrimination power. No spectral exclusion of the full five-dimensional exchange competitor has been proved. The existing exchange caveats—Gaussian closure, statistics, normal ordering, and absence of exact one-particle two-body self-interaction—remain unchanged. Physical scope and next test This calculation tests a concrete part of the response kernel already in the archive. It omits orbital magnetic energy, electric response, radiation, spatial profile relaxation, nonuniform polarization, and the nucleus. Anisotropy should next be generated by the coupled envelope/nucleus solution, rather than chosen only as a diagnostic Fourier weight. The useful discriminant is polarization response to controlled envelope anisotropy, or a preparation-resolved directional magnetic response. Whether the electron exhibits either specified response still needs a derived observable map. The mathematics does not identify an electron from CP3 geometry or an averaged cloud alone. Verification dimensional_magnetic_kernel_checks.py performs 500 runtime checks, including kernel projection, directional responses, envelope minimization, the CP1 family, numerical Hessians, and the mixed-density exchange identity. Evidence: dimensional-magnetic-kernel.json. Related Frozen magnetic texture test — subsequent predeclared test that relaxes uniform polarization while leaving this kernel unchanged. Magnetic bivector master bridge — the same constrained field projector and fixed-envelope approximation. Master scalar exchange bridge — the same Gaussian closure, whose five-dimensional decomposition has an extra channel. Five-dimensional CP3 selection and spectral discrimination — explicit spinor moments and operator-class spectral theorem. Dimensional necessity from response — separates kernel-specific discrimination from general dimensional lower bounds.

summary: An explicit quadratic nuclear-plane kernel reproduces the precession flow, while inverse-rate reconstruction exposes nonuniqueness and the oriented source required for the full petal generator.
