Summary: An explicit quadratic nuclear-plane kernel reproduces the precession flow, while inverse-rate reconstruction exposes nonuniqueness and the oriented source required for the full petal generator. What is being reverse engineered The target is first the fixed-nucleus sector precession just derived, and then the stronger target of the visualization's selected rotation generator. These are distinct inverse problems. Constructing a kernel that yields a specified motion proves compatibility, not independent physical selection. No measured masses, fields, or conventional atomic-orbital densities are used in the construction below. Retain J in SO(6)/U(3), the nuclear three-plane projector P, and the symplectic convention dot J = [grad V,J]/I of the precession note. The scale I is an action normalization. The common 6-vector frame and projectors are the binding module's geometric premises, not new coordinates added to the particle. 1. An explicit nuclear-plane interaction kernel Let u denote a nuclear configuration, P(u) its rank-three projector in the shared frame, and gamma(u) a scalar coefficient. Define \boxed{ K_{N6}^{\rm orient}(u,J) =\frac{\gamma(u)}2\|P(u)JP(u)\|_F^2 =-\frac{\gamma(u)}2\operatorname{tr}(P(u)JP(u)J). } This is a smooth, quadratic orientation interaction. Under a simultaneous SO(6) rotation of both arguments it is invariant. It measures how much the electron complex structure rotates nuclear-plane directions within that plane instead of into its complement. It does not model the nucleus as a point or a thin charged sheet. For a normalized nuclear density with a common projector P(u)=P0, V_N(J)=\int\rho_N(u)K_{N6}^{\rm orient}(u,J)d\mu_N(u) =\bar\gamma s(J;P_0),\qquad \bar\gamma=\int\rho_N(u)\gamma(u)d\mu_N(u). It gives precisely the previous V(s)=kappa s with kappa=mean gamma. Thus the previously unspecified orientation kernel now has an explicit candidate. For varying P(u), the integral remains well defined but generally does not collapse to one scalar times s; its anisotropy must be retained. The coefficients, density, and identification of the shared frames are still physical inputs. This kernel is the orientation channel only. It does not supply radial Coulomb binding, spatial falloff, retardation, a field propagator, or a definition of physical separation on the sector. Adding a J-independent term leaves the reduced J flow unchanged, but cannot be advertised as solving the separate relative-position dynamics. 2. Reciprocity is available from the same energy For fixed u and the skew pairing −tr(XY)/2, \nabla_J K=2\gamma PJP. For projector variations, with the ordinary symmetric trace pairing, \delta_P K=\operatorname{tr}(G_P\delta P),\qquad G_P=-\gamma JPJ. The latter expression is an ambient gradient restricted to allowed tangent variations delta P = [B,P], B skew; it is not by itself a nuclear velocity. Simultaneous rotation of both arguments gives \delta_J K\big|_{\delta J=[B,J]} +\delta_P K\big|_{\delta P=[B,P]}=0. Hence a joint dynamical model can use this single interaction to obtain reciprocal orientational forces. A nuclear kinetic or symplectic action is still needed for the response equation; no mechanical inertia or magnetic susceptibility is silently supplied by this identity. 3. Invert an entire precession-rate function For 0<s<1 the previous flow gives the signed rate \omega_{\rm p}(s)=\frac{2V'(s)\sqrt{s}}{\mathcal I}. Therefore a prescribed rate function determines the reduced potential up to a constant on an interval: \boxed{ V(s)=C+\frac{\mathcal I}{2} \int^s\frac{\omega_{\rm p}(v)}{\sqrt v}\,dv. } For example, omega_p(s)=a sqrt(s)+b s^(3/2) gives V(s)=C+I a s/2+I b s²/4. Substituting s(J;P(u)) into this expression gives a higher-order orientation-kernel candidate, for a fixed common plane. A single trajectory at conserved s0 gives much less information: it fixes only V'(s0)=I omega_p(s0)/(2 sqrt(s0)). Adding lambda(s−s0)² changes the kernel away from that trajectory without changing its motion. Likewise, any delta K with zero nuclear marginal leaves V unchanged. Thus neither one precessing orbit nor an entire reduced V identifies a unique microscopic kernel. 4. A nonzero universal rate has a regularity cost Demanding omega_p(s)=omega0 at every 0<s<1 gives V(s)=C+\mathcal I\omega_0\sqrt{s}. This is not smooth at the aligned configuration. Along the smooth signed-coordinate curve A=epsilon K, Q=diag(sqrt(1−epsilon²), sqrt(1−epsilon²),1), C=−epsilon K, it becomes proportional to |epsilon|. The two directional derivatives disagree at zero. This is a property of the inverse construction, not a prohibition on precession. A smooth alternative is V_\eta(s)=\mathcal I\omega_0(\sqrt{s+\eta^2}-\eta),\qquad \omega_{{\rm p},\eta}(s)=\omega_0\sqrt{\frac{s}{s+\eta^2}},\quad\eta>0. It approaches the desired rate away from alignment and tends to zero near alignment. Eta is an additional model parameter, not a derived nuclear width and not the visualization's imbalance parameter. Matching one selected s0 to an orbital clock instead only calibrates a coefficient; it does not establish a dynamically attracting frequency lock. 5. Reverse engineering the full chosen rotation For a prescribed skew generator B_star with units of inverse time, the linear potential V_{\rm target}(J)=\mathcal I\langle B_\star,J\rangle =-\frac{\mathcal I}{2}\operatorname{tr}(B_\star J) gives exactly dot J=[B_star,J] and J(t)=exp(t B_star)J0 exp(−t B_star). Choose the 1:1:3 vector-plane generator corresponding to the existing magnetic construction and this supplies its base rotation. Its specified spin/section lift can then be tested against the existing coefficient flow; the physical observer map and preparation are still required for petals. An inverse source kernel is consequently K_{\rm drive}(u,J)=\mathcal I\langle B(u),J\rangle,\qquad \int\rho_N(u)B(u)d\mu_N(u)=B_\star. This identifies the source tensor that would be needed, rather than deriving that tensor from a scalar nuclear density. It is a separate candidate from the quadratic plane kernel; summing them generally changes the target flow. No claim is made that the sum preserves the desired petals automatically. 6. What a bare nuclear plane can and cannot select A kernel depending only on the unoriented plane P and J must respect the stabilizer SO(3)_O times SO(3)_H. No nonzero fixed skew matrix B_star commutes with this whole group: each diagonal skew 3x3 block must commute with all SO(3) rotations and is therefore zero; the off-diagonal block cannot be invariant under independent rotations of O and H either. Thus a bare plane cannot select that particular linear drive. This does not contradict the quadratic kernel's precession: its effective generator 2 mean(gamma) PJP/I also depends on the electron's prepared J. The result does not exclude a joint symmetry-breaking electron–nucleus solution. It says that an oriented nuclear current, a relational electron–nucleus tensor, or another dynamically selected structure must supply the missing orientation if the full fixed generator is to follow from the source. Flatness already provides the split; it does not provide every axis and relative rotation rate inside that split. Status and next test We have constructed a smooth quadratic inverse kernel, derived both orientation variations, and inverted general precession-rate functions. We have also identified an exact linear source kernel for the stronger target and the extra source information it requires. None is a unique first-principles interaction or a completed electron–nucleus binding model. Next, use the actual projected nuclear/electron currents to calculate the allowed source tensors and their energy cost. summary: A 6D electron, relative angular source, moving finite cylindrical nuclei, and flexible nuclear-plane rotors form one translation-invariant reciprocal Hamiltonian with verified energy and Noether-charge conservation.

Summary: A 6D electron, relative angular source, moving finite cylindrical nuclei, and flexible nuclear-plane rotors form one translation-invariant reciprocal Hamiltonian with verified energy and Noether-charge conservation. Why the first combination failed The completed petal Hamiltonian was originally written about a fixed nuclear origin. Adding moving nuclei without changing that source makes its magnetic completion depend on the absolute electron coordinate and destroys visible translation invariance. A failed momentum-derivative check exposed this before the model was used for shooting. The correction is to define the source coupling using the electron--central- nucleus relative coordinate s=q-(R_0,0). The completed kinetic term is then H_e=\frac1{2m_e}|p-m_e\lambda Cs|^2 +\frac{\langle C,C\rangle}{2I_C}. The central nucleus receives the opposite visible component of the source force. It receives no unobserved translational momentum because it remains a depth-three object. Full diagnostic Hamiltonian For nuclear centres R_a\in\mathbb R^3, momenta P_a, rank-three planes \Pi_a, and skew plane velocities \Omega_a, use H=H_e+\sum_a\frac{|P_a|^2}{2M_a} +\sum_a\frac{I_a}{2}\langle\Omega_a,\Omega_a\rangle +\sum_a V_a\bigl(|\Pi_a(q-(R_a,0))|\bigr) +\sum_{a<b}\frac{Z_aZ_b}{|R_a-R_b|}. Here V_a is the finite uniform supported-space profile of the preceding note, extended cylindrically through unsupported coordinates. The source coadjoint equation uses s\wedge p and s\wedge Cs, not q\wedge p about an external origin. Each plane obeys \dot\Pi_a=[\Omega_a,\Pi_a], \qquad I_a\dot\Omega_a=2[\Pi_a,\partial_{\Pi_a}V_a]. Every force and torque is obtained from this one energy. The executable originally specialized the equations to m_e=1 while exposing a configurable mass. The September 7 audit restores the factors of m_e in the completed square, velocity, magnetic force, and source gradient; the reported unit-mass run is unchanged. Nuclear mutual repulsion is a separately assumed centre-charge interaction here. It is not the mutual interaction of overlapping finite cylindrical charge profiles, particularly when their support planes differ. The full skew rotor also permits angular momentum in the plane stabilizer; a pure Grassmannian plane rotor requires horizontal initial angular velocity or an explicit reduction. Conserved quantities The visible total momentum is \mathcal P_O=p_O+\sum_aP_a. The visible rotational charge is \mathcal J_O=q_O\wedge p_O+C_{OO} +\sum_aR_a\wedge P_a-\sum_a I_a(\Omega_a)_{OO}. Ten random states independently check the differential conservation of H, \mathcal P_O, and \mathcal J_O. A nonlinear example contains one central cylinder plus three trigonal ligand cylinders with moving centres, four flexible planes, and a nonzero electron angular source. Over eight model time units its maximum errors are: quantity maximum error energy 7.93\times10^{-8} visible momentum 3.59\times10^{-15} visible rotational charge 2.87\times10^{-10} projector idempotence 2.18\times10^{-11} The differential energy residual is below 8.9\times10^{-10}. Thus the finite profile, moving lower-depth centres, plane rotors, and completed source are mutually compatible at the Hamiltonian level. Remaining periodic-orbit problem This calculation establishes the system to shoot; it does not claim that the arbitrary nonlinear example is molecularly periodic. The next solve should start from the exact trigonal orbit and the restoring finite-profile radius, fix centre-of-mass and global-rotation gauge directions, and solve a relative-periodic boundary condition. The monodromy calculation must retain electron, source, nuclear-centre, and plane-rotor perturbations. Stable radial force balance alone is not sufficient. The uniform-ball nuclear profile and dimensionless masses, charges, and inertias remain diagnostic inputs. A successful branch would establish existence within that controlled model, not yet derive those inputs from V2. Reproduction reciprocal_cylindrical_molecule_checks.py checks the relative-source energy gradient, visible translation and rotation charges, nonlinear integration, all four plane constraints, and a nonzero source preparation. Related Finite cylindrical nuclear profile — prerequisite: supplies the finite encounter law and restoring candidate radii. Nuclear-plane rotor — prerequisite: supplies the finite-inertia projector dynamics and torque normalization. title: Ring section embedding
summary: The ring's three-state generator embeds in positive-degree section spaces under the same Killing action, but this does not identify a degree-zero electron sector.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. Summary: The ring's three-state generator embeds in positive-degree section spaces under the same Killing action, but this does not identify a degree-zero electron sector. What can be unified algebraically The demo uses a separate ring coefficient generator ν diag(0,−1,0), with initial state (A,B/√2,B/√2), and a constant-radius readout whose angle is the relative clock phase. Its projective orbit is not generated by the one-dimensional H⁰(O(0)) space. There is nevertheless a simple embedding in the same section spaces used for the petalled cases. Denote the section degree by k here, keeping it distinct from the demo's ring label L = 0. For every k ≥ 2 choose normalized monomials proportional to s_0=Z_1Z_2Z_4^{k-2},\qquad s_-=Z_3Z_4^{k-1},\qquad s_r=Z_4^k. They are distinct sections of O(k). Under the same generator Ĝ_k = N₁−N₂−N₃ their weights are exactly (0,−1,0). Hence \Phi(t)=A s_0+\frac B{\sqrt2}e^{i\nu t}s_- +\frac B{\sqrt2}s_r has precisely the demo's three-state coefficient evolution and returns after 2π/ν. The prescribed ring readout Γ_x+iΓ_y = R times the normalized clock coherence is Re^{iνt}. This is an actual time-dependent coefficient orbit in a selected section subspace, not a stationary field substituted for the ring. The selected spinor-line construction lifts this field into Σ⊗O(k+2), just as it lifts the degree-k petalled orbit. At k = 2, the 10-dimensional section space therefore contains both the ring's three-state generator and the four-state generator used for four petals. No new generator weights or electric charge have been fitted to obtain this fact. What this does not unify This is not a degree-zero construction. The earlier dimension obstruction for H⁰(O(0)) remains intact, and the k ≥ 2 ring cannot be declared the physical L = 0 atomic state without a separate identification. It shows that the generator algebra need not require an unrelated carrier space; it does not derive which carrier the physical circular state occupies. The ring and petalled prescriptions select different mode subspaces and readout rules. An algebraic embedding alone does not derive a single apparatus response that selects between those rules, a nuclear preparation mechanism, energies, or transition strengths. In particular, the petal-count rule 2k applies to the prepared extremal exchange construction, not to every trajectory in O(k). Degree alone does not force a petalled outline. The smooth geometric clock dipole from the probe calculation also exists here, but it already gives circular dipole signals for some petalled preparations. It cannot by itself distinguish those detector images. Research consequence A single positive-degree field sector may support multiple coefficient-orbit families under the same Killing action. This supplies a concrete candidate bridge for the ring, with no change to the displayed petals or their code. The remaining problem is physical family selection and the degree/flux interpretation, not merely finding three suitable abstract frequencies. The scalar effective-drive route also applies algebraically in this space, but inherits the omitted-mode leakage and locking corrections audited in the companion note. The embedding is not a stability proof. Reproduction orbit_drive_origin_checks.py checks the three weights, normalized evolution, clock readout, and full recurrence for k = 2, 3, 4, while retaining the one-dimensional degree-zero check. Research status — current proof boundaries and correction routes.

title: Five-dimensional CP3 selection and spectral discrimination
summary: A five-dimensional spinor-bivector model also selects a CP3 minimum family, but its exact spectral sum rule excludes the six-dimensional singlet-triplet gap within the linear-bivector operator class.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: A five-dimensional spinor-bivector model also selects a CP3 minimum family, but its exact spectral sum rule excludes the six-dimensional singlet-triplet gap within the linear-bivector operator class. Why this comparison matters The six-dimensional selection uses one pure normalized irreducible spinor, a real skew source, positive quadratic source energy, and linear spinor-bivector coupling. Here the same construction is performed for a five-dimensional Euclidean carrier. No inherited V1 spatial geometry is assigned to that carrier. An irreducible Spin(5) spinor has four complex components, as does either irreducible half-spin representation of Spin(6). The general dimensions are 2^n for Spin(2n+1) and 2^{n-1} for each half-spin of Spin(2n). See Woit's representation construction. The explicit five-dimensional representation and its quaternionic structure are also discussed in Niedzialomski's five-dimensional spinor analysis. The following energy and spectrum calculations are explicit local derivations, not claims taken from those references. Exact five-dimensional construction Using Pauli matrices, take the Hermitian Clifford generators \gamma=(\sigma_1\otimes I,\sigma_2\otimes I, \sigma_3\otimes\sigma_1,\sigma_3\otimes\sigma_2, \sigma_3\otimes\sigma_3). They obey \{\gamma_a,\gamma_b\}=2\delta_{ab}I_4. For z^\dagger z=1, define H_{ab}=-i\gamma_a\gamma_b,\quad b_{ab}=z^\dagger H_{ab}z,\quad n_a=z^\dagger\gamma_a z, \quad S(b)=\sum_{a<b}b_{ab}H_{ab}. Let J be the skew matrix with upper entries b_{ab}, with \|J\|^2=-\operatorname{tr}(J^2)/2=\sum b_{ab}^2. Direct Clifford calculation gives |n|^2=1,\qquad \|J\|^2=2,\qquad J^2=-I_5+nn^T,\qquad Jn=0. Thus the source has two unit rotation planes and one null axis. It is not an invertible complex structure on an odd-dimensional vector space. Furthermore S(b)z=2z,\qquad zz^\dagger=\frac{S(b)^2}{8}+\frac{S(b)}4. The last identity reconstructs the ray from the bivector, so no ray degree is lost. These identities are verified as polynomials in eight independent real spinor components, without assuming normalization numerically. For an initially unrestricted skew B, take E(B,z)=\mu\|B\|^2-g\langle B,J(z)\rangle, \qquad \mu,g>0. With \rho=g/(2\mu), completion gives E(B,z)=\mu\|B-\rho J(z)\|^2-\frac{g^2}{2\mu}. All normalized rays minimize at B=\rho J(z), and the injective reconstruction makes their minimum family CP3. This does not require assuming CP3 as the carrier's spatial base. It is the collective polarization/source family of this specified five-dimensional model. The Berry term i\hbar z^\dagger\dot z is the same nonzero projective symplectic structure as in the six-dimensional construction. Adding M\|\dot B\|^2/2 gives reciprocal dynamics and the exact conserved bound \mu\|B-\rho J(z)\|^2+\frac{\|\Pi\|^2}{2M} =E_{\rm total}-E_{\min}. This controls departure from the minimum family, not spatial localization or an electron-nucleus orbit. The ten-component source-space Hessian after ground-ray elimination has six flat directions and four positive normal directions 2\mu; these are matrix-space counts, not extra spatial axes. The Hessian statement also follows analytically: minimizing the completed square over rays gives E_{\rm eff}(B)-E_{\min}=\mu\,operatorname{dist} (B,\rho J(\mathrm{CP}^3))^2. In a tubular neighborhood of this smooth embedded orbit, the squared-distance Hessian is twice the normal projector. The numerical Hessian is an independent finite-difference check of that result. What differs from six dimensions At the selected source, the five-dimensional spinor Hamiltonian has \operatorname{spec}h_5(\rho J) =g\rho\,(-2,0,0,2), whereas the six-dimensional chiral model has \operatorname{spec}h_6(\rho J) =g\rho\,(-3,1,1,1). Their gaps above the selected ray are respectively (2,2,4)g\rho and (4,4,4)g\rho. Thus “CP3 minima, a gap, a Berry term, and conservative confinement” do not distinguish them, while the full gap multiplicity does. Their induced source kinetic metrics also differ. For Fubini–Study unit horizontal tangents at z=(1,0,0,0), the five-dimensional squared bivector derivative has weights (4,4,4,4,8,8); the six-dimensional construction has weight 8 in all six directions. The five-dimensional CP3 family is not being claimed to have the same induced metric or every same response. A genuine no-go theorem for the five-dimensional competitor Every real skew 5\times5 source is orthogonally reducible to two rotation blocks and a zero direction. The corresponding irreducible spinor Hamiltonian has eigenvalues \{\alpha+\beta,\alpha-\beta,-\alpha+\beta,-\alpha-\beta\}, up to an overall scalar shift and coupling scale. Order the positive block strengths \alpha\geq\beta\geq0. If its ground state is nondegenerate, the three gaps are \Delta_1=2\beta,\qquad\Delta_2=2\alpha, \qquad\Delta_3=2(\alpha+\beta)=\Delta_1+\Delta_2. Consequently three equal positive gaps are impossible for any source in this operator class, not just for the selected minimum or a sampled parameter range. Equivalently, the ordered eigenvalues always obey \lambda_1+\lambda_4=\lambda_2+\lambda_3. This is robust: a target with eigenvalues (E_0,E_0+\Delta,E_0+\Delta, E_0+\Delta), \Delta>0, has operator-norm distance at least \Delta/4 from every scalar-plus-five-dimensional-bivector Hamiltonian, even allowing arbitrary spinor bases. If the norm error is \epsilon, each ordered eigenvalue differs by at most \epsilon. The two pair sums of the target differ by \Delta, so the competitor's equality forces \Delta\leq4\epsilon. The bound is attained: for target \operatorname{diag}(-3,1,1,1), the aligned canonical bivector spectrum (-2,0,0,2) is at distance one. Conditional exact-six theorem Assume all of the following are independently justified: The relevant polarization is one fundamental complex spatial spin module, or one irreducible half-spin module in even dimensions, of a Euclidean d-dimensional carrier. It has exactly four complex components. This means the module supplied by the spatial Clifford construction, not an arbitrary higher-spin representation, multiplicity space, or four-level internal system. Its source Hamiltonian is linear in spatial bivectors, apart from a scalar shift; no extra vector or higher-degree operator is present. A selected ray has one nondegenerate energy and three exactly equal higher energies separated by a nonzero gap. The spin-representation dimension formula restricts d to five or six. The spectral sum rule excludes five. Within these premises, d=6. Unlike a theorem that assumes chirality from the start, this argument uses the spectrum to discriminate the two four-component irreducible spinors. It does not establish that an actual electron satisfies premises 1–3. In the existing archive the six-dimensional operator produces this spectrum, but deriving a physical requirement for it independently of that operator remains necessary to avoid circular identification. Frozen-source gaps versus reciprocal response frequencies The preceding spectra hold the source fixed during a spinor variation. They are not the normal frequencies of the entire coupled source-spinor system. The flat minimum family supplies six zero modes in that larger system. This distinction can be followed through exactly. For one complex tangent u, choose the corresponding normalized complex source displacement b. If the squared moment-map derivative weight is w, then \Delta=g^2w/(4\mu) and the linearized equations are M\ddot b=-2\mu b+g\sqrt w\,u, \qquad i\hbar\dot u=\Delta u-\frac{g\sqrt w}{2}b. With time dependence e^{-i\omega t} the characteristic polynomial is \omega\left(M\hbar\omega^2-M\Delta\omega-2\mu\hbar\right)=0. Apart from the zero mode, the positive frequency pair is \omega_{\rm high,low} =\frac{\sqrt{\Delta^2+8\mu\hbar^2/M}\ \mathord{\pm}\ \Delta}{2\hbar}. In particular \omega_{\rm high}-\omega_{\rm low}=\frac{\Delta}{\hbar}, \qquad\omega_{\rm high}\omega_{\rm low}=\frac{2\mu}{M}. Thus reciprocal source motion changes the frequencies but preserves the gap as a pair separation in this quadratic, isotropic-inertia model. Five dimensions have two identical pairs and one different pair; six dimensions have three identical pairs. The remaining source-normal modes have frequency \sqrt{2\mu/M}, with multiplicity four and nine respectively. These are additional source degrees of freedom, not spatial dimensions. At \mu=1.3,g=0.7,M=0.4,\hbar=2, the five-dimensional pairs are (2.45701979,2.64548133) twice and (2.36800433,2.74492741) once. Six dimensions give the latter pair three times. Direct full nonlinear projective evolution matches the analytic tangent response: reducing perturbations from 10^{-4} to 10^{-5} reduces the scaled prediction error by a factor of ten in both models. This is a calculable response target, not a demonstrated experimental access route. Other source inertias, extra couplings, damping, nuclear interaction, and detector selection require their own calculation. For the explicitly specified drive “force on the source tangent” and readout “the same source displacement,” the complex-helicity susceptibility is \chi_b(\omega)=\frac{\Delta-\hbar\omega} {\omega(M\hbar\omega^2-M\Delta\omega-2\mu\hbar)}. Its nonzero mode poles have nonvanishing numerators, so they are not dark to this input/output pair. The full linear-system resolvent reproduces this formula at fifteen off-resonant probes in each dimension to below 1.8\times10^{-15}. The frozen-source value \omega=\Delta/\hbar is an antiresonance of this helicity response, not a coupled-system pole. These are ideal model controls and observations; their laboratory access has not been derived. Operator-class escape route: why the hypotheses matter The same five-dimensional matrices obey S(b)+\sum_a n_a\gamma_a=4zz^\dagger-I_4. Allowing an additional vector source therefore reproduces the singlet-triplet operator exactly in five dimensions. The no-go theorem is a theorem about linear bivector coupling, not arbitrary five-dimensional interactions. Scalar nonlinearities in the bivector operator could also alter its spectrum. A microscopic derivation must justify the allowed operator class before this discriminator can decide spatial dimension. None of these source-polarization energy gaps have yet been identified with measured atomic excitation energies. Their multiplicities should not be relabelled p/d/f shell counts. Verification spin5_selection_checks.py checks universal Clifford polynomial identities, moment-map injectivity, the completed-square minimum, all six projective tangent directions, the selected spectrum, normal Hessian, induced metric, Berry curvature, and reciprocal conservation. The first run completed 501 checks. Later spectral-distance and vector-channel checks extend that run; saved reports retain their separate counts. spinor_response_poles_checks.py checks the reciprocal frequency calculation against the full variational matrix and nonlinear evolution. Evidence: extended selection checks and reciprocal response checks. The forced-response extension completes 93 runtime checks, including source-pole observability. Chiral CP3 selection — six-dimensional construction compared under the same type of source energy. Dimensional necessity from response — independent rank theorem and dynamical five-dimensional competitor.

summary: Two orthogonal occupied modes admit self-consistent collective precession through one dynamical contact source, with conserved energy and antisymmetry; this extends the response model but does not yet derive interacting petal trajectories.

Summary: Two orthogonal occupied modes admit self-consistent collective precession through one dynamical contact source, with conserved energy and antisymmetry; this extends the response model but does not yet derive interacting petal trajectories. What is established The finite response model has a two-electron collective rotating family. Both occupied modes drive the same source, and that source acts back on both. The second electron cannot be omitted while retaining this solution. This is a positive existence result in a specified reciprocal model, not two noninteracting copies of the one-electron calculation. Electron depth remains six. The four complex components below are the existing chiral carrier, not four spatial dimensions. Nor do the four available carrier modes set atomic shell capacities: spatial and other degrees of freedom have not been supplied in this truncation. Shared variational system Let U be a complex 4 by 2 occupied frame with U†U=I2. Its two columns define a normalized antisymmetric Slater state. Put D=UU†, so D²=D and tr D=2. Apply the existing linear moment map to D and take its mixed block Q. Thus Q is the sum of the two individual mixed blocks; D is a number-density matrix, not a trace-one single-electron state. For the normalized ten-state contact-source vector n, use the existing response X=2 Re(n0* n_exc), arranged as a 3 by 3 matrix. The energy is E(U,n)=\Delta\|n_{\rm exc}\|^2-g\sum_{i,j}X_{ij}Q_{ij}. Varying this energy with the occupied-state and source Berry terms gives i\hbar\dot U=h_e(X)U,\qquad i\hbar\dot n=h_N(Q)n, \qquad h_e(X)=g\sum_{i,j}X_{ij}\sigma_i\otimes\sigma_j. The source Hamiltonian has excited diagonal Delta and singlet-to-excited matrix entries -g Qij. The interaction appears once in the joint energy, not once in each subsystem energy followed by double counting. Hermiticity preserves U†U and n†n. Reciprocity conserves E. This is a variational Slater-times-source product-state model. It includes shared-source feedback but not unrestricted electron-source entanglement, general electron correlation, or direct spatial electron-electron repulsion. Explicit collective family For 0<a<1, define q=sqrt(1-a²), c=sqrt((1+a)/2), s=sqrt((1-a)/2), u_1=(0,c,-s,0)^T,\qquad u_2=(c,0,0,s)^T. These vectors are orthonormal and their total Q is diag(0,2q,0). Let K rotate the first two axes of the first real three-plane, KN act as K tensor I3 on source excitations and vanish on the singlet, and Ze=(sigma_z tensor I2)/2. With d=Delta-epsilon and b=d²-(hbar omega)², solve p_0=\left[1+4g^2q^2\frac{d^2+(\hbar\omega)^2}{b^2}\right]^{-1}, \qquad \epsilon=-\frac{4g^2q^2d}{b},\qquad \omega=\frac{4g^2a p_0 d}{(\hbar/2)b}. The source initial state is proportional to (1, g[(Delta-epsilon)I9-i hbar omega KN_exc]^{-1}vec Q). It is an eigenvector of hN-i hbar omega KN with eigenvalue epsilon. The initial occupied subspace is invariant under he-hbar omega Ze; call its 2 by 2 restriction Lambda. Then U(t)=e^{-i\omega t Z_e}U(0)e^{-it\Lambda/\hbar},\qquad n(t)=e^{-i\epsilon t/\hbar}e^{\omega t K_N}n(0) solve the coupled equations. These are relative equilibria, not imposed forcing of a frozen source. For Delta=4, g=sqrt(25/32), hbar=2: a Source rotating eigenvalue epsilon Shared rotation rate omega 0.2 -0.647223765289 0.118279749049 0.4 -0.579777848366 0.244428017949 0.6 -0.462352822676 0.390445033634 0.8 -0.283836238760 0.585670679075 Rates are in the model's units. The previous one-electron a=0.6 example has rate 0.4006985724 with the same Delta, g, and hbar. The pair changes both total preparation and source response; this is not a universal electron-count scaling law. Physical reading and remaining test U and U R for any unitary 2 by 2 matrix R describe the same occupied projector and the same Slater ray. Individual occupied-column paths are therefore not uniquely labeled electron trajectories. The gauge-invariant collective projector evolves nontrivially; a physical position readout must respect this frame freedom. This does not replace the intended actual orbits by stationary orbitals: it identifies what the present carrier calculation can establish about them. The proven extension is shared-source collective precession with two electrons. The source has not yet generated the visualization's complete petal generator and position readout, for either one or two interacting electrons. No stability conclusion follows from existence or an unperturbed integration. Next is a gauge-consistent spatial many-electron readout and interaction, followed by perturbation tests and shell observables. Neither p/d/f capacities nor a helium spectrum has been derived here. The subsequent petal response residual makes the generator mismatch explicit: the prescribed demo lift varies s at three times the clock frequency, whereas every orientation-only V(s) conserves s. Full finite-source inverse tests also find nonzero residual bounds at the tested parameters. The existing selected map already produces the radial modulation from the prescribed lift; its source dynamics, not the algebraic readout formula, is the newly tested missing connection. Reproduction two_electron_shared_response_checks.py solves all four roots and independently integrates each coupled solution for a full collective revolution. It checks energy, source normalization, occupied orthogonality, projector rank, Slater normalization and exchange antisymmetry. Random preparations test reciprocity and occupied-frame invariance. Omitting the second electron is required to fail the source equilibrium equation. Checks raise exceptions rather than using assert. The initial run completed 3,716 evaluations across 21 conditions. Maximum full-revolution occupied-state and source errors were 7.75e-12 and 1.30e-11; energy drift was 2.51e-12 and occupied Gram error was 1.31e-12. Mutation testing exposed that conservation on a relative equilibrium alone does not detect a doubled energy coupling. Twelve arbitrary-direction finite-difference energy-gradient checks were added to compare the energy function directly with both evolution equations. The expanded checker rejects reversed source evolution, doubled interaction energy, and omission of the second electron from the source tensor. This validation correction does not change the rotating solutions. The expanded checker completed 3,728 evaluations across 22 conditions in both normal and Python -O runs. The energy-gradient finite-difference residual was at most 6.41e-10; all three deliberately incorrect variants were rejected by that check. Provenance Preserved from interaction notebook section 45, recorded 2026-09-05 and corrected 2026-09-06. Original sequence contents. This is consistent with the earlier result that the scalar self-contact/rest-frequency operator does not by itself select the 3+3 orientation. 65.3 The positive commutator norm is distinct For the same motion, \operatorname{Tr}([D,\dot P]^\dagger[D,\dot P]) = 2\left[(d_3-d_1)^2+(d_4-d_2)^2\right]. This is a positive quadratic functional of the squared spectral gaps. It is not the same as the second variation of the linear compressed operator, which is linear in the gaps. Therefore \boxed{ \bar\Psi PDP\Psi \not\Rightarrow \operatorname{Tr}([D,P]^\dagger[D,P]) } with a fixed universal coefficient. 65.4 Consequence for projector dynamics The canonical candidate S_P =\frac{\alpha}{2N_s} \operatorname{Tr}([D,P]^\dagger[D,P]) gives the Grassmannian kinetic metric only under the additional assumptions in section 64, but the current V2 action does not force this term merely from the unit coefficient of the linear Dirac kinetic term. The overall coefficient \boxed{\alpha} therefore remains a genuine action-level quantity unless an additional master principle fixes it. 65.5 Status The projector route survives, but one shortcut is ruled out: \boxed{ \text{unit normalization of the linear Dirac action does not fix the projector sigma-model normalization.} } What remains viable is either: a genuine master-field quadratic commutator/projector term; a symmetry or normalization principle fixing its coefficient; or a nonperturbative relation tying the projector-gradient norm to an already derived V2 spectral ratio. Correction to the preceding research pass The target in V2 is an actual electron orbit, represented by Hamiltonian evolution and its observer projection. It is not a conventional stationary electron orbital. The earlier assistant discussion substituted the latter as the target and incorrectly suggested that only circulation and second moments had been worked out. The existing 6D orbit demo already specifies the complete projected curve and its time-occupation measure. The recent scalar Hartree and oscillator-state calculations remain correct within their stated auxiliary models. Calling them progress toward the observed shapes without establishing this connection was unjustified. A stationary field carrying an angular expectation is not a derivation of a particle trajectory. The coupled scalar branch is an auxiliary field solution, not an established source for the demo's generator or proof of stability of its orbits. Some preserved note IDs and filenames contain “orbital”; they name the auxiliary calculation that was actually performed. Replacing that word everywhere with “orbit” would falsely relabel the mathematics. Those notes now carry this correction explicitly. Standard terms such as spin-orbit coupling and orbital angular momentum do not imply a conventional-orbital ontology and are retained where mathematically appropriate. Existing orbit construction Provenance correction: Coulomb binding plus precession The user's stated starting point was a Coulomb-bound 6D orbit, with precession subsequently added to produce petals. The assistant's later framing as a search for forces to create an otherwise unexplained shape lost that history. Inspecting only the earliest trigonometric demo was insufficient; subsequent revisions contain the relevant construction. The history of visualizations/6d-orbit-slice.html records: ce71f75: computeShell rotates the four-component direction in six coordinate planes, with rates abs(I[i]-I[j])*W1, where I[i]=exp[i]+1. It explicitly sets the precession lock κ = ω₁, takes component moduli, and combines them with commensurate phase motion to generate the path. The paths are computed from this motion, not spherical-harmonic surfaces. The assigned rates, phases, and small radial breathing term are not a numerical integration of an electron–nucleus force law. Its prose's closure and stability claims are not interchangeable. f2ad825: explicitly clarifies that the direction of the trajectory in CP3 precesses, correcting the earlier wording “its amplitude precesses.” 1f8a54a: replaces the legacy rotation recipe with a specified norm-preserving Hamiltonian flow, an L-dependent exchange, and a relative-phase clock. This is a mathematical replacement, not evidence that the legacy ordered rotations obeyed that same Hamiltonian. c6d6bcf and 4701c3a: construct the exchange and clock as parts of one degree-L representation of a higher-dimensional symmetry action. Their frequency ratio follows within the selected construction; identifying its source with physical electromagnetism and fixing its rate remain conditional. Later corrections distinguish sector points from section coefficients and constrain the observer map. These revisions can be inspected with git show <commit>:visualizations/6d-orbit-slice.html from this repository. The earlier Coulomb-plus-confinement Hamiltonian in the page's prose (for example c50ef57) does not by itself derive the later precession term. The historical intent and the implemented dynamics must both be recorded without conflating them. The research baseline is therefore the existing orbit-plus-precession construction, not an arbitrary petal curve awaiting a mechanism. The next physical task is to derive or test that precession and its lock from the coupled electron–nucleus dynamics. Nuclear feedback is a candidate contribution or correction, not an already demonstrated prerequisite for petals. The recent nuclear-polarization diagnostic treats an electric dipole response; it has not calculated the induced magnetic feedback the user proposed. Current mathematical construction The demo distinguishes the sector coordinate [Z] in CP3, the orbit-state coefficient ray [c] in P(V_L), and the spatial Dirac field at [Z]. The four-state subspace V_L is selected inside the degree-L section space. For the specified Hamiltonian, [c(t)] = [exp(-iM_L t)c(0)]. This has 2L radial maxima and intervening zeros for integer L ≥ 1. The L = 0 ring has a separately supplied clock completion, since the degree-zero section space alone is one-dimensional. The observer's finite registration density is the response-broadened time measure of this actual orbit: \rho_{\rm obs}(x)=\frac1T\int_0^T G_\sigma(x-\Gamma_L(t))\,dt. The shape construction and its orbital frequency ratio are therefore present. Deriving why the physical bound system selects that representation and generator, how its clock locks to the electron–nucleus motion, and its electromagnetic curvature identification, physical rate, and observer response from the action remains open. This does not erase the conditional representation-theoretic lock already obtained. A successful derivation must connect to this construction rather than replace it with stationary oscillator densities. Scope of the geometric corrections The characteristic-class obstructions concern full-rank global bundle identifications, not the existence of the coefficient trajectory in P(V_L). Summary: Localized electron detections and accumulated spatial distributions constrain a measurement model but do not directly reveal a smeared physical electron or select a dimensional ontology. What the experiments measure Single-electron interference experiments record localized detection events; the accumulated events form interference fringes. Neither the detector spot nor the accumulated pattern is a photograph of a particle's physical boundary. The distinction is visible in the experimenters' own Hitachi account. The hydrogen photoionization-microscopy experiment measures outgoing-electron patterns. Its identification of atomic nodal structure uses the relationship between the near-atom state and the continuum wavefunction in a specified electric field. This is an experimental constraint mediated by a mathematical model, not a direct picture of a fuzzy material body surrounding the nucleus. See the AMOLF primary publication record. Conversely, localized detector events do not by themselves prove a pointlike underlying object. A model must explain the localized events and the distribution, including interference, together. Exact projection statement Let a point trajectory in the six-coordinate model be (X(t),Y(t)), with three visible and three unobserved coordinates. Its instantaneous marginal is \int \delta(x-X(t))\delta(y-Y(t))\,d^3y=\delta(x-X(t)). Unobserved-coordinate marginalization does not spread a point. For a normalized extended joint density, its visible marginal can instead be extended. A time-averaged trajectory also gives a different object, \overline\rho(x)=\frac1T\int_0^T\delta(x-X(t))\,dt. Identifying this time measure with detection probabilities requires a sampling and interaction law. Convolution with an apparatus response additionally assumes the relevant spatial response is translation invariant. These assumptions must be tested; ordinary motion averaging alone is not a derivation of interference. Correction to V2 inference The argument “one nuclear ontology produces a smeared electron, therefore it is the real ontology” is withdrawn. No such selection follows from a spread alone. The cylindrical nuclear field in Bound within, free without remains the chosen working premise, not an observationally selected conclusion. The electron's mass-formula depth assignment is unchanged; it is not inferred from an assumed appearance. title: Frequency-domain review
summary: Corrected frequency-domain conclusions and the remaining hadronic proof target.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: Corrected frequency-domain conclusions and the remaining hadronic proof target. RESEARCH NOTES, NOT A PHYSICS MODULE. This is a record of calculations, corrections, and unresolved hypotheses. It does not assert a completed hadronic-mass derivation or a validated replacement for the V2 master dynamics. 1. Where the investigation stands The most useful progress was not another numerical factor close to a nucleon residual. Several earlier exclusions depended on confusing a static matrix, an observed projection, or an operator coefficient with a frequency generator. Those exclusions were narrowed or withdrawn after exact checks. Two later results had not yet been recorded in the inspected ledger. First, the point-contact construction and a smooth coherent-density construction have different spectra; the latter does not automatically replace or disprove the graph-supported prescription explicitly chosen in V2. Second, a rank-one source-to-scalar-self-energy response supplies a concrete sufficient mechanism for the common-anchor ratios without measuring or solving for the sources. The unresolved issue is whether that response applies to complete occupied reference frequencies or to coefficients before the simplex multiplier. The companion contact-kernel note and rank-one-response note contain those previously undocumented calculations. They are live possibilities and exact comparison tests, not a numerical baryon prediction. The last inspected hadronic ledger ends at Section 76. Its Sections 67--76 contain the earlier saved corrections. The returned execution report confirmed that write and its verification. Later read-only tests did not, by themselves, save the additional findings. This notes package preserves them separately rather than extending an exploratory ledger as though it were a finished module. 2. Observable and notation discipline The target is a rest-frequency ratio, ultimately z_B=\frac{\omega_B}{\omega_e}, \qquad \omega_e=\frac{m_ec^2}{\hbar}. Use \varpi_d=\mu_d/\hbar when \mu_d denotes the sector energy unit, and distinguish it from an oscillator frequency produced by a constriction model. On the hypothesized ordinary contact branch, \omega_{n,d}=\varpi_d S(n,d), \qquad S(n,d)=\binom{n+d-1}{d}. A specified occupied reference frequency is \omega_d^\star=\varpi_d S(n_d^\star,d), not generally \varpi_d. In particular, the depth-four reference has count 15, while the electron reference has count 18564. The pre-prism source-phase proposal \Omega_{n,d}=S(n,d)-1 is yet another object; its identification with time-dependent physical dynamics remains conditional in the contact-resonance source, Section 3. No independently calibrated field amplitude is an input to these notes. Arbitrary normalization of an eigenvector cannot move the eigenvalues of a fixed linear operator. However, replacing an unknown coefficient by an unknown frequency ratio does not determine it, and a nonlinear background dependence cannot be erased by renaming its variables. Genuine coefficients, projected kernels, kinetic metrics, and boundary conditions still need a derivation or a demonstrated cancellation. 3. Corrected static and spectral matrix results For the adopted test values G=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}, \qquad a=8\sqrt7,\quad b=4\sqrt6,\quad c=12/\sqrt7, one has b^2=ac. The three quantities previously conflated are \underbrace{a-b^2/c}_{\text{actual static Schur complement}}=0, \qquad \underbrace{b^2/c}_{\text{removed relaxation contribution}}=a, \qquad \underbrace{a}_{\text{clamped principal block}}. The frequency-dependent matrix elimination instead uses f(z)=a-z-\frac{b^2}{c-z}, \qquad (c-z)f(z)=\det(G-zI)=z(z-a-c). This is exact away from the excluded complementary denominator. That excluded value must be checked in the original problem. The full matrix eigenvalues are 0 and a+c, not the removed static contribution considered in isolation. The operator square root also does not commute with projection. Here \sqrt G=\frac{G}{\sqrt{a+c}}, \qquad \frac{\langle3|\sqrt G|3\rangle}{\sqrt a}=\sqrt{14/17}, \qquad \frac{\sqrt{\langle3|G|3\rangle}}{\sqrt a}=1. The reference-band law (\omega_d^\star/\omega_e)^2=g_{dd}/g_{66} alone does not identify the full interacting frequency generator with \sqrt{G/g_{66}}. Consequently the earlier universal prohibition on a term linear in a dimensionless coupling was too strong. The particular matrix prescriptions were checked; a different operator map was not disproved. These corrections are already recorded in the hadronic ledger, Section 73. 4. Projection of a signal is not replacement of its generator For a time-independent linear map P and the same clock, P\bigl(u e^{-i\omega t}\bigr)=(Pu)e^{-i\omega t}. A nonzero projected line retains its frequency. A zero projection removes the line. This is different from physically imposing a new closed dynamics generated by PHP on a subspace that does not reduce H. The exact diagnostic used u=\begin{pmatrix}1/\sqrt6\\\sqrt{5/6}\end{pmatrix}, \qquad H=64uu^\dagger, \qquad P=\operatorname{diag}(1,0). The compressed matrix has its observed entry 32/3, but the exact projected resolvent is P(z-H)^{-1}P =\left[\frac{1}{6(z-64)}+\frac{5}{6z}\right]P. The factor 1/6 is the residue at the unchanged frequency 64. The corresponding exact reduced generator is H_{\rm eff}(z)=\frac{32z}{3z-160}. This resolves the earlier color-projection error: the ordered rank-one contact gives 64/6 under compression, but that is not a universal frequency penalty. If color and orbital factors separate as I_{\rm color}\otimes A_{\rm mode}, singlet restriction leaves the allowed orbital eigenfrequencies unchanged. Likewise, annihilation of an identical color-vector product does not exclude a shared orbital mode with a separate antisymmetric color state. These results do not establish that 64 is a physical baryon eigenvalue. See ledger Section 74. 5. A genuine color coefficient, with its sign retained With fundamental generators normalized by \operatorname{tr}(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}/2, the directly constructed pair operator is C_{ij}=\sum_aT_i^aT_j^a =\frac12\left(X_{ij}-\frac13I\right). On the normalized determinant singlet \epsilon\in\Lambda^3\mathbb C^3, X_{ij}\epsilon=-\epsilon. Hence C_{ij}\epsilon=-\frac23\epsilon, \qquad \sum_{i<j}C_{ij}\epsilon=-2\epsilon. All eight generators, their trace normalization, and all three pair operators were checked explicitly. For a derived interaction of the form \sum_{i<j}C_{ij}\otimes K_{ij}(z), the singlet restriction is -(2/3)\sum_{i<j}K_{ij}(z). It becomes -2K(z) only when the remaining pair operators actually coincide. This is not a frequency prediction. The radial, spin, and normalization content of K_{ij} is still required. A numerical equality with the 2/3 in 28/9=(2/3)(g_{33}/g_{44}) does not identify the two constructions. The adopted sector couplings must not silently be equated with the coefficient of a gauge-current pair interaction. The source generator convention appears in the contact-resonance module, Section 14; the diagnostic is recorded in ledger Section 76. 6. What the earlier numerical searches actually tested These searches used preselected illustrative prescriptions, not a derived composite generator. Their failures therefore do not falsify all V2 hadronic constructions. For the committed quark contact counts D_u=15, D_d=1, D_s=20, raw constituent products give 225 for uud, 15 for udd, and 300 for uds. This shows why that unqualified product prescription is unsuitable as a common nucleon bulk contribution; it does not establish how physical composite frequencies combine. A separate carrier-size scan gave: Candidate carrier Dimension W^{\otimes3}, \dim W=4 64 \operatorname{Sym}^3W 20 \Lambda^3W 4 U^{\otimes3}, \dim U=3 27 \operatorname{Sym}^3U 10 \Lambda^3U 1 W^{\otimes2} 16 \operatorname{Sym}^2W 10 \Lambda^2W 6 The number 64\varpi_3 lay about 2.77 percent below the chosen approximately 309.5 MeV per-constituent residual when the conditional sector scale was used. That proximity does not choose a baryon carrier. Its previous suppression-based exclusion was withdrawn, not replaced by a derivation. Another scan tried S(n,6)/S(13,6) for 35\le n\le47. The values bracketing the selected residual ratio near 605.676 were approximately 578.408 at n=42 and 661.038 at n=43. No operator identification justified borrowing the electron-sector scale for a composite. Scalar S^5 harmonic degeneracies were also scanned; their initial values are 1,6,20,50,105,196. Degeneracy is not automatically a frequency. These are records of unsuccessful exploratory identifications, not universal spectral exclusions or statistical null tests. The approximately 309--310 MeV quantity itself was a residual allocated per constituent after subtracting chosen quark contributions. It is not, absent an additional decomposition theorem, a separately measured pole that a correct operator must contain. The primary target is the whole baryon rest frequency. 7. The constructive spectral target Three positions in a common observed three-space give six relative Jacobi coordinates after center-of-mass removal. A fixed Euclidean hyperradius has an S^5 angular surface. This is useful effective three-body kinematics, not proof that the baryon is the depth-six electron sector or the depth-five neutrino sector. Native higher-depth coordinates, spinor bundles, and eliminated channels must be accounted for. Ledger Section 75 records the corrected distinction. For a specified stationary generator \mathsf H in electron-frequency units and an orthogonal model-space projector P_B, let Q_B=I-P_B. Exact reduction gives \mathsf H_{\rm eff}(z)=P_B\mathsf HP_B+ P_B\mathsf HQ_B(z-Q_B\mathsf HQ_B)^{-1}Q_B\mathsf HP_B, and seeks \ker\left[z_BI_{P_B}-\mathsf H_{\rm eff}(z_B)\right]\ne\{0\}. The complementary inverse has a specified domain; at its excluded values the original problem is checked. This is an exact block identity for a given generator, not a derivation of the missing blocks. A covariant Dirac operator must first be related to a stationary time generator. An off-diagonal map P_3D_\infty P_4 has no standalone ordinary frequency spectrum without further structure. Handoff: finish the action-to-projected-reference-response identification in the rank-one note before declaring the common-anchor law closed. Then derive the composite blocks and their induced spectral terms. Do not replace this task with amplitude fitting, a carrier-dimension search, or a declaration that every remaining factor is already a theorem. 8. Scope of verification The packaged regression checks reproduce finite algebra, the illustrative resolvent, color contractions, moving-projector identities, smooth-symbol spectra, and the source-cancellation/count-normalization distinction. They are not Monte Carlo significance tests, a full variational derivation, or a proof of empirical agreement. Source audits here are limited to the inspected passages and bounded searches returned during this session. An unsuccessful search for a formula is not proof of absence from every possible V2 companion. No prior claimed extensive null tests have been re-executed in this session. 9. title: Independent correctness audit
summary: Independent recurrence refinement exposes false numerical acceptance, while scope corrections separate valid conditional geometry and conservation tests from physical identification.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Summary: Independent recurrence refinement exposes false numerical acceptance, while scope corrections separate valid conditional geometry and conservation tests from physical identification. Verdict and scope Not everything was correct. There are valid conditional constructions and reproducible diagnostics, but the periodic-continuation acceptance and several physical-inference statements exceeded their evidence. This audit corrects those statements rather than counting earlier successful script exits as proof of the full theory. The audit inspected the core module statements and recent orbit, response, geometry, mass-operator, and conservation calculations. The initial sweep ran 57 existing diagnostic scripts, excluding the two expensive continuation searches, and all exited successfully. Independent checks then reintegrated saved continuation candidates and found the failure below. The mass-spectrum program also reproduces its stated fixed-index depth sequence. These are finite checks, not an end-to-end independent proof of every theorem in the historical archive. Earlier research notes not individually rederived remain historical records with their existing correction links. After the corrections, a fresh suite run completed 58 diagnostic scripts, including the new independent audit, with no failing exit status. The saved suite report contains every script's output, exit status, timing, interpreter version, and the two explicit continuation-search exclusions. The independent audit performed 84 checks and classified all three archived candidates as not accepted. The mass-spectrum program, knowledge-base validator (163 notes), Python syntax checks, Markdown display checks, and the visualization's two inline JavaScript blocks also passed their respective checks. Source checks are not browser rendering or mathematical proof. Corrections with explicit witnesses Periodic continuation was accepted at inadequate integration accuracy. The three archived candidates at h=0.0064,0.0096,0.0128 have refined closure errors 2.41423,7.43896,5.31450 times 10^{-6}, respectively, rather than the reported sub-10^{-6} values. Their Casimirs are correct. The optimizer's residual was not a reliable independent error estimate. See Cylindrical petal continuation for pinned states, numerical settings, and the withdrawn acceptance claim. The fully cylindrical centre had a removable implementation singularity. At h=1, the coefficient of the old Coulomb potential vanishes, but the implementation still evaluated that potential at q=0. The corrected code omits the discarded term and returns V(0)=-3/(2a) and zero central force. This fixes an endpoint evaluation; it does not remove the actual Coulomb singularity when h<1. Projection does not establish a smeared physical electron. The delta-distribution calculation and experimental distinction are in Electron detection and shape. An additional normalization mistake is corrected in Bound within, free without: a uniform probability density normalized in a fibre box of volume V gives an overlap proportional to 1/V, not an automatically volume-independent coupling. A cylindrical field and a normalized uniform wavefunction are different objects; the action must specify which is intended. A frozen-route ligand minimum is not full molecular stability. The positive ligand Hessians are meaningful for the specified frozen route, fixed centre, and fixed planes. The regular tetrahedral snapshot has nonzero transverse force in that energy and relaxes to a disphenoid. At nuclear radius 0.6, overlapping profiles are still assigned point-centre repulsion, so those entries are hybrid-model controls. See Cylindrical molecular shape stability. Configurable electron mass had inconsistent factors. The completed kinetic energy is |p-m_e\lambda Cs|^2/(2m_e). The reciprocal executable previously used the unit-mass factors even when m_e changed. Corrected velocity, force, and source equations now pass independent Hamiltonian-derivative and conservation checks at m_e=0.7,1,2.3, including nonaligned nuclear planes. The original unit-mass trajectory is unchanged. See Reciprocal cylindrical molecule. A classical angular source is not automatically the CP3 electron. The continued orbit occupies an invariant four-coordinate subspace of the six-coordinate model. Random-state checks verify the exact embedding of its h=0 field, including zero inactive derivatives, to roundoff. It therefore is not an independent dimension witness. This does not reassign the electron: depth six remains the working mass-formula input. Also, a generic skew C need not obey C^2=-c^2I_6, whereas an orthogonal complex structure representing CP3 does. A classical coadjoint source, a CP3 spatial point, and a spinor field are not identified merely because their symmetry groups are related. See Sector geometry premise audit. Several module summaries omitted necessary premises. Base-coordinate locality does not force a rank-one contact operator: band-compressed identity remains identity, whereas a specified point evaluation can be rank one. The occupied-ray and normalization assumptions are now explicit in the self-contact module. See Contact-kernel audit. A generation-blind charged-current vertex is identity in a common basis, but its mass-basis matrix is U_{u,L}^\dagger U_{d,L}; obtaining identity there additionally requires aligned left mass bases. The CKM module now says so. The coherent CPd submanifold is also distinguished from the full projectivization of the cumulative mode bundle. Energy preference and representation realization were overstated. A positive lock-energy coefficient is not dynamical capture: for H=V(s), \dot s=\{s,V(s)\}=0. A small observer-space motional magnetic estimate does not prove that additional curvature supplies the missing lock. Constructing a group action with the desired generator does not derive its physical electromagnetic current. The visualization prose now makes these distinctions without changing its petal rendering. The photon module also states that spatial polarization and normal propagation are premises of its orthogonality theorem, not consequences of dimensional counting alone. What survives and what comes next The exact representation algebra, specified analytic orbit constructions, fixed-source chart, and checked conservative equations remain useful. They are positive mathematical results for defined models. They are not a completed derivation of the physical electron, chemistry, or a unique CP3 geometry. Known unstable and rejected branches must remain in the record. The immediate numerical task is accurate correction and independent closure testing of the fixed-Casimir cylindrical candidates. After that come coupled moving-nucleus recurrence and full perturbation stability. In parallel, the physical identification requires a common action and measurement law tying together the spatial electron, source variables, interaction, and detections. Neither chain can substitute for the other. Reproduction From the repository root (use a fresh report filename for a new run): OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -B experiments/independent_audit_checks.py OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -B experiments/reciprocal_cylindrical_molecule_checks.py OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -B experiments/run_checks.py --skip-continuation --jobs 3 --report experiments/results/audit-2026-09-07/reproduction-suite.json python3 -B experiments/idwt-v2.py python3 -B scripts/validate-kb.py The independent script consumes archived states without re-fitting them and regenerates its report. Its successful diagnostic checks and the candidates' computed acceptance fields are separate: passing the audit does not mean the orbit candidates passed. Integration-failure negative controls reject failed, partial, and nonfinite trajectories. Full long-run continuation has not been rerun as part of this independent saved-state test.

title: Sector geometry premise audit
summary: The sphere and projective sector assignments occur in V1 and remain conditional candidates in V2; spatial depth, topology, phase rules, and interaction dynamics require separate justification.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Summary: The sphere and projective sector assignments occur in V1 and remain conditional candidates in V2; spatial depth, topology, phase rules, and interaction dynamics require separate justification. Fixed physical meaning All sectors are nested submanifolds of the one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. This is a fixed IDWT premise. Every sector direction is macroscopic and spatial. In particular, CP3 denotes the electron's six-dimensional physical submanifold, not an internal state space. Three are shared with us, but that makes none of the six different in kind. Similarly, the electron's six dimensions are six of the tau's ten; the electron is lower-dimensional, or “flat,” relative to the tau. Neither comparison gives the containing particle an inherent physical split. The three-dimensional nuclear sector is the proposed basis of ordinary matter's three-dimensional experience. A particular observer-adapted frame calculation does not establish that general claim. The earlier attribution of three-dimensional experience to nuclear 3+3 locking is withdrawn. An incompatible coordinate construction, candidate topology, or effective model must be corrected to respect this premise. It cannot be rescued by reinterpreting a sector as an independent internal space or by abandoning nesting. The audit below distinguishes the intended physical meaning from what the written mathematics actually establishes. Nesting is a geometric requirement The named candidate list in the polarization module does not establish its required smooth inclusions. There is a concrete obstruction in that list. Suppose an embedding of CP2 into S5 existed. Both are oriented, so its real normal line would be trivial. Restricting the sphere tangent bundle would give i^*TS^5=T\mathbb{CP}^2\oplus\mathbf1. The sphere tangent bundle is stably trivial, hence its second Stiefel–Whitney class vanishes. The Whitney sum formula would then require the same for the CP2 tangent bundle. But the projective-space calculation gives w_2(T\mathbb{CP}^2)=c_1(T\mathbb{CP}^2)\bmod2=3H\bmod2\ne0. Here H is the hyperplane class. This contradiction rules out that smooth nesting of the proposed CP2 and S5 assignments. The characteristic-class tools are given in Ralph Cohen, The Topology of Fiber Bundles, chapter 3. The conclusion here is an application of those tools to the candidate list. Therefore that list needs a geometry correction; the requirement that all sectors are nested remains fixed. This audit does not choose a replacement topology or a different electron depth. The Hopf map from S5 onto CP2 is a quotient and does not supply the missing inclusion. More generally, a nested inclusion does not automatically provide a global product, retraction, or marginalization map. Contact calculations using local tangent–normal coordinates retain that conditional domain until a compatible global construction is supplied. Compact topology also supplies no metric length by itself and gives no reason to call a spatial direction microscopic. Mathematical descriptions must retain their physical meaning Existing construction What it establishes Requirement for the intended spatial theory Tangential compression of the master Dirac operator A d-direction symbol under the stated embedding and Clifford-compatibility assumptions The embedding is of a nested physical submanifold of the same infinite manifold. Homogeneous CP3 coordinate and its four-component lift A representation of points of the proposed six-dimensional spatial submanifold The coordinate lift is not automatically the Dirac field value at that point. Spinor and oscillator-mode bundles Representations of fields and modes on a spatial submanifold Their ranks do not add physical dimensions or independently postulated internal sectors. Chiral or bivector response minimum with CP3 shape A CP3 family in the chosen effective variables A family of field polarizations alone does not derive the physical spatial submanifold; its relation to spatial position and the master field must be supplied. Selected coefficient orbit and displayed petals A trajectory and readout in a chosen reduced model The dynamics must describe actual motion on physical CP3 and the response of nuclear-constrained observers. Observer-adapted 3+3 frame-lock energy A conditional energy and its extrema for a chosen grouping of equivalent spatial directions No inherent electron split follows. Any physical role of the assumed frame constraint needs a derivation; its energy minimum does not derive three-dimensional experience. Product of two particle-position spaces Records two positions on the same physical submanifold Its parameter count is not a new set of physical dimensions. The existing bundle obstructions, conditional response calculations, and stability limitations still apply. The correction is to their interpretation and claim boundaries; adding a spatial label cannot supply missing dynamics. Provenance found, physical derivation not established The user cautioned that the depth geometries may be incorrect and may have been copied from a mathematically underjustified V1. The local V1 forces document, section 0.8b, already lists CP1, S3, CP2, S5, CP3, and CP5 at depths 2,3,4,5,6,10. This establishes their presence in V1, not a complete edit-by-edit copying history and not the correctness of the accompanying force claims. Section 12 of the V2 polarization module gives an inverse reconstruction conditional on: a smallest complex amplitude carrier; fixed normalization; a chosen physical or redundant status of common phase; transitive unitary action; and an already prescribed real spatial dimension. Within that ansatz, retaining phase gives S(2r−1), and quotienting it gives CP(r−1). The dimension arithmetic is valid. It does not show that a particle's actual configuration is this amplitude space, that its norm is constrained in this way, or that its common phase has the assumed physical status. The written reconstruction does not derive these premises from the master interaction or establish that alternative geometries are impossible. Three questions must remain separate Question What would support it What does not settle it Spatial depth d Independent kinetic derivative directions in a derived sector operator Number of display controls or complex coefficients Geometry of Q_d A derived metric, constraints, identifications, and global structure Real dimension alone or a convenient homogeneous-space construction Interaction and observed orbit Derived source, dynamics, physical projection/current and perturbation response A chosen generator with a trajectory-shaped readout The particle-depth module already identifies depth with the number of local spatial derivative directions. Even if that count were established, it would not select a unique global topology or metric. Its projected-symbol theorem itself requires a sector embedding, projector, and compatibility assumptions; writing a d-direction operator after assuming the sector is not a measurement or a derivation selecting d. The local symmetric-mode count is likewise conditional on independent quadratic directions and the specified mode construction. It is not a unique signature of CP3, S5, or another global manifold. Consequences for the current orbit investigation CP3 precession and the finite response model are valid conditional constructions on a chosen six-real-dimensional geometry. They do not establish that geometry for the electron. The earlier SO(4)/U(2) comparison varied carrier dimension, not V2's proposed particle-base dimension. Its minimum-carrier theorem cannot establish a minimum-six particle depth. The exact three-amplitude restriction on candidate CP2 and S5 reproduces the prepared ideal demo with the restricted original readout. It is a counterexample to uniqueness inside these candidate constructions, not evidence that CP2 or S5 is the correct lower-depth geometry. A response-control rank calculated in the assumed CP3 model is not yet an empirical dimension witness. title: Cross-sector moment kernel
summary: The unaveraged quadratic kernel retains the tensor data needed to investigate orientation dependence.
text: Physical premise (IDWT): There is one infinite-dimensional physical manifold. All sectors form one nested chain of submanifolds within it. Particle depth counts ordinary, literal macroscopic spatial dimensions. “Observed” and “unobserved” describe an observer's access to those dimensions, not different kinds of physical dimension. See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Source and scope Starting point: Gravity §3.10.1–2 and Appendix B §20a. The explicit rectangular identification and tensor generalization below are an adaptation derived during the import review, not a theorem quoted from V1. Retain the second moments Let x in R^d, y in R^e, and let B:R^e -> R^d be a specified identification. For unit-normalized densities define K_B(x,y)=g(x^{\mathsf T}By)^2,\qquad M_x=\int xx^{\mathsf T}\rho_x(x)\,dx,\quad M_y=\int yy^{\mathsf T}\rho_y(y)\,dy. Then, exactly, V_x(x)=g x^{\mathsf T}B M_y B^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad U_{xy}=g\operatorname{tr}(M_x B M_y B^{\mathsf T}). For fixed M_y and B, the coordinate Hessian of V_x is 2g B M_y B^T. This is not automatically the full coupled-field Hessian: the background moments can fluctuate too. For equal dimensions and B=I, write M_x=aI+Q_x and M_y=bI+Q_y, with traceless Q_x,Q_y. Then U_{xy}=g\left[dab+\operatorname{tr}(Q_xQ_y)\right]. The historical isotropic reduction sets both Q tensors to zero. Retaining them gives an explicit orientation-sensitive term. Its sign and eigenvalue structure must determine the preferred orientation; alignment is not automatic. Even a preferred quadrupole-axis alignment need not determine a unique signed frame or the electron's complex-structure polarization. Symmetry and missing inputs Under independent orthogonal frame changes x->R x and y->S y, covariance requires B->R B S^T. Holding B fixed preserves only compatible transformations. An unspecified cross-sector dot product is therefore not invariant under arbitrary independent rotations. For complex coordinates, specify a Hermitian kernel such as |x-dagger B y|^2 and its representation separately. Rank-one sector coefficients g_de=v_d v_e do not force the coordinate kernel or its projected matrix elements to be rank one. Promising next calculation: derive B and background moments from the V2 field, retain their fluctuations, and project onto the actual polarization states. Do not identify this scalar coordinate Hessian with a spin-dependent lock operator without that projection and the corresponding kinetic form. Related Self-consistent moment lock test — follow-up: the positive scalar ground-state model does not generate a mixed covariance spontaneously, but its response to a supplied source is calculable. Self-consistent functional — the isotropic background to generalize. Import boundaries — explains why older uniqueness and closure claims are not imported.

title: Import boundaries
summary: Negative results and faulty closure claims constrain what may safely be transferred from V1.

See spatial meaning and mathematical scope. Preserve these useful restrictions Chemistry §6.1–6.4 contains a useful conditional factorization result. If H=H_obs tensor I + I tensor H_hidden, the unobserved states are orthonormal, and O=O_obs tensor I, then \langle\psi\otimes\chi_a|O|\psi'\otimes\chi_b\rangle =\langle\psi|O_{\rm obs}|\psi'\rangle\delta_{ab}. A purely unobserved contribution gives a common shift when all compared states share the same unobserved state and particle content. Under these assumptions it cannot generate orbital-dependent splittings. A mixed interaction is the place to investigate deviations. Do not import the universal chemistry claim or numerical contact bound without separately establishing their premises, range, units, amplitude, and relevant observables. Appendix B §20a and §50 record that isotropic density overlaps retain the monopole, with the mean traceless quadrupole vanishing. This is a restriction on that reduction, not on all anisotropic states, virtual transitions, or spinor operators. The imported notes do not rely on §50's separate fourth-moment formulas. Appendix D §49b records the rejection of an old rho-meson comb-root claim: a target-bracketed root among many roots does not select a physical resonance. Preserve this warning rather than the contradictory positive claim still present in Mass §10. Do not copy these claims as established mathematics Kernel uniqueness: Spectral T2 treats a cross-sector dot square as invariant under independent rotations. It is not, with a fixed identification. The identification and its symmetry must be specified; coefficient rank one also remains a separate condition. Colour connection: Forces §3a defines psi_color as a column in C^3. Then i psi_color-dagger d psi_color is a scalar, not a matrix in su(3). It does not solve the V2 global gauge-bundle problem. For two exclusive channels whose actual rate ratio is r, normalizing their sum instead gives r/(1+r). A distinct incident-flux or dynamical argument is needed to justify r itself. The full charged-current calculation still requires kinetic metrics and mass bases; a chosen unitary completion is not that calculation. CP closure: CP Completion and Appendix E §47 contain candidate determinant-phase and beat-link arguments. A determinant phase alone does not establish rephasing-invariant CP violation.
